0ab50bc17861492a:01.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge2$, $H>0$ and $0<U<H$. Put $B=H+1$ and $r(z)=(H-z)/B$. On $-1\le z\le U$, $|x|\le r(z)$, use the measure of density $f(x,z)=r(z)^{d-2}/2$ with respect to $dx\,dz$. Set $a=r(U)$, $T=U/a$, $t=a^d=[H/(B+T)]^d$, $V_0=B/d$, and $V=(1-t)V_0$. The associated cone has the same density formula on $-1\le z\le H$, $|x|\le r(z)$, and mass $V_0$.

For a finite slope $s\ge0$, let $P(s)$ be the mass of $z+sx\ge0$. Let $C(s)$ and $M(s)$ be the integrals of $f$ and $zf$, respectively, over the section $z+sx=0$ inside the support, against $d\mathcal H^1/\sqrt{1+s^2}$. A law's record is the average of $(P,C,M)$, and a law is centered if its averaged $M$ is zero.

Given any probability law on finite slopes $s\ge0$, let $\phi$ be the mixture of the uniform probabilities on $[-s,s]$, with the layer at $s=0$ interpreted as $\delta_0$. Put $v=\phi((-\infty,1])$, $w=\phi([-T,\infty))$, $C_0=(H/B)^{d-1}$, $p_0=(H/B)^d$, and $a_0=1/B$. For $0<q<1$ put $e(q)=\int_{[-T,1]}(1-qb)^{-d}\,d\phi(b)$. The averaged frustum records satisfy

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{P}{V_0}&=p_0e(a_0)+1-v-tw,\\
\frac{C}{C_0}&=e(a_0),\\
\frac{M}{C_0}&=-\frac HB\int_{[-T,1]} b(1-b/B)^{-d-1}\,d\phi(b).
\end{aligned}
$$

The energy $e$ is differentiable and convex on $(0,1)$. Centering is equivalent to $e'(a_0)=0$, or equivalently to $a_0$ minimizing $e$ on $(0,1)$.

If $T\ge1$ and the slope law is supported on $[0,T]$, the corresponding full-cone energy at $a_0$ is the same integral and satisfies $e(a_0)\ge (2v-1)+(t/p_0)(1-v)$. This last bound applies in particular to centered cone laws.

Write $R_f(s)=(P_f(s),C_f(s),M_f(s))$ for the frustum record and $R_c(s)$ for the cone record. Every finite slope has positive frustum and cone coarea. The frustum records have a limit $R_f(\infty)=(V/2,0,0)$, which defines the record at the optional endpoint $\infty$.

If $T\le1$, then $M_f(s)<0$ for every finite $s>0$. Each centered law on $[0,\infty]$ is supported on $\{0,\infty\}$ and its averages obey $P-cC=V/2$ with the same $c=(P_f(0)-V/2)/C_f(0)$ for all such laws.

If $T\ge1$, the bounded cone and frustum records and the finite frustum tail satisfy

$$
\begin{aligned}
R_f(s)&=R_c(s)-(tV_0,0,0) &&(0\le s\le T),\\
R_f(s)&=\frac Ts R_f(T)+\left(1-\frac Ts\right)R_f(\infty) &&(T\le s<\infty).
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus every probability law on $[0,\infty]$ has a representative supported on $[0,T]\cup\{\infty\}$ with the same frustum records. If the original law is centered and the representative has positive finite mass, its conditional finite law is centered for the cone as well as for the frustum.

For $T\ge1$, let $\mu,\nu$ be separately centered probability laws on cone slopes $[0,T]$. Use $P_\mu^c,P_\nu^c,C_\mu,C_\nu$ for their averaged cone cap and coarea records. If $P_\mu^f,P_\nu^f$ denote the corresponding frustum cap records, the coareas are the same, and

$$
\begin{aligned}
\beta_c&=\frac{C_\nu P_\mu^c+C_\mu(V_0-P_\nu^c)}{V_0(C_\mu+C_\nu)},&
\omega&=\frac{C_\nu}{C_\mu+C_\nu},\\
\beta_f&=\frac{C_\nu P_\mu^f+C_\mu(V-P_\nu^f)}{V(C_\mu+C_\nu)}

\end{aligned}
$$

For arbitrary separately centered frustum laws, use their record-preserving representatives on $[0,T]\cup\{\infty\}$ and write $\lambda_\mu,\lambda_\nu$ for their finite masses. If both are positive, let $\beta_f$ in the next formula be the bounded frustum ratio of their conditional finite laws, and $C_\mu,C_\nu$ their conditional finite coareas. $$
\frac12+\frac{\lambda_\mu\lambda_\nu(C_\mu+C_\nu)}
{\lambda_\mu C_\mu+\lambda_\nu C_\nu}\left(\beta_f-\frac12\right).
$$

If exactly one law has zero coarea, the ratio is $1/2$. If both have zero coarea, the literal quotient has zero denominator, and its continuous extension has value $1/2$. Each cap record in that case is $V/2$. For $T\le1$ the positive-denominator ratio for any separately centered pair is $1/2$, with the same extension at zero total coarea.

0dca404d0a46dbff:02.statement:
For a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$, let $\mu_K$ be the measure obtained by summing $d$-dimensional volume on its integer fibers. Let $B$ be the standard $4$-simplex, of volume $V$, with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_4$, where $\lambda_1=x_1$. Put
$$
\alpha=\frac{17}{100},\qquad \beta=\frac{199999}{1000000},\qquad L=B\cap\{\alpha\le\lambda_1\le\beta\},\qquad
m=\frac{|L|}{V}=\left(\frac{83}{100}\right)^4-\left(\frac{800001}{1000000}\right)^4.
$$
Set $Q=m^{-1/4}$, $r=2-Q$, $A=rL$, $C_+=QL$, and $a=(2m^{1/4}-1)^4$. Let $K$ be the convex hull of the lifts of $A,B,C_+$ at levels $-1,0,1$, respectively. Its integer fibers are precisely $A,B,C_+$ with masses $aV,V,V$ and $0<a<10^{-8}$.

Define $v$ by $\lambda_1(v)=37/200$ and $\lambda_i(v)=163/800$ for $i\ne1$, and put $h=a^{1/4}$, $C'=2v-A$, and $B_h=B\cap\{\lambda_1\le1-h\}$. The convex hull $K'$ of the lifts of $A,B_h,C'$ at levels $-1,0,1$ is a full-dimensional subbody of $K$ with these exact integer fibers. Its mixed mass is $(1+a)V>(2+a)V/2$ and its mixed centroid is $(0,c)$, where
$$
\lambda_1(c)=\frac15-4e,\qquad \lambda_i(c)=\frac15+e\ (i\ne1),\qquad
e=\frac{(83/400-h/5)a}{1+a},\qquad \frac a5\le e\le\frac{83a}{400}.
$$

Write $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Every closed ambient halfspace containing $(0,c)$ has $\mu_{K'}$-mass at least $\Gamma_4(1+a)V$. The normalized depth of $(0,c)$ in $K'$ is at least $\Gamma_4$, and its normalized depth in $K$ is at least $\Gamma_4(1+a)/(2+a)>\Gamma_4/2$.

0e1bf4bac5d35265:05.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be nonempty and finite, with $n\ge0$ and $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$. Let $d\ge1$ and let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex bodies with nonempty interior for $z\in P$. Put $S=\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$ and $C=\operatorname{conv}S$, and assume $C\cap(\{z\}\times\mathbb R^d)=\{z\}\times K_z$ for each $z\in P$. All hulls and affine coefficients are relative to $\operatorname{aff}(P)\times\mathbb R^d$. Write $dm=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes dX|_{K_z}$ and $M=m(S)$. Let $L$ be positive, continuous, and concave on $C$, with $\int_S\log L\,dm/M=0$. Fix $k\ge1$ marks $Y_i=(p_i,y_i)$ with $p_i\in P$ and $y_i\in\operatorname{int}K_{p_i}$, and write $l_i=L(Y_i)$ and $l=(l_i)_{i=1}^k$.

Assume there is at least one contact certificate. This means weights $\sigma_i\ge0$ with $\sum_i\sigma_i=1$ and, for each $\sigma_i>0$, a probability measure $\rho_i$ on $S$ with
$$
\int_S w\,d\rho_i=Y_i,\qquad
\int_S L\,d\rho_i=l_i,\qquad
\sum_{i:\,\sigma_i>0}\frac{\sigma_i}{l_i}\rho_i=\frac{dm}{ML}.
\tag{1}
$$
Let $\mathcal W$ be the set of all weight vectors of such certificates. For $b\in(0,\infty)^k$, let $H_C(b)$ be the supremum of $M^{-1}\int_S\log U\,dm$ over positive continuous concave functions $U$ on $C$ with $U(Y_i)\le b_i$ for all $i$.

For another compatible family of compact convex bodies $K'_z$ over the same $P$, write $S'$, $C'$, and $dm'$ for the corresponding sampled set, hull, and measure. Retain the same marks and define $H_{C'}(b)$ by the same supremum with domain $C'$ and integral over $S'$ against $dm'/M$, with the fixed old denominator $M$.

There is a fixed function $\widetilde L$, a minimum of at most $k$ affine functions on the relative ambient space, positive on a neighborhood of $C$ and equal to $L$ on $S$. For all families sufficiently close to the old family in maximum fiber Hausdorff distance and all $b$ sufficiently close to $l$, the marks stay interior to their own fibers and $H_{C'}(b)$ is finite and attained. It has a representative that is the minimum of at most $k$ affine functions, whose coefficients are uniformly bounded and whose minimum has a uniform positive floor on $C'$, on $C$, and on a fixed neighborhood of $C$. The maximizing sampled restriction is unique. As $(K'_z,b)\to(K_z,l)$, the optimal value tends to zero, the maximizing restriction converges uniformly on $S'$ to $\widetilde L|_{S'}$, and the bounded finite-plane representatives in the proof converge uniformly to $L$ on $S$.

Let $t\downarrow0$ and let $K_z(t)$ be such compatible bodies with $\max_z d_H(K_z(t),K_z)=O(t)$, using subscript $t$ for the moving objects. For arbitrary $b(t)\to l$ in the positive orthant,
$$
H_t(b(t))
=H_C(b(t))+
\frac{1}{M}\left(\int_{S_t}\log\widetilde L\,dm_t-\int_S\log L\,dm\right)+o(t).
\tag{6}
$$
Suppose in addition that for each $z$ and some fixed $o_z\in\operatorname{int}K_z$, the endpoint on the ray through each $X\in\partial K_z$ changes to $o_z+(1-s_{z,t}(X))(X-o_z)$. Assume $|s_{z,t}|\le Ct$ uniformly and
$s_{z,t}(X)/t\to v_z(X)/(n_z(X)\cdot(X-o_z))$ for surface-almost every $X$, where $n_z$ is the outward unit normal and $v_z$ is a bounded measurable signed inward speed. Use counting measure on the two endpoints for $d=1$. For $b_i(t)=l_i+th_i+o(t)$, with arbitrary $h\in\mathbb R^k$,
$$
H_t(b(t))
=t\left[-\frac1M\sum_{z\in P}\int_{\partial K_z}\log L(z,X)v_z(X)\,dS(X)
+\min_{\sigma\in\mathcal W}\sum_i\frac{\sigma_i h_i}{l_i}\right]+o(t).
\tag{7}
$$
The minimum is attained. Using the current total volume $M_t=m_t(S_t)$ as the denominator gives the same first-order coefficient.

0e1bf4bac5d35265:07.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be nonempty and finite, with $n\ge0$ and $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$. Let $d\ge1$ and let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex bodies with nonempty interior for $z\in P$. Put $S=\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$ and $C=\operatorname{conv}S$, and assume $C\cap(\{z\}\times\mathbb R^d)=\{z\}\times K_z$ for each $z\in P$. All hulls and affine coefficients are relative to $\operatorname{aff}(P)\times\mathbb R^d$. Write $dm=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes dX|_{K_z}$ and $M=m(S)$. Let $L$ be positive, continuous, and concave on $C$, with $\int_S\log L\,dm/M=0$. Fix $k\ge1$ marks $Y_i=(p_i,y_i)$ with $p_i\in P$ and $y_i\in\operatorname{int}K_{p_i}$, and write $l_i=L(Y_i)$ and $l=(l_i)_{i=1}^k$.

Assume there is at least one contact certificate. This means weights $\sigma_i\ge0$ with $\sum_i\sigma_i=1$ and, for each $\sigma_i>0$, a probability measure $\rho_i$ on $S$ with
$$
\int_S w\,d\rho_i=Y_i,\qquad
\int_S L\,d\rho_i=l_i,\qquad
\sum_{i:\,\sigma_i>0}\frac{\sigma_i}{l_i}\rho_i=\frac{dm}{ML}.
\tag{1}
$$
Let $\mathcal W$ be the set of all weight vectors of such certificates. For $b\in(0,\infty)^k$, let $H_C(b)$ be the supremum of $M^{-1}\int_S\log U\,dm$ over positive continuous concave functions $U$ on $C$ with $U(Y_i)\le b_i$ for all $i$.

For every such $U$ and every $\sigma\in\mathcal W$ one has
$$
\frac1M\int_S\log(U/L)\,dm
\le\sum_{i=1}^k \sigma_i\log\frac{U(Y_i)}{l_i}.
\tag{2}
$$
This also holds for continuous nonnegative concave $U$ on $C$ that are positive in the interior of every sampled fiber and have integrable sampled $\log U$. If $U(Y_i)\le l_i$ for all $i$ and the left-hand side is zero, then $U=L$ on every closed sampled fiber.

The function $H_C$ is finite, concave, and coordinatewise nondecreasing on the positive orthant, with $H_C(cb)=H_C(b)+\log c$ for $c>0$. One has $H_C(l)=0$, attained by $L$, and
$$
\partial^+H_C(l)=\left\{\left(\frac{\sigma_i}{l_i}\right)_{i=1}^k:\ \sigma\in\mathcal W\right\},
\tag{3}
$$
where $\partial^+$ consists of the supergradients for the concave function. In particular $\mathcal W$ is compact and convex, and for every $h\in\mathbb R^k$ and $t\downarrow0$,
$$
H_C(l+th+o(t))=t\min_{\sigma\in\mathcal W}\sum_i \frac{\sigma_i h_i}{l_i}+o(t).
\tag{4}
$$

191a0eb2244ea4a9:03.statement:

$$
P(a,b)=\Pr\left(\sum_i a_iE_i\ge\sum_j b_jF_j\right).
$$

If $p\ge2$, $a_i=\max_k a_k$, and $j\ne i$ is another positive index, then replacing $(a_i,a_j)$ by $(a_i+t,a_j-t)$ strictly decreases $P(a,b)$ for every $0<t\le a_j$. At $t=0$ it leaves $P(a,b)$ unchanged. Any tied largest index can be chosen. A zero donor allows only the unchanged transfer.

For all $p,q\ge1$,
$$
P(a,b)\ge\prod_{j=1}^q\left(1+\frac{b_j}{\sum_i a_i}\right)^{-1}
\ge\Gamma_q,\qquad \Gamma_q=\left(\frac{q}{q+1}\right)^q.
$$
Equality in the first bound holds exactly when $p=1$. Equality at $\Gamma_q$ holds exactly when $p=1$ and the $b_j$ are equal. For each fixed positive phase count $p$ and negative phase count $q$, $\Gamma_q$ is the infimum.

191a0eb2244ea4a9:06.statement:
Let $T=\operatorname{conv}(v_0,\ldots,v_d)$ be a $d$-simplex with $d\ge1$ and centroid $g$. Let $h$ be a nonconstant affine function on $\operatorname{aff}(T)$ with $h(g)=0$. Let $p=\#\{i:h(v_i)>0\}$ and $q=\#\{i:h(v_i)<0\}$. Then $p,q\ge1$ and the closed centroid cap $C=T\cap\{h\ge0\}$ satisfies
$$
\frac{|C|_d}{|T|_d}\ge \Gamma_q=\left(\frac{q}{q+1}\right)^q.
$$
Equality holds exactly when $p=1$ and all $q$ strictly negative margins are equal. For each $d$ and $1\le q\le d$ the bound is attained. If $p>1$ is fixed as well with $p+q\le d+1$, the bound is the infimum and is never attained.

For $d\ge2$, a proper closed centroid cap containing at least two vertices has fraction at least $\Gamma_{d-1}>\Gamma_d$. This bound is attained exactly when one vertex has positive margin, one has zero margin, and the remaining $d-1$ have equal negative margins. In dimension one, each proper closed centroid cap is a half-interval of relative length $1/2$ and contains exactly one vertex.

191a0eb2244ea4a9:07.reason: With at least two contained vertices, q≤d−1 and γ_q≥γ_(d−1). The same fact characterizes equality and handles the dimension-one exception.
191a0eb2244ea4a9:07.statement: For d≥2, a proper closed centroid cap containing at least two vertices, with boundary vertices counted, has fraction at least Γ_(d−1)>Γ_d. Equality holds exactly when one vertex lies strictly inside the halfspace, one on the boundary, and the other d−1 vertices have equal negative margins.

191a0eb2244ea4a9:08.reason: Classical Grünbaum and its apex-side equality case are recorded in the opening proof paragraph of 03bc771bddd39a8a. A simplex pyramid has its opposite facet as base. The q=d one-positive margin calculation is also the one-vertex beta specialization at threshold 1/(d+1).
191a0eb2244ea4a9:08.statement: The ordinary centroid floor is Γ_d. In d≥2, its equality orientations are the apex-side caps parallel to their opposite facets. In d=1, both midpoint half-intervals have length fraction Γ_1=1/2.

191a0eb2244ea4a9:09.reason: The exact two-phase Erlang tail gives an increase of 25/1173942 when the two nonlargest positives are merged.
191a0eb2244ea4a9:09.statement:
Let $E_1,E_2,E_3,F_1,F_2$ be independent exponential random variables of mean one. Define $X=(E_1+E_2+18E_3)/20$, $X'=(2E_1+18E_3)/20$, and $Y=(F_1+F_2)/2$. Both positive coefficient totals and the negative coefficient total are one. The two smallest positive coefficients of $X$ are merged in $X'$, and
$$
\Pr(X'\ge Y)-\Pr(X\ge Y)=\frac{25}{1173942}>0.
$$
This refutes the claim that merging any two positive coefficients of a balanced signed-exponential sum can only decrease its nonnegative sign probability.

197c4420ab5b2852:01.reason: A common invertible linear change maps the ellipsoid to a ball and transports the coarea balance. Rotating each horizontal normal and taking its reflected pair preserves section centering and cap mass and gives a menu in one plane, where the exact accepted stationary bound applies.
197c4420ab5b2852:01.statement:
Let $d=m+1\ge2$, let $D\subset\mathbb R^m$ be a centered full-dimensional ellipsoid, and let $r$ be positive and concave on $[a,b]$ with $a<0<b$. Put $K=\{(X,z):a\le z\le b,\ X\in r(z)D\}$. For a finite menu of unit normals $u_i$, let $S_i=\mathcal H^{d-1}(K\cap u_i^\perp)$ and $p_i=|K\cap\{Y:u_i\cdot Y\ge0\}|/|K|$. Suppose each section has centroid $0$, and $\theta_i\ge0$, $\sum_i\theta_i=1$, $\sum_i\theta_i S_i u_i=0$. Then
$$
\sum_i\theta_i p_i\ge c_d,\qquad
c_2=\frac49,\qquad
c_d=\frac1{1+\max\{4/3,\sqrt{2(d-1)/d}\}}\quad(d\ge3).
$$
In particular, $c_d=3/7$ for $3\le d\le9$, $c_d>2/5$ for $d\ge10$, and $c_d\ge(d/(d+1))^d$.

197c4420ab5b2852:02.reason: An even unimodal horizontal marginal is a mixture of uniform interval densities. Scaling each interval to unit radius gives the same planar homothetic profile, with the corresponding change of slope in its fixed-cut records.
197c4420ab5b2852:02.statement:
Let $m\ge1$, let $D\subset\mathbb R^m$ be a centrally symmetric convex body with center $0$, and let $K=\{(X,z):a\le z\le b,\ X\in r(z)D\}$, with $a<0<b$ and $r$ positive and concave. For a fixed horizontal unit vector $e$, write $x=e\cdot X$. There is a probability law $\mu$ on radii $R>0$ under which the projection $e\cdot U$ of uniform $U$ on $D$ is a mixture of the uniform laws on $[-R,R]$. The layer of radius $R$, in coordinates $x=Ry$, has density
$$
f(y,z)=\frac12 r(z)^{m-1}\mathbf1_{\{a\le z\le b,\ |y|\le r(z)\}}
$$
after dividing ordinary volume on $K$ by $|D|$. Its mass is $V=\int_a^b r(z)^m\,dz$. Let $P(s)$ be the cap mass of $z+sy\ge0$ under this density. Let $C(s)$ and $M(s)$ be its section integrals of $f$ and $zf$ over $z+sy=0$, with line measure divided by $\sqrt{1+s^2}$. For any finite $t\in\mathbb R$, the cap mass, raw section coarea, and raw vertical section first moment of $z+tx\ge0$ in $K$, divided by $|D|$, are the $\mu$-averages of $P(tR),C(tR),M(tR)$. Raw section integrals in $K$ use $\mathcal H^m/\sqrt{1+t^2}$. In particular full centering of the actual section implies $\int M(tR)\,d\mu(R)=0$.

The profile is positive and concave and the mass is $V=281/2$. Let $P(s)$ be the mass of $z+sx\ge0$, and let $C(s)$ and $M(s)$ be the integrals of $f$ and $zf$ on $z+sx=0$ against $d\mathcal H^1/\sqrt{1+s^2}$. No real $c,\lambda$ satisfy
$$
\frac49 V\le P(s)-cC(s)-\lambda M(s)\le\frac59 V
\qquad\text{for all }s\ge0.
$$
An explicit witness uses slopes $0,1/10,3/5$, with the middle cap reversed, and total weights $18245,16128,5658$ divided by $40031$. Splitting each oblique type equally under $x\mapsto-x$ gives raw coarea vector balance and signed vertical section first-moment balance, with weighted mass fraction $4942884/11248711<4/9$.

1a4f9cc73e4a014c:02.reason: The two endpoint incidences give the exact extremal sector triangle. The proof checks equality, attainment and the unbounded parameter regime.
1a4f9cc73e4a014c:02.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a convex body with $0$ in its interior. Suppose the endpoints of the $K$ chords on the negative $y$-axis and on the positive-$x$ ray of $x+y=0$ are $(0,-\beta)$ and $(\rho,-\rho)$, with $\beta,\rho>0$. In the coordinates $u=-y$, $v=x+y$, the sector $K\cap\{y<0<x+y\}$ lies in
$$
u>0,\qquad v>0,\qquad \beta u+(\beta-\rho)v\le\beta\rho.
$$
When $\beta>\rho$, its area is at most $\beta\rho^2/[2(\beta-\rho)]$. Equality holds exactly when the closure of the sector in $(u,v)$ is the corresponding closed triangle. This bound is attained for each $\beta>\rho$. When $\beta\le\rho$, the two endpoints alone give no finite uniform area bound for the sector.

1a4f9cc73e4a014c:03.reason: For the same depth-attaining cap menu the accepted chord centers bound both endpoint distances. Applying the sharp two-endpoint sector envelope gives the strict scale inequalities at their exact hypotheses.
1a4f9cc73e4a014c:03.statement:
Let $A,K,B\subset\mathbb R^2$ be convex bodies at the only integer bases $-1,0,1$, respectively, with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. Use planar area on each fiber. Fix $y\in\operatorname{int}K$ and nonzero spanning vectors $v_1,v_2,v_3$ with $\sum_i v_i=0$. With $h_i=\max_{x\in B}v_i\cdot x$, assume that each closed ambient cap
$$

$$
p_{\mathcal A}(y)=\inf_{H\ni(j,y)}\sum_i |\{x\in A_i:(p_i,x)\in H\}|,
\qquad y\in D_{\mathcal A},
$$
where $H$ ranges over closed ambient halfspaces and $|\cdot|$ denotes ordinary $d$-volume.

$$

2b7d1c7e003a98d0:1.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite set in an affine Euclidean space, with masses $m_z>0$ for $z\in P$, and put $Q=\operatorname{conv} P$ and $M=\sum_{z\in P}m_z$. Fix $N>0$ and $p\in Q$. Let $F_p$ be the unique face of $Q$ with $p\in\operatorname{relint} F_p$, and write $P_p=P\cap F_p$ and $V_p=\operatorname{span}(F_p-p)$. Set
$$
L_z(\alpha)=1+\alpha\cdot(z-p),\qquad
E_p=\inf_{\substack{\alpha\in V_p\\L_z(\alpha)>0\ (z\in P_p)}}\sum_{z\in P_p}m_z L_z(\alpha)^{-N}.
$$

The infimum is attained at a unique $\alpha_p$. Its value is also the infimum of the analogous sum over $P$ with $\alpha\in\operatorname{span}(Q-p)$ and all denominators positive. This latter infimum is attained exactly when $F_p=Q$. In particular a singleton face $F_p=\{p\}$ gives $E_p=m_p$.

Let $e_z=m_zL_z(\alpha_p)^{-N-1}$ on $P_p$, and $e_z=0$ off $P_p$. Then $\sum_{z\in P}e_z=E_p$ and $\sum_{z\in P}e_z z=E_p p$. With $s=N/(N+1)$,
$$
E_p=\max_{\substack{\lambda_z\ge0,\ \sum_{z\in P}\lambda_z=1\\\sum_{z\in P}\lambda_z z=p}}
\left(\sum_{z\in P}m_z^{1/(N+1)}\lambda_z^s\right)^{N+1},
$$
and the unique maximizer is $\lambda_z=e_z/E_p$. In particular $E_p^{1/(N+1)}$ is concave on $Q$. If $\pi_z=m_z/M$ and $D_s(\lambda\Vert\pi)=(s-1)^{-1}\log\sum_z\lambda_z^s\pi_z^{1-s}$, then $E_p/M=\exp(-\min_\lambda D_s(\lambda\Vert\pi))$, over the same constraint set.

If $p\in P$ and $m_z$ are volumes of positive-volume compact convex $d$-fibers $K_z$ with centroids $g_z$, assume $\sum_z\lambda_z K_z\subseteq K_p$ for the displayed maximizing row (as for fibers of a convex body). Then $\sum_z\lambda_z g_z\in\operatorname{int}K_p$.

$$

3502773126e88b57:01.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^D$ be a convex body, let $\mu$ be uniform probability on $K$, and let $\pi:\mathbb R^D\to\mathbb R^r$ be a surjective linear map with $1\le r\le D$. Put $\nu=\pi_\#\mu$ and $B=\pi K$. Let $\alpha$ be the maximum closed-halfspace depth for $\nu$ and let $\mathcal A$ be its set of maximizers. The set $\mathcal A$ is nonempty and compact in $\operatorname{int}B$. Let $\ell$ have width one on $B$ and let $p$ be the scalar section-volume density of $\ell_\#\nu$, extended by zero off its support. Then $0\le p\le D$. For each $c_*\in\mathcal A$, put $t_*=\ell(c_*)$ and $L=t_*-\min_B\ell$. Then $p(t_*)\ge\alpha$ and
$$
\nu\{x:t_*-a\le\ell(x)\le t_*\}\ge\alpha a/D\qquad (0\le a\le L).
$$
In particular, if $c\in B$ and $\ell(c_*-c)\ge0$, the cap $\{x:\ell(x-c)\ge0\}$ has mass at least $\alpha+(\alpha/D)\ell(c_*-c)$.

Put $\nu=\pi_\#\mu$ and $B=\pi K$. Write $\gamma_0=1$ and $\gamma_j=(j/(j+1))^j$ for $j\ge1$. Suppose finitely many closed halfspaces $H_i=\{x:\ell_i(x-c)\ge0\}$ cover $\mathbb R^r$, each $\ell_i$ has width one on $B$, and $\nu(H_i)\le\tau<\gamma_{r-1}$ for every $i$. Then $c\in\operatorname{int}B$ and
$$
\max_i\ell_i(v)\ge\frac{\gamma_{r-1}-\tau}{D}\qquad(v\in\partial(B-B)).
$$
Equivalently, the convex hull of the $\ell_i$ contains $(\gamma_{r-1}-\tau)(B-B)^\circ/D$, where $(B-B)^\circ$ is the polar in the dual space. In particular, the $\ell_i$ span the dual space.

3c669076dab13e6a:01.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be real, and let $(w_i)$ be a nonzero nonnegative sequence on a finite consecutive integer interval, with $(w_i^{1/d})$ concave there and $\sum_i i w_i=0$. Put $M=\sum_i w_i$, $m=\max_i w_i$, $r_d=(2/(d+2))^{(d+1)/d}$ and $\kappa_d=1/(3+d r_d)$. For every integer $h\ge0$,
$$
\min\left\{\sum_{i>h}w_i,\ \sum_{i<-h}w_i\right\}
\ge\kappa_d\bigl[M-(2h+1)m\bigr].
$$
The constants satisfy $1/5<\kappa_d\le9/31<3/10$, with $\kappa_1=9/31$ and $\lim_{d\to\infty}\kappa_d=1/5$.

Let $d$ be a positive integer and $C\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ a convex body of positive mixed $d$-volume $M$ whose mixed-volume centroid has integer base coordinate $j$. Write $w_i=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_i)$ and $m=\max_{i\in\mathbb Z} w_i$. With $\kappa_d$ as above, each of $z>j+h$ and $z<j-h$ has mixed $d$-volume in $C\cap(\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R^d)$ at least $\kappa_d[M-(2h+1)m]$ for every integer $h\ge0$.

Then F_{s+v}≤(T^β−vc)_+^(d+1) for every integer v≥0, using F_{s+v}=0 beyond r for this estimate. In particular ∑_{i≥s}(i−s+1)w_i≤T+T^(1+β)/((d+2)c). For a single-term suffix the distance moment is exactly T.

3ed6256a0896f434:01.statement:
Let $L\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a compact convex body with $0\in\operatorname{int}L$. Let $p_1,\ldots,p_N$ be nonzero vectors with $\pm p_i\in\partial L$. Write $R(x_1,x_2)=(-x_2,x_1)$ and $H_i=\{x:(Rp_i)\cdot x\ge0\}$. Suppose $\lambda_i\ge0$, $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$, and $\sum_i\lambda_i p_i=0$. For every real $b\ge4/3$ and $q_i\in[1,b]$, put $\theta_i=\lambda_iq_i/\sum_j\lambda_jq_j$. Then
$$
\sum_i\theta_i\frac{|L\cap H_i|}{|L|}\ge\frac1{1+b}.
$$
In particular the lower bounds at $b=4/3$ and $b=3/2$ are $3/7$ and $2/5$.

46f947c28385c3ea:01.statement:
Let $n,d\ge1$ be integers, let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body, and put $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$. For $z\in\mathbb Z^n$ set $K_z=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}$. Assume that the maximum affine dimension $q$ of the nonempty integer fibers satisfies $1\le q\le d$. Set $\mu=\mathcal H_q|_S$, and for
$$
P=\{z:\dim K_z=q\},\qquad w_z=\mathcal H_q(K_z),\qquad v_z=(1,z),
$$
write $Z=\sum_{z\in P}[0,w_z]v_z$. The set $Z$ is exactly the set of pairs $(\eta(S),\int_S z\,d\eta)$ for positive measures $0\le\eta\le\mu$.

Fix any $u\in\mathbb R^d$ such that $x\mapsto u\cdot x$ is nonconstant on $\operatorname{aff}K_z$ for every $z\in P$. Such $u$ exist, and if $q=d$ every nonzero $u$ qualifies. For every $r\in Z$ there are finite $b\in\mathbb R$ and $a\in\mathbb R^n$ such that the single closed halfspace
$$
H=\{(z,x)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d:b+a\cdot z+u\cdot x\ge0\}
$$
satisfies $\mu(\partial H)=0$ and $(\mu(H),\int_H z\,d\mu)=r$. This includes the zero and full-mass targets and arbitrary real first moments.

If the mass $t$ of $r$ is positive, $D=C\cap H$ is a convex body with maximum integer-fiber dimension $q$ and $\mathcal H_q|_{D\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)}=\mu|_H$. If $r=(t,tj)$ with $j\in\mathbb Z^n$, the barycenter of this unweighted intrinsic measure belongs to $D\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$ and $D_j=\{x:(j,x)\in D\}$ has positive $\mathcal H_q$ measure. In particular, for an integer $j$, if
$$
T_j=\max\left\{\sum_{z\in P}s_z:0\le s_z\le w_z,\quad \sum_{z\in P}(z-j)s_z=0\right\}>0 ,
$$
then $T_j$ is the maximum mass of a dominated submeasure with base barycenter $j$ and also the maximum retained mass of a convex subbody of $C$ with that base barycenter, measured using the original exponent $q$. A single cap with the prescribed direction $u$ attains both maxima.

49e262af8d182671:03.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with nonempty interior, and let $y\in\operatorname{int}K$. Define
$$
E_K(y)=\min_{\substack{a\in\mathbb R^d\\1+a\cdot(x-y)>0\ (x\in K)}}
\int_K[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx,\qquad
T_K(y)=\max_{\substack{0\le f\le1\\\int_K(x-y)f(x)\,dx=0}}\int_Kf(x)\,dx,
$$
where $f$ is Lebesgue measurable. Both extrema are attained, and the energy minimizer is unique. The maximizing density for $T_K(y)$ is the indicator, up to null sets, of a unique convex cap of centroid $y$. The cap is all of $K$ at its centroid. In particular $T_K(y)$ is the greatest volume of a convex subbody of $K$ with centroid $y$.

For every such $(K,y)$,
$$
0<T_K(y)\le E_K(y)<(d+1)T_K(y).
$$
Equality $T_K(y)=E_K(y)$ holds exactly when $y$ is the centroid of $K$. For each fixed $d\ge1$, the supremum of $E_K(y)/T_K(y)$ over these pairs is $d+1$, and no pair attains it. More precisely, if $K=\operatorname{conv}\{0,e_1,\ldots,e_d\}$ and $y=(\varepsilon,\ldots,\varepsilon)$ with $0<\varepsilon\le1/(d+1)$, then
$$
\frac{E_K(y)}{T_K(y)}=(d+1)(1-d\varepsilon).
$$
For an arbitrary simplex of volume $V$ and an interior mark with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_d$, $E_K(y)=V(d+1)^{d+1}\prod_{i=0}^d\lambda_i$. In dimension one, for $K-y=[-\ell,r]$ with $\ell,r>0$, $T_K(y)=2\min(\ell,r)$ and $E_K(y)=4\ell r/(\ell+r)$.

$$
\nabla F(0,0)=\frac1V\binom{M_1(0)}{-S(0)},\qquad
\nabla^2F(0,0)=\frac1V
\begin{pmatrix}
-M_2'(0)&M_1'(0)\\
M_1'(0)^\mathsf T&-S'(0)
\end{pmatrix}.
$$

=\frac1V\int_{\partial Q_0}zz^\mathsf T\,\frac{N_t}{\lVert N_z\rVert}\,d\mathcal H^{k-1}(z).

5048c7e97ca98aef:02.statement:
Let $C\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R$ be a convex body whose only nonempty integer fibers are positive-length intervals at three consecutive bases. After an integer base translation, a possible base reflection, and a shear affine in the base, its fibers at $-1,0,1$ have the form
$$
K_-=[-a/2,a/2],\qquad K_0=[s-U/2,s+U/2],\qquad K_+=[-b/2,b/2],
$$
where $0<a\le b$ and $U>0$. These parameters are realizable exactly when $U\ge(a+b)/2$ and $|s|\le U/2-(a+b)/4$.

Write $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R)$ and $W=a+b+U$. For $y\in S$, let $h_S(y)$ be the infimum of the total fiber length captured by closed ambient halfspaces containing $y$. Thus $h_S$ is raw depth, and $h_S/W$ is normalized depth. With $g(x)=\min\{a,\max\{0,(a+b)/2-2x\}\}$, for every $x\in K_0$,
$$
h_S((0,x))=\min\{U/2+s-x+g(x),\ U/2-s+x+g(-x)\}.
$$
Set $\sigma=|s|$, $\alpha=(b-a)/4$, and $\beta=(b+3a)/4$. There is a unique maximizer on the middle fiber, $(0,x_*)$, with $x_*=0$ if $s=0$ and with the sign of $s$ otherwise. Its absolute coordinate and its raw depth $F$ are
$$
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{range}& |x_*|&F\\ \hline
0\le \sigma\le \alpha&\sigma&U/2+a\\
\alpha\le\sigma\le\beta&\sigma/2+(b-a)/8&U/2-\sigma/2+(b+7a)/8\\
\sigma\ge\beta&\sigma-a/2&(U+a)/2
\end{array}
$$
The formulas agree at their shared endpoints. On either endpoint fiber of length $c\in\{a,b\}$, the raw depth at height $x$ is $c/2-|x|$.

The global raw maximum is $Q=\max\{b/2,F\}$, and its normalized value is $Q/W$. The complete set of deepest points consists of $(0,x_*)$ when $U>b-2a$, of $(1,0)$ when $U<b-2a$, and of both when $U=b-2a$. Equality $U=b-2a$ is compatible precisely when $a\le b/5$ and $s$ obeys the compatibility condition above. In particular if $a=b$, the middle point is the unique deepest point.

For fixed $a,b,U$, $F$ and $Q/W$ are nonincreasing in $|s|$ on its feasible interval. At the largest compatible shift $|s|=U/2-(a+b)/4$ the middle raw maximum is
$$
F_{\mathrm{contact}}(a,b,U)=
\begin{cases}
U/2+a,&(a+b)/2\le U\le b,\\
(U+b)/4+a,&b\le U\le b+2a,\\
(U+a)/2,&U\ge b+2a.
\end{cases}
$$

55fd8fec61360536:03.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^D$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body with affine coordinates $(v,t,y)$, where $v\in\mathbb R^r$, $1\le r\le D-1$, $y\in\mathbb R^{D-r-1}$, and $t\ge0$ on $K$. Write $J>0$ for the constant volume Jacobian of these coordinates. The pushforward of $D$-volume on $K\cap\{t>0\}$ under $z=v/t$ has bounded integrable density
$$
F(z)=J\int_0^\infty\int_{\mathbb R^{D-r-1}}\mathbf1_K(tz,t,y)t^r\,dy\,dt
    =J\int_0^\infty\int_{\mathbb R^{D-r-1}}\mathbf1_\Omega(z,s,w)s^{-(D+1)}\,dw\,ds,
$$
where $\Omega=\{(z,s,w):s>0,\ (z/s,1/s,w/s)\in K\}$. The set $\{F>0\}$ is convex and full-dimensional, and $F^{-1/(r+1)}$ is convex on it. Its boundary may be discarded without changing the measure. The total mass is $|K|$, and any cap on $K$ with margin $a\cdot v+bt$ has exactly the mass of $\{z:a\cdot z+b\ge0\}$ under $F(z)\,dz$.

55fd8fec61360536:05.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^D$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body of volume $V$, with $D\ge1$. Let $H_1,\ldots,H_m$ be proper closed halfspaces covering $K$, where $m\ge1$, and write $A_i=|K\cap H_i|$. Put $\gamma_0=1$ and $\gamma_q=(q/(q+1))^q$ for integers $q\ge1$. For any fixed inclusion-minimal subcover indexed by $I$, let $j=|I|$ and let $\rho$ be the rank of its normals. For every $\alpha\ge0$,
$$
\sum_{i\in I}(A_i-\alpha)_+ + \frac{\alpha}{\gamma_{\min(\rho,j-1)}}\ge V,
\qquad x_+=\max(x,0).
$$
Consequently, with $s=\min(D,m-1)$,
$$
\sum_{i=1}^m(A_i-\alpha)_+ + \frac{\alpha}{\gamma_s}\ge V
\quad(\alpha\ge0),
\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^m A_i-V\ge (m-1/\gamma_s)\min_i A_i .
$$
For each pair $(D,m)$, $\gamma_s$ is the largest constant that can replace it in the all-cover positive-part profile.

571b5ceb2d4e114a:01.statement: Let $n\ge0$, $d\ge1$, $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite and nonempty, and $K_p\subset\mathbb R^d$ be convex bodies for $p\in P$. Fix $q\in P$. 571b5ceb2d4e114a:03.statement:
Let $n\ge0$, $d\ge3$, and let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty with $\operatorname{aff}(P)=\mathbb R^n$. For each $p\in P$ let $K_p\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body with nonempty interior. For each $q\in P$, let $E_q$ be the polytope of nonnegative coefficient vectors $(\lambda_p)_{p\ne q}$ with $\sum_{p\ne q}\lambda_p=1$ and $\sum_{p\ne q}\lambda_p p=q$. The family is strictly compatible if for every $q\in P$ and every extreme point $\lambda$ of $E_q$, the Minkowski sum $\sum_{p\ne q}\lambda_p K_p$ is compactly contained in $\operatorname{int}K_q$. An empty $E_q$ imposes no condition. Let $C=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{p\in P}(\{p\}\times K_p)$ and assume its actual integer fibers are the given $K_p$. Let $\mu$ be the sum of $d$-dimensional Lebesgue measure on those fibers, $M$ its total mass, $\beta$ the maximum normalized closed-halfspace depth over the measured points, and $I$ the bases where this maximum is attained. Assume that $C$ is a local minimum of $\beta$ among all actual positive fiber families on this fixed $P$, in the fiberwise Hausdorff topology.

For each $p\in I$ fix a finite positive circuit of actual critical caps $H_{pj}=\{(z,x):a_{pj}\cdot z+u_{pj}\cdot x\ge b_{pj}\}$, with $\lVert u_{pj}\rVert=1$, $\rho_{pj}>0$, and $\sum_j\rho_{pj}u_{pj}=0$. Each circuit passes through an interior maximizing mark of its own fiber and its caps have raw mass $Q=\beta M$. Assume each old aggregate threshold mass is $Q-S_{pj}s+o(|s|)$ when its threshold is moved by $s\to0$ from either side, with $S_{pj}>0$. Write $\kappa_{pj}=(\rho_{pj}/S_{pj})/\sum_\ell(\rho_{p\ell}/S_{p\ell})$. Let a finite collection of nonempty relatively open boundary patches $U$ be given, each in some $\partial K_q$, with $U$ a $C^1$ hypersurface containing no nontrivial line segment.

There exists one probability vector $\pi$ on $I$ such that on every patch in the collection, at each point $x$ off all restricted cap planes, $\sum_{p\in I,j}\pi_p\kappa_{pj}\mathbf1_{H_{pj}}(q,x)=\beta$. For every listed unoriented restricted plane $L$ that meets the patch and intersects $\operatorname{int}K_q$, the total weight $\pi_p\kappa_{pj}$ of the restricted caps with plane $L$ is the same in either orientation.

If a patch in fiber $q$ is the whole boundary, let $F_q$ be the total stress weight of nonproper cap restrictions that contain the whole boundary off the planes, and $P_q$ the total stress weight of properly cutting restricted caps. Then $\beta=F_q+P_q/2$. For such a fiber with $q\in I$ one has $\pi_q\le2\beta$. If the collection includes the entire boundary of every deepest fiber, then $\beta\ge 1/(2|I|)$. The two-sided positive slope hypothesis holds automatically if every $K_p$ is strictly convex.

5811f0ad1132ce56:01.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with nonempty interior, and let $y\in\operatorname{int}K$. For $a\in\mathbb R^d$ put $L_a(x)=1+a\cdot(x-y)$ and define
$$
E_K(y)=\inf_{\{a:L_a>0\ \text{on }K\}}\int_K L_a(x)^{-d-1}\,dx.
$$
The infimum is positive and attained at a unique admissible $a_*$, and $E_K(y)$ is the minimum $d$-volume of the images of $K-y$ under $w\mapsto w/(1+a\cdot w)$ over these $a$. For $L=L_{a_*}$ and $E=E_K(y)$,
$$
\int_K (x-y)L(x)^{-d-2}\,dx=0,\qquad
\int_K L(x)^{-d-2}\,dx=\int_K L(x)^{-d-1}\,dx=E.
$$
Thus $\rho=L^{-d-2}/E$ on $K$ is a probability density with barycenter $y$ and $\int_K L\rho\,dx=1$. Its restriction to $K$ extends to a smooth positive function on a neighborhood of $K$.

For every invertible linear $Q$ and every $b\in\mathbb R^d$, $E_{QK+b}(Qy+b)=|\det Q|E_K(y)$. If $K\subset H$ for another convex body $H$, then $E_K(y)\le E_H(y)$ with equality exactly when $K=H$. Writing $g_K=|K|^{-1}\int_K x\,dx$ for the ordinary centroid, $E_K(y)\le |K|$ with equality exactly when $y=g_K$.

5811f0ad1132ce56:04.statement:
Let $d,m\ge1$, let $K_i\subset\mathbb R^d$ be convex bodies, and choose $y_i\in\operatorname{int}K_i$ and weights $\lambda_i\ge0$ with $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$. Use the energy $E_K(y)=\min_{a:\,1+a\cdot(x-y)>0\ (x\in K)}\int_K[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx$. Put $M=\sum_i\lambda_i K_i$ and $y=\sum_i\lambda_i y_i$. Then $y\in\operatorname{int}M$ and
$$
E_M(y)^{1/d}\ \ge\ \sum_i\lambda_i E_{K_i}(y_i)^{1/d}.
$$
Equality holds exactly when the centered bodies $K_i-y_i$ with $\lambda_i>0$ are positive scalar multiples of one another. In particular $y\mapsto E_K(y)^{1/d}$ is strictly concave on $\operatorname{int}K$.

If $H$ is a convex body containing $M$, the same lower bound holds for $E_H(y)^{1/d}$. Equality then requires both $H=M$ and the same marked homothety condition. Consequently, for a compact convex set $C\subset\mathbb R^{n+d}$ with fibers $C_z=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}$, the function $(z,y)\mapsto E_{C_z}(y)^{1/d}$ is jointly concave on the convex domain $\{(z,y): y\in\operatorname{int}_{\mathbb R^d}C_z\}$.

The maximum is over ordinary Lebesgue densities on $K$ with the displayed mass and mean. Its unique maximizer up to Lebesgue null sets is $\rho=L^{-d-2}/E_K(y)$, where $L(x)=1+a_*\cdot(x-y)$ is the attained optimal denominator.

58dcf29bfb78a573:02.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite subset of a real affine space, with $k$ occupied labels. Assume the geometric midpoint of every pair of distinct points of the same label belongs to $P$. Give each $p\in P$ a weight $w_p>0$, put $M=\sum_{p\in P}w_p$, $Q=\operatorname{conv}(P)$ and $\alpha=M/k$, and set $w(F)=\sum_{p\in P\cap F}w_p$ for each face $F$ of $Q$, allowing $Q$ itself. Let $\mathcal F$ be the faces of weight $\alpha$, and write $\chi_F$ for their incidence vectors on $P$.

Exactly one of the following holds.

1. There is $v\in\mathbb R^P$ with $\sum_{p\in P}v_p=0$ and $v\cdot\chi_F<0$ for every $F\in\mathcal F$. When $\mathcal F$ is empty, $v=0$ works.
2. The set $P$ consists of exactly $k$ vertices of $Q$, all of weight $\alpha$.

Moreover, a nonnegative combination $\sum_{F\in\mathcal F}\lambda_F\chi_F=\mathbf 1_P$ exists precisely in case 2. In that case its coefficients are $\lambda_{\{p\}}=1$ for all $p\in P$.

58dcf29bfb78a573:03.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite set in a real affine space with $k$ occupied labels. For every pair of distinct points of the same label, assume their geometric midpoint belongs to $P$. Give the points positive weights $w_p$, with total $M=\sum_{p\in P}w_p$. Let $Q=\operatorname{conv}(P)$ and let $F_p$ be the unique face of $Q$ whose relative interior contains $p$, allowing $Q$ itself. Write $w(F)=\sum_{p\in P\cap F}w_p$ and let $\delta_w(p)$ be the minimum weight in any closed affine halfspace containing $p$. The whole-space trace is allowed and is the sole trace containing $p$ in rank zero.

There exists $p\in P$ with $\delta_w(p)\ge M/k$. Such a point can be chosen with $w(F_p)>M/k$ except exactly when $P$ consists of $k$ vertices of $Q$ of weight $M/k$ each. In the exception every point has $\delta_w(p)=w(F_p)=M/k$. In particular, strict minimal-face mass holds for some center whenever $|P|>k$.

For a finite nonempty complete subset $P=Q\cap(c+L)$ of an affine lattice, the labels can be the occupied cosets modulo $2L$. Then $k\le 2^{\operatorname{rank} L}$, including rank zero. For a finite graph $P=\{(p,g_p):p\in P_0\}$ over an affine-lattice base, the labels can be the occupied base parities if every distinct same-parity pair $p,q\in P_0$ has $m=(p+q)/2\in P_0$ and $g_m=(g_p+g_q)/2$. In this graph case the depth and the minimal face are taken in the lifted space.

6146c77d1d7c5e08:01.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge2$ and $H>0$. Put $B=H+1$ and $r(z)=(H-z)/B$. On $-1\le z\le H$, $|x|\le r(z)$, take density $f(x,z)=r(z)^{d-2}/2$ with respect to $dx\,dz$. The total mass is $V=B/d$. For finite $s\ge0$, let $P(s)$ be the mass of the cap $z+sx\ge0$. Let $C(s)$ and $M(s)$ be the integrals of $f$ and $zf$, respectively, over the section $z+sx=0$ inside the support, against $d\mathcal H^1/\sqrt{1+s^2}$. The records of a probability law are the averages of $(P,C,M)$, and the law is centered if its averaged $M$ is zero. Write $C_0=(H/B)^{d-1}$ and $p_0=(H/B)^d$.

For a probability law on finite slopes, let $\phi$ be the mixture of uniform probability laws on $[-s,s]$ with the given slope weights and with $\delta_0$ at $s=0$. Put $v=\phi((-\infty,1])$, $a_0=1/B$, and $e(q)=\int_{b\le1}(1-qb)^{-d}\,d\phi(b)$ for $0<q<1$. Then $1/2<v\le1$ and the averaged records are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overline P/V &= p_0e(a_0)+1-v,\\
\overline C/C_0 &= e(a_0),\\
\overline M/C_0 &= -\frac HB\int_{b\le1} b(1-b/B)^{-d-1}\,d\phi(b).
\end{aligned}
$$

The function $e$ is convex and differentiable on $(0,1)$. Centering is equivalent to $e'(a_0)=0$, or equivalently to $a_0$ minimizing $e$ on $(0,1)$. Every such centered law satisfies $2v-1\le e(a_0)\le(2v-1)/v$.

For finite $s\ge0$, let $P(s)$ be the mass of the cap $z+sx\ge0$. Let $C(s)$ and $M(s)$ be the integrals of $f$ and $zf$, respectively, over the section $z+sx=0$ inside the support, against $d\mathcal H^1/\sqrt{1+s^2}$. The records of a probability law are the averages of $(P,C,M)$, and the law is centered if its averaged $M$ is zero. Write $C_0=(H/B)^{d-1}$ and $p_0=(H/B)^d$.

Allow also an atom at $s=\infty$, whose record is the limit $(V/2,0,0)$ as $s\to\infty$. Put $c=(V/C_0)(p_0-4/9)$. Every centered probability law on $[0,\infty]$ satisfies $4V/9\le\overline P-c\overline C\le5V/9$, with this same $c$.

For any two separately centered probability laws $\mu,\nu$ with $\overline C_\mu+\overline C_\nu>0$,

$$
\frac{\overline C_\nu\overline P_\mu+\overline C_\mu(V-\overline P_\nu)}
{V(\overline C_\mu+\overline C_\nu)}\ge\frac49\ge
\Gamma_d:=\left(\frac d{d+1}\right)^d.
$$

If exactly one coarea is zero, the quotient is $1/2$. If both are zero, both cap fractions are $1/2$ and the quotient has continuous extension $1/2$ in the records.

61c2a6c203bcade2:06.statement:

$$
v_{\alpha,z}(x)=\sum_{a=1}^N\alpha_a v_{a,z}(x)
$$
at every regular point $x$ of every original measured boundary $\partial K_z$. It has first total loss $D_\alpha=\sum_a\alpha_a D_a$ and, for every fixed closed ambient halfspace $H$, first cap loss $L_\alpha(H)=\sum_a\alpha_a L_a(H)$, with uniform little-o remainders on each fixed finite cap list. If every $\alpha_a=0$, the constructed action is identically $C$ for all $\varepsilon\ge0$. All actions, including the constructed one, have zero-parameter body exactly $C$. The speeds and their finite linear response vectors therefore form algebraic cones under finite nonnegative combinations.

660db01ed45063dd:01.statement:
For real $d\ge1$, set $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, $A_d=1/\Gamma_d$, and $L_d=4A_d/3-1$. Write $t_+=\max(t,0)$ and define

$$
\Delta_d=2+(1+1/d)(1+A_d/3)
   -2(1+1/(2d))^{d+1}-2(1-L_d/(2d))_+^{d+1},
\qquad \varepsilon_d=\frac{d}{d+1}\Delta_d.
$$

Then $\Delta_d>0$. For each integer $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, let $0\le\eta\le\mathbf 1_K\,dx$, and let $g$ be the centroid of $\mathbf 1_K\,dx+2\eta$. Then $g\in\operatorname{int}K$, and every closed halfspace $H$ containing $g$ satisfies

$$
|K\cap H|+\eta(H)\ \ge\
\frac{3\Gamma_d}{4}(|K|+\eta(K))
+\frac{3\Gamma_d^2\varepsilon_d}{4\cdot3^d}|K|.
$$

660db01ed45063dd:02.reason: The exact equal-mass midpoint coupling identifies the selected point as the actual mixed centroid. The bound has a uniform surplus over all cap directions.
660db01ed45063dd:02.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, and let $A,K,B\subset\mathbb R^d$ be convex bodies of volumes $v,k,v>0$ with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. Let $\mu$ be the sum of the $d$-volumes on the integer fibers $A,K,B$ at bases $-1,0,1$ of their lifted convex hull. The actual mixed centroid is

$$
Y=\left(0,\frac{v g_A+k g_K+v g_B}{k+2v}\right),
$$

where $g_A,g_K,g_B$ are the uniform-volume centroids. It lies in $\lbrace 0\rbrace\times\operatorname{int}K$. Write $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, $A_d=1/\Gamma_d$, and let the positive constant $\varepsilon_d$ be

$$
\varepsilon_d=\frac{d}{d+1}\left[2+(1+1/d)(1+A_d/3)
-2(1+1/(2d))^{d+1}-2(1-(4A_d/3-1)/(2d))_+^{d+1}\right],
$$

with $t_+=\max(t,0)$. The raw depth at $Y$, the infimum of $\mu(H)$ over closed ambient halfspaces containing $Y$, is at least

$$
\frac{3\Gamma_d}{4}(k+v)+
\min\left(\frac{3\Gamma_d^2\varepsilon_d k}{4\cdot3^d},
               (1-3\Gamma_d/4)(k+v)\right).
$$

In particular it is strictly greater than $(3\Gamma_d/4)(k+v)\ge(\Gamma_d/2)(k+2v)$. The same conclusion holds in any convex body whose only positive $d$-volume integer fibers are those three fibers; any other integer fibers of zero $d$-volume do not affect $\mu$.

6748c967393345b9:09.statement:

\sum_{z\in P}\lambda_z K_z\subseteq K_p
\quad\text{whenever}\quad
\lambda_z\ge0,\qquad \sum_{z\in P}\lambda_z=1,\qquad \sum_{z\in P}\lambda_z z=p .
\tag{1}
$$
Use the given Euclidean base coordinates. The affine rank $r=\dim\operatorname{span}(P-p)$ may be any integer from $0$ to $n$. Write $h_z(u)=\max_{x\in K_z}u\cdot x$. For every $u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}$ the inequalities
$$
h_z(u)\le h_p(u)+A\cdot(z-p)\qquad(z\in P)
\tag{2}
$$
have a unique minimum-Euclidean-norm solution $A_p(u)$. It lies in $\operatorname{span}(P-p)$, and the map $u\mapsto A_p(u)$ is continuous and bounded. The affine function $z\mapsto h_p(u)+A_p(u)\cdot(z-p)$ yields a supporting inequality $u\cdot x\le h_p(u)+A_p(u)\cdot(z-p)$ on $\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$, with equality at every point of the $u$-supporting face of $\{p\}\times K_p$.

773c78a48aafd464:02.statement:
Let $P\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be finite, with capacities $a_z>0$ for $z\in P$. Fix a mass $m\ge0$ and a vector $g\in\mathbb R^n$, and assume
$$
Q=\{b:0\le b_z\le a_z,\ \sum_{z\in P}b_z=m,\ \sum_{z\in P}z b_z=mg\}
$$
is nonempty. A point of $Q$ is extreme exactly when the columns $(1,z)$ at its partially filled sites $0<b_z<a_z$ are linearly independent. Every linear cost $\sum_z c_zb_z$ has an extreme minimizer, and this minimizer has at most $\operatorname{rank}((1,z)_{z\in P})\le n+1$ partially filled sites.

There are a scalar $\lambda$ and vector $v\in\mathbb R^n$ such that the minimum value is
$$
\lambda m+v\cdot(mg)+\sum_{z\in P}a_z\min(0,c_z-\lambda-v\cdot z).
$$
For this pair a feasible $b$ is optimal exactly when $b_z=a_z$ at each strict negative reduced cost $c_z-\lambda-v\cdot z$ and $b_z=0$ at each strict positive one. If $c_z=\|z-g\|_2^2$ and $m>0$, the reduced cost is the squared distance from $g+v/2$ minus a nonnegative squared radius. Every optimizer thus fills the strict interior sites of the corresponding closed ball, leaves its exterior sites empty, and can be fractional only on its sphere.

\lVert v-x_0\rVert_2\le \frac{mV_0}{\kappa_{m-1}r^{m-1}},

The middle body $B$ is arbitrary subject to $m+\rho K\subseteq B$.

Write $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ and $c_d=(2\Gamma_d)^{1/d}$. For $0<r\le s$ put
$$
\Phi_d(r,s)=
\begin{cases}
r,&d=1,\\
\left[r c_d+\dfrac{s-r}{d-1}(1-c_d)\right]^d,&d\ge2,\ r\le s\le dr,\\
r^d,&d\ge2,\ s\ge dr,
\end{cases}
$$
and extend $\Phi_d$ symmetrically to $r>s$. The branches agree at $s=dr$.

Let $a=r^dV$, $b=s^dV$, $U=|B|$, and let $g_B$ be the ordinary volume centroid of $B$. If $S$ is the actual mixed-integer part of the body and $h_S$ is its raw depth, then
$$
h_S((0,m))\ge V[\Gamma_d\rho^d+\Phi_d(r,s)],
\qquad
h_S((0,g_B))\ge\Gamma_d U.
$$
In particular, under the scalar condition
$$
\rho^d+\frac{\Phi_d(r,s)}{\Gamma_d}\ge r^d+s^d,
$$
choosing $(0,m)$ for $U\le a+b$ and $(0,g_B)$ for $U\ge a+b$, with either choice at equality, gives raw depth at least $\Gamma_d(a+b+U)/2$ and normalized depth at least $\Gamma_d/2$. The same conclusion holds under the simpler sufficient condition $b/a\le (3+\sqrt5)/2$.

81d65baa0f0a1024:01.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let $\mu$ be uniform probability on $F=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:x_i\ge0,\ \sum_i x_i=1\}$, and let $g=(1/d,\ldots,1/d)$. Independently take $Z\sim\mu$ and a uniform vertex index $I$. For $0\le b\le1/d$ put $Y_b=(1-b)Z+be_I$ and $a=1-db$. The largest constant for which
$$
\mathbb E\psi(Y_b)-\mathbb E\psi(Z)
\ge c_d(b)\bigl(\psi(g)-\mathbb E\psi(Z)\bigr)
$$
holds for every continuous concave $\psi$ on $F$ is
$$
c_d(b)=\frac{a-a^d/(1-b)^{d-1}}{(d-1)^2}.
$$
It is positive for $0<b<1/d$ and vanishes at both endpoints. The test $\psi(x)=\min_i x_i$ attains equality with a positive Jensen gap throughout the parameter interval. In particular,
$$
c_d\bigl(1/(d+1)\bigr)=\frac{1-d^{1-d}}{(d-1)^2(d+1)}.
$$

**Facet consequence.** On any facet of a $d$-simplex, $d\ge2$, let $\mu$ be normalized facet volume, $s_1,\ldots,s_d$ its barycentric coordinates, and $g_F$ its centroid. Set $m=d+1$, $\Gamma=(d/m)^d$, $c=c_d(1/m)$, $N(s)=\#\{i:s_i\ge1/m\}$, and $E_d(\psi)=\int_F(N-m\Gamma)\psi\,d\mu$. The uniform point $Z$ and averaged point $Y_{1/m}$ on the facet obey
$$
E_d(\psi)=m\Gamma\bigl(\mathbb E\psi(Y_{1/m})-\mathbb E\psi(Z)\bigr).
$$
For every continuous concave $\psi$ and every supporting affine majorant $\ell$ at $g_F$,
$$
\int_F(\ell-\psi)\,d\mu=\psi(g_F)-\int_F\psi\,d\mu\le\frac{E_d(\psi)}{m\Gamma c}.
$$
The coefficient is sharp, and $E_d(\psi)=0$ exactly for affine $\psi$. In convex form, every continuous convex $f\ge0$ with $f(g_F)=0$ satisfies $\int_F Nf\,d\mu\le m\Gamma(1-c)\int_F f\,d\mu$.

For any continuous concave ψ and any affine supporting majorant ℓ at the facet centroid g, E_d(ψ)=mΓ[Eψ(Y_{1/m})−Eψ(Z)] and ∫(ℓ−ψ)dμ=ψ(g)−∫ψ dμ≤E_d(ψ)/(mΓc_d). The coefficient is sharp, and E_d(ψ)=0 iff ψ is affine.

81d65baa0f0a1024:03.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $m=d+1$, $\Gamma=(d/m)^d$, $c=(1-d^{1-d})/[(d-1)^2(d+1)]$, and $V=1/d!$. Let $B=\{z\in\mathbb R^{d-1}:z_j\ge0,\ \sum_j z_j\le1\}$, with normalized volume $\mu$ and barycentric coordinates $s=(z_1,\ldots,z_{d-1},1-\sum_j z_j)$. For a fixed continuous concave $\psi\ge0$ on $B$ and $\varepsilon>0$ put
$$
K_\varepsilon=\{(z,r):z\in B,\ \sum_jz_j-1\le r\le\varepsilon\psi(z)\}.
$$
This is a full-dimensional convex body, with $|K_\varepsilon|=V+\varepsilon dV\int_B\psi\,d\mu$. Let $\ell(z)=A+\sum_j B_jz_j$ be a fixed supporting affine majorant at the centroid of $B$. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, the simplex $S_\varepsilon$ given by
$$
q\ge0,\qquad z_j\ge0,\qquad q+\sum_j(1-\varepsilon B_j)z_j\le1+\varepsilon A,\qquad q=r-\sum_jz_j+1
$$
encloses $K_\varepsilon$. It satisfies
$$
|S_\varepsilon|=\frac{V(1+\varepsilon A)^d}{\prod_j(1-\varepsilon B_j)},\qquad
1-\frac{|K_\varepsilon|}{|S_\varepsilon|}
=\varepsilon d\int_B(\ell-\psi)\,d\mu+O(\varepsilon^2).
$$
For a full-dimensional body $K$, write $D(K)$ for maximum ordinary halfspace depth with respect to normalized volume. With $E_d(\psi)=\int_B[\#\{i:s_i\ge1/m\}-m\Gamma]\psi\,d\mu$,
$$
D(K_\varepsilon)=\Gamma+\varepsilon\frac{d}{m}E_d(\psi)+o(\varepsilon).
$$
For each fixed nonaffine roof the denominator in the following limit has positive linear coefficient, and
$$
\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}
\frac{D(K_\varepsilon)-\Gamma}{1-|K_\varepsilon|/|S_\varepsilon|}
=\frac{E_d(\psi)}{m\int_B(\ell-\psi)\,d\mu}
\ge\Gamma c.
$$
Equality in this limit is attained by $\psi=\min_i s_i$. If $\psi$ is affine, both linear terms vanish and the enclosing simplex formula still holds. The total variation distance of the two normalized uniform laws equals the displayed missing fraction, which therefore bounds their discrepancy over closed halfspaces. All error estimates are for the fixed roof and, where applicable, the fixed majorant.

821242aee5d2f3e1:02.statement:

$$
S_d(q+1)^{1/(d+1)}+S_d(q-1)^{1/(d+1)}\le 2S_d(q)^{1/(d+1)}.

For each fixed $d$ the exponent $1/(d+1)$ is the largest positive exponent that works uniformly over the sequences $A_m$.

821242aee5d2f3e1:04.statement:

$$
\sum_{i\ge\mu}a_i>\left(\frac{d+1}{d+2}\right)^{d+1},
\qquad
\sum_{i\le\mu}a_i>\left(\frac{d+1}{d+2}\right)^{d+1}.
$$
At every fixed $d$ this constant is the infimum of either tail among profiles with exactly integer mean.

For the geometric consequence, let $d$ be a positive integer and $C\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ a convex body with positive mixed $d$-volume $W$. If the base coordinate of its mixed-volume centroid is an integer, every closed vertical halfspace containing the centroid has mixed $d$-volume strictly greater than $W((d+1)/(d+2))^{d+1}$. This normalized bound is also sharp as an infimum.

A finite global-cut action on $C$ uses a nonempty finite index set $I$. For each $i\in I$, its function $\ell_i(u,z)$ is continuous in $u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}$ and affine in $z\in\operatorname{aff}(P)$, with $\ell_i(u,z)\ge h_z(u)$ on $P$. Its field $V_i(u,z,x)$ is jointly continuous and nonnegative on $\mathbb S^{d-1}\times C$ and convex in $(z,x)$ on $C$ for each fixed $u$. Fields satisfying these assumptions on a larger common convex domain can be restricted to $C$. For $\varepsilon\ge0$ define
$$
C_\varepsilon=C\cap
\bigcap_{i\in I,\;u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}}
\{(z,x):u\cdot x+\varepsilon V_i(u,z,x)\le\ell_i(u,z)\}.
$$
Then $C_0=C$, and for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon\ge0$, $C_\varepsilon$ is a nested compact convex body in $\operatorname{aff}(P)\times\mathbb R^d$. Its projection is $\operatorname{conv}(P)$, its integer fibers $K_z(\varepsilon)=(C_\varepsilon)_z$ have nonempty interior exactly for $z\in P$, and it has no other integer fibers. The deformed fibers satisfy all the same anchored Minkowski inclusions.

At a regular $x\in\partial K_z$, with unique outward unit normal $\nu_z(x)$, define
$$
v_z(x)=\max\Bigl(\{V_i(\nu_z(x),z,x):i\in I,\ \ell_i(\nu_z(x),z)=h_z(\nu_z(x))\}\cup\{0\}\Bigr).
$$
About each fixed $o_z\in\operatorname{int}K_z$, let $s_\varepsilon(x)$ be the fractional radial loss, so the new endpoint on the ray through $x$ is $o_z+(1-s_\varepsilon(x))(x-o_z)$. $$
|K_z|-|K_z(\varepsilon)|=\varepsilon\int_{\partial K_z}v_z\,dS+o(\varepsilon),
\qquad dS=d\mathcal H^{d-1}.
$$

Let $\mu_\varepsilon(H)=\sum_{z\in P}|K_z(\varepsilon)\cap H_z|$, where $H_z=\{x:(z,x)\in H\}$ for a fixed closed ambient halfspace $H$. The second includes an outside supporting trace, even when that trace has positive surface measure. Then
$$

\qquad L(H)=\sum_{z\in P}\int_{\partial K_z}\kappa_{z,H}v_z\,dS.
$$

86934b651b11f7d5:01.reason: The same cap's signed derivative determines the A and K chord moments and the location of the B interval. The symmetric intersection gauge gives the reciprocal weight bound on that same actual menu.
86934b651b11f7d5:01.statement:
Let $A,K,B\subset\mathbb R^2$ be convex bodies at the only integer bases $-1,0,1$, respectively, with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. Use planar area on each fiber. Fix $y\in\operatorname{int}K$ and nonzero spanning vectors $v_1,v_2,v_3$ with $\sum_i v_i=0$. Set $h_i=h_B(v_i)$, where $h_B(v)=\max_{x\in B}v\cdot x$, and $b_i=2v_i\cdot y-h_i$. Assume each of the three closed ambient caps
$$
v_i\cdot(x-y)+(v_i\cdot y-h_i)z\ge0
$$
attains the actual mixed depth at $(0,y)$, and cuts both $A$ and $K$ properly. The trace on $B$ is the supporting face $F_i=B\cap\{v_i\cdot x=h_i\}$. Let $a_i,k_i$ be the lengths of the $A,K$ cutting chords, respectively, divided by $\lVert v_i\rVert$. Put $\lambda_i=1/(2a_i+k_i)$ and $\Lambda=\sum_i\lambda_i$.

Let $J$ be rotation through a right angle. Give the three cutting lines compatible coordinates by writing $x=y+r v_i/\lVert v_i\rVert^2+uJv_i$, using the appropriate constant $r$ on each line. Let $c_{A,i}$ and $c_i$ be the $u$-centers of the $A,K$ chords. Then $F_i$ contains a $u$-interval of length $a_i$ centered at $-c_{A,i}-(k_i/a_i)c_i$. In particular,
$$
k_i\ge a_i,\qquad
|c_i|\le \frac{a_i(k_i-a_i)}{k_i+2a_i}.
$$
For the single centrally symmetric body $(K-y)\cap(y-K)$, its Minkowski gauge $N$ satisfies
$$
2\lambda_i\le N(Jv_i)\le 6\lambda_i,\qquad
\lambda_i\le3\sum_{j\ne i}\lambda_j,\qquad
\frac{\lambda_i}{\Lambda}\le\frac34.
$$

86934b651b11f7d5:02.reason: Integrate weighted capture on the disappearing shell and separate the singly captured points. The proper cuts give the stated exact first-order cap losses.
86934b651b11f7d5:02.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body and let the finitely many closed halfspaces $H_i=\{x:v_i\cdot x\ge b_i\}$ cover $A$ and cut it properly. Write $w_i>0$, $U_i=|A\cap H_i|$ and $\sigma_i=\mathcal H^{d-1}(A\cap\{v_i\cdot x=b_i\})/\lVert v_i\rVert$. If $\sum_{i:x\in H_i}w_i\ge\tau$ almost everywhere on $A$, then every $p\in A$ satisfies
$$
\sum_i w_i\bigl[dU_i+(b_i-v_i\cdot p)\sigma_i\bigr]\ge d|A|\tau.
$$
If all singleton-capture regions with indices in a set $E$ are null, a valid $\tau$ is the minimum of the singleton weights $w_i$ for $i\notin E$ and all pair sums $w_i+w_j$ with $i\ne j$, taking the minimum over the combined nonempty list.

86934b651b11f7d5:03.reason: The fixed-B-facet equal-budget equations give the common-budget derivative under one endpoint contraction. Global descent requires the two strict endpoint gaps. The below-2/9 specialization with an original global budget has empty hypotheses by 2a8c2bc6d7992c5e.
86934b651b11f7d5:03.statement:
Let $A,K,B\subset\mathbb R^2$ be convex bodies at the only integer bases $-1,0,1$, with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. Fix $y\in\operatorname{int}K$, and nonzero spanning normals $v_i$ for $1\le i\le3$ with $\sum_i v_i=0$. Put $h_i=h_B(v_i)$ and $b_i=2v_i\cdot y-h_i$. Suppose the caps $v_i\cdot(x-y)+(v_i\cdot y-h_i)z\ge0$ have common raw mass $Q$ and proper $A,K$ cuts. Write $a=|A|$, $M=|A|+|K|+|B|$, $U_i=|A\cap\{v_i\cdot x\ge b_i\}|$, and $a_i,k_i$ for the $A,K$ chord lengths divided by $\lVert v_i\rVert$. Put $s_i=2a_i+k_i$, $\lambda_i=1/s_i$, $\Lambda=\sum_i\lambda_i$, and
$$
L_i(p)=2U_i+(b_i-v_i\cdot p)a_i,\qquad
\overline L(p)=\frac{\sum_i\lambda_i L_i(p)}{\Lambda}.
$$

For every $p\in A$, contract $A$ to $A_t=p+(1-t)(A-p)$ and keep $K,B$ fixed. For all sufficiently small $t\ge0$ there is a $C^1$ meeting point $y(t)$ with $y(0)=y$ and a common cap budget $q(t)$ with $q(0)=Q$, obtained by substituting $y(t)$ for $y$ in the same three ambient caps. They cover the full middle plane, and $q'(0)=-\overline L(p)$. If $Q$ is the original global raw maximum and the two ordinary endpoint maxima are strictly below $Q$, the new global raw maximum is at most $q(t)$ for all sufficiently small $t\ge0$. Writing $M(t)=|A_t|+|K|+|B|$,
$$
\left.\frac{d}{dt}\frac{q(t)}{M(t)}\right|_{t=0}
=\frac{-M\overline L(p)+2aQ}{M^2}.
$$
In particular the optimized normalized depth strictly decreases if $\overline L(p)>2aQ/M$.

If the three original caps attain the true depth at $(0,y)$ and every singleton-capture region of the $A$ traces is null, then $\overline L(p)\ge a/2$ for every $p\in A$. The derivative above is then at most $(-Ma/2+2aQ)/M^2$. At a budget ratio $Q/M<2/9$ this last expression is less than $-a/(18M)$.

86934b651b11f7d5:04.reason: The sole positive deficient corner case of the accepted loss theorem gives the displayed estimate at every point of its closure. 86934b651b11f7d5:04.statement: Let A,K,B be planar convex bodies at the only integer bases −1,0,1, with (A+B)/2⊆K. Let y∈int K and let v₁,v₂,v₃ be nonzero spanning normals with sum zero. Let τ₂=Λ−maxλᵢ and suppose only one region Rⱼ of positive area has λⱼ<τ₂. For every p∈closure Rⱼ, L̄(p)≥[2aτ₂−2(τ₂−λⱼ)|Rⱼ|]/Λ≥(a−|Rⱼ|)/2. Thus |Rⱼ|≤a/9 suffices for L̄(p)≥4a/9. If all deficient regions are null every p works. With Q original global, both strict endpoint gaps, and Q/M<2/9 this gives strict normalized descent.

86934b651b11f7d5:05.reason: The two transverse boundary strips give the exact corner derivative. Optimizing the resulting affine lower bound via the support function gives an attained common center.
86934b651b11f7d5:05.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a convex body, let $H_i=\{x:v_i\cdot x\ge b_i\}$ for $1\le i\le3$ cover $A$, and assume the normals are pairwise linearly independent and all cuts are proper. Write $a=|A|$, $U_i=|A\cap H_i|$, $a_i=\mathcal H^1(A\cap\{v_i\cdot x=b_i\})/\lVert v_i\rVert$, and $L_i(p)=2U_i+(b_i-v_i\cdot p)a_i$. For arbitrary positive weights $\lambda_i$ put $\Lambda=\sum_i\lambda_i$, $\tau_2=\Lambda-\max_i\lambda_i$, and $c_i=(\tau_2-\lambda_i)_+$. The region $R_i=A\cap\bigcap_{j\ne i}\{v_j\cdot x<b_j\}$ is the region captured only by $H_i$. For each $i$ with $r_i=|R_i|>0$, set $C_i=\overline{R_i}$ and, for $j\ne i$, let $\ell$ be the third index and put
$$
\tau_{ij}=\frac{\mathcal H^1(A\cap\{v_j\cdot x=b_j,\ v_\ell\cdot x\le b_\ell\})}{\lVert v_j\rVert}.
$$
Then $C_i=A\cap\bigcap_{j\ne i}\{v_j\cdot x\le b_j\}$. For every $p\in A$ and $A_t=p+(1-t)(A-p)$ the exact right loss is
$$
D_i(p)=\lim_{t\downarrow0}\frac{|R_i\setminus A_t|}{t}
=2r_i-\sum_{j\ne i}(b_j-v_j\cdot p)\tau_{ij}\ge0.
$$
It satisfies $D_i(p)\le2r_i$ on $C_i$ and its minimum there is attained and equals
$$
2r_i-\sum_{j\ne i}b_j\tau_{ij}
-h_{C_i}\Bigl(-\sum_{j\ne i}\tau_{ij}v_j\Bigr),
$$
where $h_C$ is the support function of $C$.

With null corners omitted, for every $p\in A$,
$$
\sum_i\lambda_i L_i(p)\ge 2a\tau_2-\sum_i c_iD_i(p).
$$
The right side attains its maximum at one common $p\in A$, with value
$$
2a\tau_2-2\sum_i c_ir_i+\sum_i c_i\sum_{j\ne i}b_j\tau_{ij}
+h_A\Bigl(-\sum_i c_i\sum_{j\ne i}\tau_{ij}v_j\Bigr).
$$
If just one positive-area corner $R_j$ has $c_j>0$, every $p\in C_j$ satisfies $\sum_i\lambda_i L_i(p)\ge 2a\tau_2-2(\tau_2-\lambda_j)r_j$. If all deficient corners are null, $\sum_i\lambda_i L_i(p)\ge2a\tau_2$ for every $p\in A$.

In the actual mixed setting of the critical chord-weight theorem, these one-corner and all-deficient-null estimates imply a normalized loss of at least $(a-r_j)/2$ and $a/2$, respectively, after dividing by $\Lambda$. In particular $r_j\le a/9$ gives a normalized loss of at least $4a/9$ at every $p\in C_j$.

Let $d\ge1$ and $m\ge0$ be integers and put $T_d=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_d)$ and $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Take radii $R=r_0\ge r_1\ge\cdots\ge r_m\ge0$ with $R>0$ and nondecreasing drops $r_{h-1}-r_h$. Let $S$ consist of the fibers $r_h T_d$ at integer bases $-h$ and $h+1$ for $0\le h\le m$ and no other fibers. Then $S$ is the mixed-integer part of a compact convex body with nonempty interior. For the measure $\mu$ given by summing $d$-dimensional volume on these fibers, the point $y=(0,R/(d+1),\ldots,R/(d+1))$ satisfies
$$
\mu(S\cap H)\ge\frac{\Gamma_d}{2}\,\mu(S)
\quad\text{for every closed ambient halfspace }H\ni y.
$$
For $m=0$ the maximum normalized depth over $S$ is exactly $\Gamma_d/2$.

97eab0f821e54041:01.statement:
Let $n\ge0$ and $d\ge1$ be integers. Let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty, with $\operatorname{aff}(P)=\mathbb R^n$, and let $K_p\subset\mathbb R^d$, $p\in P$, be compact convex bodies with nonempty interior. For each $q\in P$, let
$$
E_q=\left\{\lambda\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{P\setminus\{q\}}:\quad
\sum_{p\ne q}\lambda_p=1,\quad \sum_{p\ne q}\lambda_p p=q\right\}.
$$
Call the family strictly compatible if for each extreme point $\lambda$ of each nonempty $E_q$, the Minkowski combination $\sum_{p\ne q}\lambda_p K_p$ is compactly contained in $\operatorname{int}K_q$. Under this condition there is a common $\kappa>0$ such that $\sum_{p\ne q}\lambda_p K_p+\kappa B_d\subseteq K_q$ for every such extreme point, where $B_d$ is the closed unit ball. For any family of convex bodies $K'_p$ with $d_H(K'_p,K_p)<\eta<\kappa/2$ for all $p$, the convex hull of the lifted bodies $\{p\}\times K'_p$ has exactly the prescribed integer fibers $K'_p$ at $p\in P$. In particular the original family is actual.

97eab0f821e54041:02.statement:

Fix $h$ with $u\cdot h>0$. Then $K(t)=\operatorname{conv}(K\cup\{v+th\})$ has added volume $\Delta(t)=|K(t)|-|K|>0$ for $t>0$. The function $\Delta$ is continuous and strictly increasing, with $\Delta(0)=0$, and $\sup_{x\in K(t)\setminus K}\lVert x-v\rVert\to0$ as $t\downarrow0$. In particular each sufficiently small prescribed positive added volume has a unique small positive parameter.

For a finite list of distinct points $v_i$ with these hypotheses and corresponding directions $h_i$, write $a_i=v_i+t_i h_i$. For all sufficiently small positive $t_i$ one has the exact disjoint union
$$
\operatorname{conv}(K\cup\{a_i:i\})\setminus K
=\bigsqcup_i\bigl(\operatorname{conv}(K\cup\{a_i\})\setminus K\bigr).
$$

Choose finitely many distinct $w_i=(p_i,v_i)$, $p_i\in P$, each exposed in $C$ by an ambient linear functional with unique maximizer $w_i$. Assume $v_i$ has a unique unit supporting normal $u_i$ in $K_{p_i}$, whose support face is $\{v_i\}$, and fix $h_i$ with $u_i\cdot h_i>0$. For each fixed real vector $\xi=(\xi_i)$ and every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ there is an actual convex body $C_\varepsilon$ with nonempty integer fibers of positive volume exactly at $P$, converging fiberwise in Hausdorff distance to $C$. The signed measure $\mu_{C_\varepsilon}-\mu_C$ is a sum of signed restrictions of mixed volume to pairwise disjoint regions shrinking to the respective $w_i$, each of exact signed mass $\varepsilon\xi_i$. In particular $M_\varepsilon=M+\varepsilon\sum_i\xi_i$. For every fixed finite family of closed halfspaces $H$ whose boundaries avoid all $w_i$, one has
$$
\mu_{C_\varepsilon}(H)-\mu_C(H)=\varepsilon\sum_i\xi_i\mathbf1_H(w_i)
$$
for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon$. The same identity holds for parallel threshold changes of order $O(\varepsilon)$, comparing the two measures at the same shifted threshold and keeping the old indicators on the right.

$$

\le \frac1M\max_{p\in I}\sum_i\xi_i(A_{pi}-\beta).

If $C$ is a local minimum among all actual positive fiber families over $P$, with the fiberwise Hausdorff topology, there is a probability vector $\pi$ on the selected deepest-base circuits such that $\sum_{p\in I}\pi_p A_{pi}=\beta$ for every selected $i$. a21ff89aef880b49:01.statement:
For integers $k,m\ge1$, let $X_k\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(k,1)$ and $Y_m\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(m,1)$. Let $E_+,E_-$ be unit-mean exponentials, with all four variables independent. For $p\in[0,1]$ and $b=(k+p-1)/m\in[0,1]$, set
$$
V_{k,m,p}=X_k+pE_+-E_--bY_m,\qquad
G_{k,p}=\Pr(X_k+pE_+\ge E_-+k+p-1).
$$
The variance of $V_{k,m,p}$ is $\sigma^2=k+p^2+1+mb^2$ and lies in $[k+1,2(k+1)]$. As $k\to\infty$, the probability $\Pr(V_{k,m,p}\ge0)$ tends to $1/2$ uniformly over the admissible $m,p$. For fixed $k$, if $m_j\to\infty$ and $p_j\to p\in[0,1]$ along admissible parameters, then $\Pr(V_{k,m_j,p_j}\ge0)\to G_{k,p}$.

a46be036ec7c0eb5:01.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and $1\le H\le d$ be integers. Put $t=1/(d+1)$ and $\Gamma=(dt)^d$. At the zero-right-index double knot let
$$
a_H=\frac{H+1}{H(d+1)},\qquad \beta_H=\frac{1}{d(d+1)}.
$$
Write $x_+=\max\{x,0\}$. For each integer $h\ge0$ put $r_h=(1-a_H h)_+$, $q_h=t-\beta_H h$, and $p_h=t+\beta_H(h+1)$. For $r,s>0$ let $E_d(s,r)=d^d s^{d-1}(r-ds)_+$, and let $E_d(s,0)=0$ for every real $s$. The thresholds are positive on positive radii. Define the finite diagonal-envelope deficit and the two normalized sums by
$$
\begin{aligned}
D_d(a_H,\beta_H)&=\Gamma\sum_{h\ge0}r_h^d-\sum_{h\ge0}\bigl[E_d(q_h,r_h)+E_d(p_h,r_h)\bigr],\\
W_{d,H}&=\sum_{j\ge0}(1-a_H j)_+^d,\\
K_{d,H}&=\sum_{j=0}^{H-1}(1-j/d)^{d-1}(1-j/H).
\end{aligned}
$$
The normalized left envelope sum is $K_{d,H}$, the right envelope sum vanishes, and $D_d(a_H,\beta_H)/\Gamma=W_{d,H}-K_{d,H}<1/6$.

a6e6fd61fe60c16a:01.reason: The conditional geometric increments and exact recurrence give the mode comparison with its endpoint strictness.
a6e6fd61fe60c16a:01.statement:
Let $N_i$ be finitely many independent geometric random variables on the nonnegative integers, with means $b_i\ge0$ and at least one $b_i>0$. A zero mean denotes a deterministic zero variable. Write $N=\sum_i N_i$, $\mu=\sum_i b_i$, $b_{\max}=\max_i b_i$, $p(n)=\Pr(N=n)$, $m_i(n)=\mathbb E[N_i\mid N=n]$, and $\tau(n)=\sum_i b_i(m_i(n)+1)$. Then $p(n)>0$ for $n\ge0$, and for every integer $n\ge1$ the increments $m_i(n)-m_i(n-1)$ belong to $[0,1]$ and sum to one. They are positive for each $i$ with $b_i>0$. The recurrence is
$$
\tau(n-1)p(n-1)=[\tau(n)+n-\mu]p(n).
$$
In particular, $p(n)\ge p(n-1)$ for $1\le n\le\mu-b_{\max}$. In this range equality holds exactly when $n=\mu-b_{\max}$ and all the positive means are equal.

a6e6fd61fe60c16a:02.reason: Tilting the negative phases gives a sum of independent geometric counts. The mode comparison supplies the derivative sign and the exact equality case.
a6e6fd61fe60c16a:02.statement: Let $k\ge2$ be an integer, let $X$ have the $\operatorname{Gamma}(k,1)$ law, and let $Y=\sum_i b_iE_i$ for finitely many unit-mean exponentials $E_i$, independent of each other and of $X$. Assume $0\le b_i\le1$ and $\sum_i b_i\ge k$. The continuous convolution density $f$ of $X-Y$ is differentiable at zero and satisfies $f'(0)\le0$. Equality holds exactly when $k$ of the $b_i$ equal one and all others equal zero.

a6e6fd61fe60c16a:03.reason: A signed size-biased derivative and the augmented gamma-density sign make every nontrivial capped residual equalization strictly decrease the probability.
a6e6fd61fe60c16a:03.statement:
Let $k\ge2$ and $q\ge k-1$ be integers. For $b=(b_1,\ldots,b_q)\in[0,1]^q$ with $\sum_i b_i=k-1$, let
$$
P_k(b)=\Pr\!\left(X\ge E_0+\sum_{i=1}^q b_iE_i\right),
$$
where $X$ has the $\operatorname{Gamma}(k,1)$ law and $E_0,\ldots,E_q$ are unit-mean exponentials, with all variables independent. Set $\bar b=(k-1)/q$. Transferring a positive amount from an above-average coefficient to a below-average one, up to the first point at which either reaches $\bar b$, strictly decreases $P_k$. Consequently
$$
P_k(b)\ge \Pr(X\ge E_0+\bar b\,G),
$$
where $G$ is an independent $\operatorname{Gamma}(q,1)$ variable. Equality holds exactly when every $b_i=\bar b$.

a6e6fd61fe60c16a:04.reason: Zero padding and strict finite-count equalization give decreasing exact minima. The equalized gamma average converges to its deterministic mean, giving the stated exponential polynomial limit.
a6e6fd61fe60c16a:04.statement:
Let $k\ge1$ be an integer. Consider the laws
$$
P_k(b)=\Pr\!\left(X\ge E_0+\sum_{i=1}^q b_iE_i\right),
\qquad 0\le b_i\le1,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^q b_i=k-1,
$$
where $X$ has the $\operatorname{Gamma}(k,1)$ law and $E_0,\ldots,E_q$ are unit-mean exponentials, with all variables independent. Here $q$ ranges over the finite nonnegative integers for which the coefficient constraints are feasible. For $k\ge2$, the fixed-$q$ minimum is
$$
A_{k,q}=\Pr\!\left(X\ge E_0+\frac{k-1}{q}\,G\right),
\qquad G\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(q,1)
$$
with $G$ independent. These minima strictly decrease as $q$ increases and converge to
$$
G_k=\Pr(X\ge E_0+k-1)
=e^{-(k-1)}\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\frac{(k-1)^j}{j!}\left(1-2^{-(k-j)}\right).
$$
Thus the infimum over all finite $q$ and all feasible $b$ is $G_k$, and $P_k(b)>G_k$ for every such $b$ when $k\ge2$. In particular $G_2=5/(4e)$ and $G_3=27/(8e^2)$. When $k=1$ every residual coefficient is zero, and $P_1(b)=G_1=1/2$, including the empty list.

ace4ff0d14f43769:4.statement:
Let $m,s\ge1$ be integers, let $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, and let $K\subset\mathbb R^s$ be a full-dimensional simplex of volume $V$ and centroid $c$. Put $\gamma_s=(s/(s+1))^s$, $Q_m=\{p\in\mathbb R^m:\sum_i |p_i|\le1\}$, $g(p)=(1+\sum_i p_i)/2$, and

C=\{(p,u,x)\in\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^s:
p\in Q_m,\ |u-g(p)|\le\varepsilon,\ x\in K\}.
$$
The body $C$ is full-dimensional. The coarse rule requires $p\in\mathbb Z^m$, with admissible set $S_{\mathrm c}=C\cap(\mathbb Z^m\times\mathbb R^{1+s})$ and measure $\mathcal H_{s+1}|_{S_{\mathrm c}}$. The fine rule additionally requires $u\in\mathbb Z$, with admissible set $S_{\mathrm f}=C\cap(\mathbb Z^{m+1}\times\mathbb R^s)$ and measure $\mathcal H_s|_{S_{\mathrm f}}$. For each rule normalize its measure by its own total mass. Define its maximum depth as the maximum over its admissible set of the infimum of normalized mass of all closed ambient halfspaces containing the point.

The coarse rule has $2m+1$ fibers of mass $2\varepsilon V$ and maximum depth $D_{\mathrm c}=\gamma_s$, attained at $(0,1/2,c)$. The fine rule has exactly $2m$ fibers of mass $V$, at $(e_i,1)$ and $(-e_i,0)$ for $1\le i\le m$, and maximum depth $D_{\mathrm f}=\gamma_s/(2m)$, attained at the centroid of each fiber. The ambient normalized laws are mutually singular. After projection to $(p,x)$, their total variation distance, defined by the supremum over measurable sets, is exactly $1/(2m+1)$, the coarse probability of the omitted base $p=0$.

The affine span of the fine bases has dimension $m$. Its integer points project bijectively to the odd-sum coset of the index-two even-sum sublattice of $\mathbb Z^m$. The fine mixed hull is $\operatorname{conv}(S_{\mathrm f})=\{(p,g(p),x):p\in Q_m,\ x\in K\}$ and has codimension one in $C$. Replacing $C$ by this hull preserves the fine set and fine measure and reduces the original coarse $\mathcal H_{s+1}$ mass to zero.

Thus for fixed $s$ and $\varepsilon$, a single added integer condition of projected index two gives $D_{\mathrm f}/D_{\mathrm c}=1/(2m)\to0$ with projected total variation tending to zero. In particular there is no positive dimension-independent retention factor for this comparison, even when the omitted coarse base marginal mass is arbitrarily small.

af36a5fc25ebff84:02.statement:
Let $n,d\ge1$ and let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body. Fix a full-dimensional compact convex body $K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ with volume centroid zero and volume $V>0$. Suppose that the actual fiber at $j\in\mathbb Z^n$ is $C_j=c_j+r_jK$ with $r_j>0$. Select any finite family of pairs $(p_\ell,q_\ell)$ with $p_\ell+q_\ell=2j$, $p_\ell\ne q_\ell$, and all endpoint bases distinct. At each selected endpoint $i$ suppose the actual fiber is $C_i=c_i+r_iK$ with $r_i>0$.

Write $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ and $c_d=(2\Gamma_d)^{1/d}$. For $0<r\le s$ put
$$
\Phi_d(r,s)=
\begin{cases}
r,&d=1,\\
\left[r c_d+\dfrac{s-r}{d-1}(1-c_d)\right]^d,&d\ge2,\ r\le s\le dr,\\
r^d,&d\ge2,\ s\ge dr,
\end{cases}
$$
and extend $\Phi_d$ symmetrically to $r>s$. The branches agree at $s=dr$.

For each pair write
$$
\rho_\ell=\frac{r_{p_\ell}+r_{q_\ell}}2,\qquad
m_\ell=\frac{c_{p_\ell}+c_{q_\ell}}2,\qquad
\delta_\ell=r_j-\rho_\ell,\qquad
\theta_\ell=\frac{\gamma_K(c_j-m_\ell)}{\rho_\ell},
$$
where $\gamma_K(x)=\inf\{t\ge0:x\in tK\}$ is the Minkowski gauge. Then $\delta_\ell\ge0$, and the compatibility inclusion $m_\ell+\rho_\ell K\subseteq C_j$ is equivalent to $m_\ell-c_j\in\delta_\ell K$. In particular $\theta_\ell\le d\delta_\ell/\rho_\ell$.

Write $H_i=\{x:(i,x)\in H\}$ for a closed ambient halfspace $H$ containing $(j,c_j)$, and $t_+=\max\{t,0\}$. For each selected pair,
$$
|C_{p_\ell}\cap H_{p_\ell}|+|C_{q_\ell}\cap H_{q_\ell}|
\ge V(1-\theta_\ell)_+^d\Phi_d(r_{p_\ell},r_{q_\ell})
\ge V(1-d\delta_\ell/\rho_\ell)_+^d\Phi_d(r_{p_\ell},r_{q_\ell}).
$$
Writing $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$, the raw depth obeys
$$
h_S((j,c_j))\ge V\left[\Gamma_d r_j^d+
\sum_\ell (1-\theta_\ell)_+^d\Phi_d(r_{p_\ell},r_{q_\ell})\right].
$$
The same inequality holds with each factor replaced by the conservative one above. For a pair with $a=\rho_\ell^dV$ and $b=r_j^dV$, that conservative factor equals $[(d+1)-d(b/a)^{1/d}]_+^d$, positive exactly when $a>\Gamma_d b$. To obtain the corresponding normalized bounds, divide by the full mixed volume $\mathcal H_d(S)$.

Its middle centroid is $(0,-\delta v)$, with $\gamma_K(-\delta v)=d\delta$, where $\gamma_K$ is the Minkowski gauge.

At $\delta=\rho/d$ a closed halfspace through this centroid captures zero endpoint volume. Hence no constant $D<d$ can replace $d$ in a universal endpoint-volume lower bound of the form $(1-D\delta/\rho)_+^d$ times a positive equal-pair budget, with $(t)_+=\max\{t,0\}$. More generally, for $0\le\delta\le\rho/d$ there is a through-point cap of total endpoint volume $\rho^dV[1-(1-2a)^d]$, where $a=(1-d\delta/\rho)/(d+1)$.
