b84198b3fe4ca80c:01.statement: For compact convex C⊂R^n×R^d, d≥1, real-base fibers K_z on P=proj C, r(z)=|K_z|^(1/d), and affine L(z,x)=a·z+u·x−b with u≠0, define U(z,0)=max_{x∈K_z}L(z,x) and U(z,t)=sup{s:|K_z∩{L(z,·)≥s}|≥t^d} when 0<t≤r(z). The domain {z∈P,0≤t≤r(z)} is convex; U is finite bounded upper semicontinuous and jointly concave. For fixed H={L≥0}, its cap roots c(z) are concave on proj(C∩H) when nonempty, including nonempty null caps.

external_dependencies: One-dimensional survival quantile transformation for a continuous strictly monotone distribution, §2 (1), proved by substitution.
b84198b3fe4ca80c:02.reason: For positive fibers the affine projection law is nonatomic and strictly increasing on its support; the survival-quantile substitution gives the first moment. Closed nonvertical boundaries are null. A zero-volume fiber has root zero and contributes zero to every sum, even if geometrically nonempty. The mixed centroid's discrete weights are the full r(z)^d, not the sectional weights of the stationarity law.
b84198b3fe4ca80c:02.statement: Under §1, for every positive fiber ∫_{K_z}L(z,x)dx=d∫_0^{r(z)}t^(d−1)U(z,t)dt. The actual mixed cap mass of {L≥0} is Σ_{z∈Z^n}c_z^d for c_z=|K_z∩{L≥0}|^(1/d); on positive fibers a proper cap has the unique root U(z,c_z)=0, and the support extrema decide empty/full mass cases. If the actual mixed centroid is (j,y), j integral, L(j,y)=0 and M=Σ_z r(z)^d>0, then Σ_z(z−j)r(z)^d=0 and Σ_z d∫_0^{r(z)}t^(d−1)U(z,t)dt=0.

external_dependencies: Ordinary coarea on the positive fibers and implicit differentiation of the strictly monotone inverse, §3.
b84198b3fe4ca80c:03.reason: Implicit differentiation of the proper cap root and coarea give the same gradient. Proper sections of positive compact convex fibers have positive continuous section area, whereas strict empty or full fibers are locally constant. The accepted general cap derivative has overlapping proper-section terms but its theorem assumes an ambient-interior depth region and imposes further projected-contact hypotheses for its certificate. Here true centroid weights and stationary section weights are independent; no convex-order conclusion or universal equality of β_z is asserted.
b84198b3fe4ca80c:03.statement: For the same C,L and H_v={L(z,x)+v·(z−j)≥0} through a fixed point (j,y), U_v(z,t)=U(z,t)+v·(z−j). At a parameter with no endpoint contacts on positive fibers and differentiable inverse at every proper cap root c_z, put β_z=−∂_t U_v(z,c_z)>0. Then the tilt gradient of the mixed cap mass equals Σ_{proper z}(z−j)α_z, where α_z=d c_z^(d−1)/β_z=H_(d−1)(K_z∩∂H_v)/|u|. It vanishes at a differentiable tilt minimum. If d=1 and the continuous axis is oriented and scaled in the functional so u=1, all proper fibers have α_z=1.

b85e6bd6eff40d13:01.reason: The full actual middle face grows. Only vertices in the apex seed’s exposed B face can escape old K, by strict slack at all other facets. Proper cut continuity gives the same reciprocal slopes at the moving mark, and the positive menu derivative handles the unchanged B tie. The related accepted result covers contraction of A alone, not this coupled growth; 6e9992972c414d73 §§1–4 supplies the checked analogous implicit argument, which is also stated here.
b85e6bd6eff40d13:01.statement: Let A,K,B be compatible planar polygons at −1,0,1. Three spanning balanced normals give equal-budget Q caps through y∈int K with proper A,K cuts and supporting B thresholds h_B(v_i), and weights p_i normalized from 1/(2σ_Ai+σ_Ki). Let r=Q/M and W_A,W_K be the same normalized weighted cap indicators. If an outward unit normal n has h_A(n)+h_B(n)=2h_K(n), with F_A an edge and F_B an edge or point, choose p∈relint F_A and J=(p+F_B)/2. For small ε>0, A_ε=conv(A,p+εn) adds exactly the triangle over F_A, and K_ε=conv(K,(A_ε+B)/2)=conv(K,J+εn/2) adds the trapezoid with base F_K and top J+εn/2. With lengths L_A,L_K,L_B, M'=L_A/2+L_K/4+L_B/8. The moving common budget has derivative q'=∫_(F_A)T_pW_A+(1/2)∫_(F_K)H_JW_K with unit tent T_p and unit trapezoid H_J, and q'−rM'=∫_(F_A)T_p(W_A−r)+(1/2)∫_(F_K)H_J(W_K−r). If Q is global and m_A<Q, negative cost gives strict normalized descent, even when the unchanged B endpoint ties Q.

b85e6bd6eff40d13:02.reason: Use actual A and B row pairings: for a paired midpoint, capture by the ith middle cap implies capture of its A point by the same ith A cap. Both costs use the same p_i. Area scaling is 1/4, the paired plateau adds the L_B term, and the full middle growth outside the inner profile contributes at most (1−r)Δ/4.
b85e6bd6eff40d13:02.statement: In the actual full-profile enlargement above let Δ=L_K−(L_A+L_B)/2≥0 and C_A=∫_(F_A)T_p(W_A−r). If p lies on none of the three A cutting lines, the actual coupled cost obeys C_coupled≤(5/4)C_A+(L_B/4)(W_A(p)−r)+(1−r)Δ/4. In particular Δ=0, C_A<0 and W_A(p)<r imply negative cost. When Δ=0 and F_B is a point, C_A<0 alone implies negative cost without strict apex signature.

b85e6bd6eff40d13:03.reason: Actual old midpoint vertices and the new apex seed satisfy the signed planes, and the corners give O(ε²) errors for polygons. In the tied case use max(Q,q_ε) before dividing by M_ε, giving the coefficient max(q_s',0)−rD_s. The optimum mass apex and the cost apex must be the same; the mass supremum can be unattained with one-sided excess.
b85e6bd6eff40d13:03.statement: In the same polygon setup, let F_K=[a,b], I_0=(F_A+F_B)/2=[a_0,b_0], and J=[c,d] in the unit tangential coordinate. Retain all other K facets and replace the old face by t≤(ε/2)G(s), G(s)=min{1,(s−a_0)/(c−a_0),(b_0−s)/(b_0−d)}. This is an actual compatible polygon path with middle signed displacement coefficient G/2, common-menu normalized cost numerator C_s=C_A+(1/2)∫_(F_K)G(W_K−r), and total mass derivative D_s=5L_A/8+L_B/4−ell_L²/(2d_L)−ell_R²/(2d_R), where ell_L=a_0−a, ell_R=b−b_0 and d_L,d_R are apex distances to A face endpoints. The supremum over the relative interior of F_A of D_s is 5L_A/8+L_B/4−(ell_L+ell_R)²/(2L_A). If Q is global and both endpoint maxima have strict gaps, C_s<0 gives descent. If m_A<Q and unchanged m_B=Q, strict first-order negativity of this upper certificate is equivalent to D_s>0 and C_s<0.

b85e6bd6eff40d13:04.reason: A negative displacement contributes nonpositively wherever the actual load is at least r; the inside part has the same row comparison as §4. ba445d671279810a applies to the same critical cap weights and gives the pair lower load 1/4. Mere excess length does not imply the required signatures.
b85e6bd6eff40d13:04.statement: For the signed roof of §§5–6, if the same apex has C_A<0 and strict signature W_A(p)<r and the actual outer portions of F_K outside I_0 satisfy W_K≥r almost everywhere, then C_s≤(5/4)C_A+(L_B/4)(W_A(p)−r)<0. For genuine critical caps with r<2/9, pair capture almost everywhere on those outer portions is sufficient for the W_K hypothesis. Both endpoint gaps give descent, and a tied B endpoint additionally needs D_s>0 for this certificate.

external_dependencies: Real Stone–Weierstrass theorem for the coordinate-polynomial algebra on a compact sphere
b90a2673d60a00b3:01.reason: Test against odd Gaussian Hermite moments of v·G. Conditional Gaussian expectation gives (v·θ)^(2k+1) times H_(2k+1)(θ·G), with multiplier c_(2k+1)=2φ(0)(−1)^k(2k−1)!!≠0. Hence all odd polynomial moments vanish, and density of polynomial restrictions gives evenness. This applies also to singular angular measures and N=1.
b90a2673d60a00b3:01.statement: Let σ be a finite signed Borel measure on S^(N−1), N≥1, with ∫sign(u·θ)dσ(θ)=0 for almost every normal u with respect to spherical measure. Then σ is invariant under θ↦−θ. Values assigned on equators do not affect the almost-everywhere statement.

b90a2673d60a00b3:02.reason: Fubini over Gaussian normals makes almost every through-y plane μ-null. The two opposite caps have equal mass for those normals, so the odd-transform lemma gives angular evenness. The converse uses every closed hemisphere, including those with charged boundaries. Neither bounded support nor fiber geometry is used in this step.
b90a2673d60a00b3:02.statement: For a finite nonzero Borel measure μ on R^N with μ({y})=0, every closed halfspace containing y has mass at least μ(total)/2 if and only if its angular pushforward about y is antipodally invariant. Under these equivalent conditions the normalized depth is exactly 1/2.

external_dependencies: Polar integration in the q-dimensional Euclidean own-fiber affine span
b90a2673d60a00b3:03.reason: Primitive integer rays split disjoint angular strata. Convexity from y makes (K_(j+kv)−c)/k and (c−K_(j−kv))/k nested. Equal angular laws pull back to equal weighted sums of H_q restrictions with weights k^q. Positive sets first force a common affine q-plane, then strictly increasing prefix sums recover each positive scaled body exactly. Polar integration recovers the own fiber. The marked point is an actual mixed point and the centroid conclusion concerns the full physical law. The escort identity of 08b344179e054c1c instead concerns maximal finite energy at the weighted base mean, and does not give half-depth rigidity. The accepted equal-endpoint actual-centroid depth bound is under a different hypothesis and does not characterize equality at one half.
b90a2673d60a00b3:03.statement: Let C⊂R^n×R^d be compact convex, S=C∩(Z^n×R^d), q=dim_H S>0 and μ=H_q|S of total M>0. At any actual y=(j,c)∈S the following are equivalent: normalized closed ambient halfspace depth at least 1/2, antipodal symmetry of the angular law about y, central symmetry of μ about y, and H_q(S∩(2y−S))=M. Every positive-volume opposite fiber pair reflects exactly, the own fiber is positive and centrally symmetric, y is the true full ambient centroid, and depth is exactly 1/2. Fibers of zero H_q measure need not reflect.

b90a2673d60a00b3:04.reason: The left closed ray at 1 has mass two, the right has mass three, and any containing ray captures at least two. The atom at the center is present in both rays.
b90a2673d60a00b3:04.statement: The half-depth equivalence can fail for q=0: on S=[0,3]∩Z with counting measure, y=1 has normalized closed-halfspace depth 1/2, while reflection about 1 fails to preserve the law.

b90a2673d60a00b3:05.reason: If E lacks ambient interior, its base affine span A is proper: a full base projection puts j in the interior of π(C), which forces q=d, and the positive own d-fiber then forces E to be full-dimensional. Take a small interior ball of C with base projection strictly to one side of a hyperplane through A and closer to A than every integer base of C outside A. The convex hull with E changes no integer fiber. This preserves the entire mixed trace, not only positive fibers.
b90a2673d60a00b3:05.statement: Let C⊂R^n×R^d be an ambient convex body with q=dim_H(C∩(Z^n×R^d))>0. At actual y=(j,c), set E=C∩(2y−C) and assume R=H_q(E∩(Z^n×R^d))>0. There is an ambient convex body D⊂C with D∩(Z^n×R^d)=E∩(Z^n×R^d) exactly. Its intrinsic mixed mass is R, its true centroid is y, and its local normalized closed-halfspace depth at y is 1/2.

b90a2673d60a00b3:06.reason: Apply the exact thickening to the intersection for one direction. For the other, positive H_q mass fixes D's intrinsic fiber dimension q and the rigidity theorem makes its law centrally symmetric about the actual centroid, so the mass is contained up to null sets in the original reflection intersection. This equivalence does not supply a positive universal retention threshold.
b90a2673d60a00b3:06.statement: Under the ambient-body hypotheses of §7, for every 0<t≤M, some actual mixed point has reflection retention H_q(S∩(2y−S))≥t if and only if some ambient convex body D⊂C has H_q mixed mass at least t and has a true integer-base centroid of local normalized depth at least 1/2. For d=1 with q>0 this is the local Γ_1 condition; for d>1 it asks for the stronger local half-depth condition.

b989614dc4f86228:01.reason: Affine evaluations on the finite threshold indices can be fixed while retaining the signs on the diverging indices. This realizes all limiting bounded traces by one actual finite cap.
b989614dc4f86228:01.statement: Fix $n,d\ge1$, finite nonempty $P\subset\mathbb R^n$, and a ball $R B_d$ centered at zero with $R>0$. Let $H_j=\{(z,x):u_j\cdot x\ge t_j(z)\}$, where $\|u_j\|=1$ and $t_j$ is real affine. Some subsequence has $u_j\to u$ with $\|u\|=1$ and $t_j(z)\to t(z)\in[-\infty,\infty]$ for every $z\in P$. On $P\times R B_d$, the limiting traces $\{x:u\cdot x\ge t(z)\}$ at finite thresholds, the full traces at $t(z)=-\infty$ and the empty traces at $t(z)=+\infty$ are realized by one actual closed halfspace with unit continuous normal $u$ and a finite affine threshold. For summed $d$-volume $\mu$ on any fixed family of measurable fibers inside that ball, $\mu(H_j)$ along the subsequence tends to the mass of that halfspace. Every fixed point of $P\times R B_d$ contained in infinitely many caps of the subsequence belongs to the realizing halfspace.

external_dependencies: Averkov–Weismantel mixed-integer Helly theorem, Theorem 1.1(3).
b989614dc4f86228:02.reason: Strict threshold relaxation gives a finite interior cover. The mixed-integer Helly number reduces its size, and threshold compactification gives the exact closed cover including the boundary.
b989614dc4f86228:02.statement:
Fix $n,d\ge 1$, a finite nonempty $P\subset\mathbb R^n$, and nonempty compact convex sets $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ for $z\in P$. Write $S=\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$, $\mu=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes(\mathcal L^d|_{K_z})$, and $M=\mu(S)$. Let $h_\mu(z,x)$ be the infimum of $\mu(H)$ over closed ambient halfspaces $H$ containing $(z,x)$. Assume $M>0$ and put $Q=\max_{(z,x)\in S}h_\mu(z,x)$. Suppose for every $\varepsilon>0$ the interiors of at most $N$ nonvertical closed ambient halfspaces cover $S$, each of mass less than $Q+\varepsilon M$. Then $S$ is covered by at most $N$ nonvertical closed ambient halfspaces of mass at most $Q$, with at least one of mass $Q$.

If $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$ for a compact convex set $C\subset\mathbb R^{n+d}$, the hypothesis holds with $N=2^n(d+1)$. The conclusion at this cardinality covers $S$.

b989614dc4f86228:03.reason: Use the bounded-cover part of the accepted variational theorem. For each fiber the common missed region is open convex and disjoint from the old fiber, so its separating support constraint with the same cap budgets forces the stated volume maximality.
b989614dc4f86228:03.statement: Given a finite fixed ambient cap cover of a compatible convex fiber family, each fiber K_z disjoint from the open common missed region Q_z admits one closed supporting halfspace E_z containing K_z and disjoint from Q_z, unless Q_z is empty. For an attained depth minimizer S_* over its fixed actual projection P, with mass M_* and value β, the exact caps of §§1–2 and the E_z constraints make S_* an attained global volume maximizer among all compatible fibers on P obeying |S'∩H_j|≤βM_* and K'_z⊆E_z where imposed.

b989614dc4f86228:04.reason: An interior point of a positive-volume fiber contributes positive own-ball depth. At other points a compatible supporting cap has zero mass, and convexification of the positive lifts preserves all positive slices.
b989614dc4f86228:04.statement:
Fix $n,d\ge 1$, a finite nonempty $P\subset\mathbb R^n$, and nonempty compact convex sets $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ for $z\in P$. Write $S=\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$, $\mu=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes(\mathcal L^d|_{K_z})$, and $M=\mu(S)$. Let $h_\mu(z,x)$ be the infimum of $\mu(H)$ over closed ambient halfspaces $H$ containing $(z,x)$.

The family is compatible if the fiber of $C=\operatorname{conv}(S)$ at every $z\in P$ is exactly $K_z$. Equivalently, whenever a convex combination of bases in $P$ equals a base $z\in P$, the same Minkowski combination of the corresponding fibers lies in $K_z$. For a lattice application require $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$, so $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$.

Assume compatibility and $M>0$. A point $(z,x)\in S$ has positive depth if and only if $x\in\operatorname{int}K_z$. If $\mathcal L^d(K_z)=0$, every site of $P$ on the minimal face of $\operatorname{conv}(P)$ containing $z$ also has zero fiber volume.

Put $P_+=\{z\in P:\mathcal L^d(K_z)>0\}$ and let $C_+$ be the convex hull of the lifted fibers over $P_+$. The fibers of $C_+$ at the sites in $P_+$ are the original $K_z$, and the bases of $C_+$ in $P$ are exactly $P_+$. Deleting the null fibers therefore preserves $\mu$ and the maximum depth over the remaining mixed set. If $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$, then $P_+=\operatorname{conv}(P_+)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ and $C_+\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$ consists exactly of these retained fibers.

b989614dc4f86228:05.reason: The anchored version of threshold compactification attains the infimum. Coupled limit thresholds prove continuity, and finite tilt approximation includes the pure-base comparison.
b989614dc4f86228:05.statement:
Fix $n,d\ge 1$, a finite nonempty $P\subset\mathbb R^n$, and nonempty compact convex sets $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ for $z\in P$. Write $S=\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$, $\mu=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes(\mathcal L^d|_{K_z})$, and $M=\mu(S)$. Let $h_\mu(z,x)$ be the infimum of $\mu(H)$ over closed ambient halfspaces $H$ containing $(z,x)$. For each $z\in P$ and $(u,t)\in\mathbb S^{d-1}\times\mathbb R$ define
$$
c_z(u,t)=\inf_{a\in\mathbb R^n}\mu\{(w,y):a\cdot(w-z)+u\cdot y\ge t\}.
$$
The infimum is attained by a finite $a$, and $c_z$ is continuous on its entire parameter space. For every $x\in K_z$,
$$
h_\mu(z,x)=\min_{\|u\|=1}c_z(u,u\cdot x).
$$
In particular, the depth is continuous on each fiber, is attained by a nonvertical closed halfspace through the point, and attains its maximum over $S$.

b989614dc4f86228:06.reason: The active normalized continuous normals must balance because a separating motion increases every near-active own cap uniformly. A finite positive balance gives the exact whole-plane cover, and null sites are handled by two zero-mass caps.
b989614dc4f86228:06.statement:
Fix $n,d\ge 1$, a finite nonempty $P\subset\mathbb R^n$, and nonempty compact convex sets $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ for $z\in P$. Write $S=\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$, $\mu=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes(\mathcal L^d|_{K_z})$, and $M=\mu(S)$. Let $h_\mu(z,x)$ be the infimum of $\mu(H)$ over closed ambient halfspaces $H$ containing $(z,x)$.

The family is compatible if the fiber of $C=\operatorname{conv}(S)$ at every $z\in P$ is exactly $K_z$. Equivalently, whenever a convex combination of bases in $P$ equals a base $z\in P$, the same Minkowski combination of the corresponding fibers lies in $K_z$. For a lattice application require $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$, so $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$.

Assume compatibility and $M>0$. Put $q_z=\max_{x\in K_z}h_\mu(z,x)$ and $Q=\max_{z\in P}q_z$. At any maximizing mark $x_z$ of a positive-volume fiber $K_z$, the active unit continuous normals
$$
U_z=\{u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}:c_z(u,u\cdot x_z)=q_z\}
$$
have zero in their convex hull, where $c_z(u,t)=\inf_a\mu\{(w,y):a\cdot(w-z)+u\cdot y\ge t\}$. There are $2\le k\le d+1$ actual nonvertical closed caps of mass exactly $q_z$ through $(z,x_z)$ whose unit continuous normals form a minimal positive dependence. The caps cover the whole plane $\{z\}\times\mathbb R^d$. At a null site two actual nonvertical zero-mass caps cover its whole plane. In particular at most $|P|(d+1)$ such caps cover $P\times\mathbb R^d$, each of mass at most $Q$. Caps selected at a site with $q_z<Q$ have strict slack at the common budget $Q$.

b989614dc4f86228:07.reason: At an attained fixed-projection minimum, the chosen exact cap budgets remain a cover for competing bodies. The bounded cover uses explicit support constraints and the whole-plane version needs only the cap budgets.
b989614dc4f86228:07.statement:
Fix $n,d\ge1$ and a finite nonempty lattice-convex projection $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$. Consider compatible families of nonempty compact convex fibers over exactly $P$, with positive total mixed $d$-volume. Compatibility means that the convex hull of the lifted fibers has the specified fiber at every site of $P$. For a family $S$, write $\mu_S$ for summed $d$-volume on its fibers, $M(S)=\mu_S(S)$, and $h_{\mu_S}$ for raw closed-halfspace depth. Suppose $S_*$ attains the minimum of $\max_{y\in S}h_{\mu_S}(y)/M(S)$ in this fixed-$P$ class, with value $\beta$ and total mass $M_*>0$.

There are two fixed-cap volume formulations of this attained minimum.

1. For any finite nonvertical closed cap cover $(H_j)$ of $S_*$ with $\mu_{S_*}(H_j)\le\beta M_*$, at each $z\in P$ whose plane is not entirely covered there is one closed supporting halfspace $E_z$ containing $K_{*,z}$, entirely covered by the cap traces at $z$. Then $S_*$ globally maximizes $M(S')$ over compatible families $S'$ on $P$ with $K'_z\subset E_z$ where imposed and $\mu_{S'}(H_j)\le\beta M_*$ for each $j$. In particular such a cover can be chosen with at most $2^n(d+1)$ caps.
2. There is a fixed cover by at most $|P|(d+1)$ nonvertical closed caps such that $S_*$ globally maximizes $M(S')$ subject solely to the budgets $\mu_{S'}(H_j)\le\beta M_*$ in the same class. In each formulation, the tight budget inequalities at $S_*$ are exactly those with cap mass $\beta M_*$.

external_dependencies: Ordinary Brunn–Minkowski inequality in dimension d−1 on the positive interior sections.
b9b0fda52c8adffe:01.reason: Equal-height Minkowski sums give exact sections. Sectional BM yields the expansion and in d=2 interval addition is exact. The actual midpoint of the captured D and supporting F is in the middle trace, though F’s d-volume is zero. Each T facet has length/||v_i||=3. This value requires a full supporting facet; a smaller B needs its actual facet length. A supporting face is retained as a set throughout.
b9b0fda52c8adffe:01.statement: Let D be a d-dimensional convex body, d≥2, and let F be a compact convex set in a hyperplane normal to unit e with positive (d−1)-volume f. Translate F to height zero, put m=d−1 and let h be D’s e-width. Then (D+F)_t=D_t+F and |D+F|≥∫( |D_t|^(1/m)+f^(1/m) )^m dt≥|D|+fh, where the integral runs over the open height interval. The first lower bound equals |D|+fh+Σ_{j=1}^{m−1} binom(m,j)f^(j/m)∫|D_t|^((m−j)/m)dt, and |D+F|=|D|+fh for d=2. If (A+B)/2⊂K, D=A∩{u·x≥a_0} is proper and positive, B⊂{u·x≤b_0}, and F=B∩{u·x=b_0} is such a facet, then q=|K∩{u·x≥(a_0+b_0)/2}|≥2^(−d)(U+f(h_A(u)−a_0)/||u||), U=|D|. If an actual through-middle cap with those thresholds has mass Q=U+q, then 2^dQ≥(2^d+1)U+f(h_A(u)−a_0)/||u||. In d=2 for B=T={x≤1,y≤1,−x−y≤1} and caps v_i·x≥z with v_1=(1,0), v_2=(0,1), v_3=(−1,−1), the common mass satisfies 4Q≥5U_i+3(h_A(v_i)+1) for every proper A cut.

b9b0fda52c8adffe:02.reason: The polygon Minkowski area polynomial has first variation Σ_F length(F)h_A(n_F)=3Σ_j h_A(v_j), by a strip at each T facet after translating A to contain zero. Inscribed polygon approximation extends to A. The residual midpoint remains on the complementary middle side; the boundary line is area-null. 2021348e0b2d8c9f uses the general quadratic mixed-area polynomial in a different same-base reweighting. Its statement does not supply this explicit triangle first variation.
b9b0fda52c8adffe:02.statement: For T={x≤1,y≤1,−x−y≤1}, b=9/2, and v_1=(1,0), v_2=(0,1), v_3=(−1,−1), every planar convex body A satisfies |(A+T)/2|=(|A|+b+3Σ_j h_A(v_j))/4. Consequently this lower-bounds k=|K| when (A+T)/2⊂K. If R_i=A∩{v_i·x≤−1} has positive area and q_i=|K∩{v_i·x≥0}|, then k−q_i≥(|R_i|+b+3Σ_j h_{R_i}(v_j))/4.

bbd9056fa863fc6b:01.statement:
Let $1/2\le\theta<1$, $0\le b\le1-\theta$, $a\ge0$, and let $m\ge0$ be an integer with $am\le1$. For $0\le h\le m$ put
$$
\rho_h=1-ah,\qquad L_h=1-\frac{a(1-b)h}{\theta},\qquad B_h=1-\frac{ab}{\theta}-\frac{a(1+b)h}{\theta}.
$$
For every $x\in(0,1]$ the combined lists $(L_h)$ and $(B_h)$ have at least as many entries at least $x$ as $(\rho_h)$, counting multiplicities. Hence for every real $p>0$,
$$
\sum_{h=0}^m\big[(L_h)_+^p+(B_h)_+^p\big]\ \ge\ \sum_{h=0}^m\rho_h^p ,
\qquad v_+=\max(v,0).
$$
For $m=0$, equality in the power sum holds exactly when $ab\ge\theta$. For $m\ge1$, equality holds exactly when $m=1$, $a=1$ and $b=\theta=1/2$.

bd3988521f16dd20:1.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with $0\in\operatorname{int}K$, and let $u_1,\ldots,u_m$ be unit vectors. Write $H_i=\{x:u_i\cdot x\ge0\}$, $V=|K|$, and $\Phi(K)=\sum_i\theta_i|K\cap H_i|/V$ for weights $\theta_i>0$ with $\sum_i\theta_i=1$. Let $h$ be the support function of $K$ on the unit sphere. Take a nonzero $C^2$ function $\psi\ge0$ on the sphere such that on an open neighborhood of $\operatorname{supp}\psi$, $h$ is $C^2$ and $A_h=\nabla_S^2 h+hI$ is positive definite on each spherical tangent space. Suppose the support points $X(n)=h(n)n+\nabla_S h(n)$ for $n\in\operatorname{supp}\psi$ satisfy $s_i u_i\cdot X(n)>0$ for fixed signs $s_i\in\{-1,1\}$ and every $i$.

For all sufficiently small signed $t$, $h_t=h+t\psi$ is the support function of a convex body $K_t$ with $0\in\operatorname{int}K_t$. The changed radial intervals are in $\{x:s_i u_i\cdot x>0\text{ for all }i\}$ and stay uniformly away from the cutting planes. In particular $K_t\cap u_i^\perp=K\cap u_i^\perp$ for all $i$. Set $V_t=|K_t|$, $\Delta V(t)=V_t-V$, $e_i=\mathbf1_{\{s_i=1\}}$, and $W=\sum_i\theta_i e_i$. Then
$$
|K_t\cap H_i|-|K\cap H_i|=e_i\Delta V(t),\qquad
\Phi(K_t)-\Phi(K)=(W-\Phi(K))\,\frac{\Delta V(t)}{V_t}.
$$
The volume $V_t$ is $C^1$ near $0$, $\Delta V(t)$ has the sign of $t$ for $t\ne0$, and
$$
V'_0=\int_{\partial K}\psi(n(x))\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}(x)>0
$$
where $n(x)$ is the outward unit normal wherever it is unique.

At a Hausdorff local minimum of $\Phi$ subject to the same section traces, every such patch has $W=\Phi(K)$. Group the $u_i$ by their unoriented planes. A positive-curvature patch crossing exactly one such plane at a point on no other distinct plane excludes a local minimum if the two orientations in that class have unequal total weights. If $h$ is $C^2$ and $A_h>0$ on the entire sphere, an imbalanced class always gives such a patch. If all classes balance, $\Phi(K)=1/2$ for every $K$.

bd3988521f16dd20:2.reason: Either sign of volume change is available. The two signature weights differ by the nonzero orientation imbalance, so at least one sign region yields a strict decrease.
bd3988521f16dd20:2.statement: At a Hausdorff local minimum of the weighted cap mean among bodies with the same sections, every eligible strict signature patch satisfies $W=\Phi(K)$. A locally positive-curvature normal patch crossing only one unoriented plane class with unequal total weights in its two orientations excludes such a minimum, including when the body is nonsmooth elsewhere.

bd3988521f16dd20:4.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with $0\in\operatorname{int}K$. Suppose the $d+1$ unit vectors $u_i$ span $\mathbb R^d$ and form a minimal positive circuit, and that $\theta_i>0$, $\sum_i\theta_i=1$ satisfy $\sum_i\theta_i S_i u_i=0$, where $S_i=\mathcal H^{d-1}(K\cap u_i^\perp)$. As in the stationary setting, suppose the sections have centroid $0$. Assume the central cap masses $|K\cap\{x:u_i\cdot x\ge0\}|$ all equal $Q$, where $Q$ is the maximum over $y\in K$ of $\inf_{H\ni y}|K\cap H|$ for closed halfspaces $H$. Then the selected caps attain the depth at the deepest point $0$.

Take a bump $K_t$ as in the section-preserving support-bump lemma with signature weight $W\ne Q/|K|$. Such a bump exists if $h$ is $C^2$ with everywhere positive-definite $A_h$. For small signed $t$ there are a point $y(t)$ near $0$ and $d+1$ parallel translates of the respective original caps through $y(t)$, all with the same mass $q(t)$. They cover $\mathbb R^d$ and bound the new maximum raw depth by $q(t)$. The normalized cover bound has derivative
$$
\left.\frac{d}{dt}\frac{q(t)}{|K_t|}\right|_{t=0}
=\left(W-\frac Q{|K|}\right)\frac{V'_0}{|K|}.
$$
For all sufficiently small nonzero $t$ of the appropriate sign, the maximal normalized ordinary depth of $K_t$ is strictly below that of $K$.

bd3988521f16dd20:5.reason: The bump is $C^3$ at the joins. With $z=\cos^2(6\phi)$, $\psi+\psi''=432z-575z^2\ge-143$. The old patch is at least $\sin(\pi/12)>1/4$ from the other two lines, and at least $\cos(\pi/12)$ from the first, whereas the boundary displacement is at most $25t\le1/40$. The planar area formula follows from $\frac12\int\det(X_t,X_t')=\frac12\int (h_t^2-(h_t')^2)$. Integrating the even cosine powers gives $\int\psi=\pi/16$, $\int\psi^2=35\pi/768$ and $\int(\psi')^2=15\pi/4$. The normalized derivative uses $W=1/3$, $Q/|K|=1/2$ and $V'(0)=\pi/16$. The derivative concerns the upper cover.
bd3988521f16dd20:5.statement: For the unit disk with three equally weighted normals $120^\circ$ apart, take $h_t(\phi)=1+t\cos^4(6\phi)$ on $|\phi|\le\pi/12$ and $h_t=1$ elsewhere, for $0<t\le1/1000$. The exact volume change is $\Delta V=\pi t/16-2845\pi t^2/1536>0$, the three cap areas are $(\pi/2+\Delta V,\pi/2,\pi/2)$, the weighted mean is $1/2-\Delta V/[6(\pi+\Delta V)]$, and the normalized equal-cover bound has derivative $-1/96$ at zero.

beffb23a92dd631a:03.statement:
Let $d\ge1$. Let $P\subset\mathbb R^r$ be finite and affinely spanning, with the origin in the relative interior of $\operatorname{conv}(P)$. For each $p\in P$, let $K_p$ be a compact convex set of positive $d$-volume. Suppose the family is compatible, meaning that the convex hull of $S=\bigcup_{p\in P}(\{p\}\times K_p)$ has exactly $K_p$ as its fiber at $p$. Write $\mu=\sum_p\delta_p\otimes(\mathcal L^d|_{K_p})$ and $M=\mu(S)$. For an affine $L$ positive on $P$, take the unweighted fiber-volume measure of the family obtained from $S$ by $(p,x)\mapsto(p/L(p),x/L(p))$. Assume its maximum normalized closed-halfspace depth is locally minimized at $L=1$ among positive affine denominators. Write $\beta$ for this maximum at $L=1$ and $Q=\beta M$.

Index the deepest bases by $p_i$. At each one choose any exact positive circuit of nonvertical closed caps
$$
H_{ij}=\{(p,x):a_{ij}\cdot p+u_{ij}\cdot x\ge b_{ij}\},\qquad
\|u_{ij}\|=1,\qquad \mu(H_{ij})=Q,
$$
whose boundaries pass through a common deepest mark $(p_i,x_i)$ and whose weights satisfy $\rho_{ij}>0$, $\sum_j\rho_{ij}=1$, and $\sum_j\rho_{ij}u_{ij}=0$. At every other base use a fixed circuit covering the full fiber plane with each cap of mass strictly below $Q$. Such choices exist.

For each selected critical cap, let $\theta^{\rm pr}_{ij}$, $\theta^{\rm in}_{ij}$ and $\theta^{\rm out}_{ij}$ be the sums of $(d-1)$-dimensional section area on its proper sections, inside supporting sections (the fiber is contained in the closed cap), and outside supporting sections (the cap meets the fiber in a supporting face of zero $d$-volume), respectively. These are measures on the lifted sections in the original coordinates, with zero-area sections contributing zero. For $d=1$ the section measure is counting measure.

For every such choice of circuits and every Borel system $\sigma^{\rm in}_{ij}\in[0,1]$ on the inside supporting sections, there exist outside densities $\sigma^{\rm out}_{ij}\in[0,1]$ and nonnegative multipliers $\lambda_{ij}$. Put
$$
\zeta_{ij}=\theta^{\rm pr}_{ij}+\sigma^{\rm in}_{ij}\theta^{\rm in}_{ij}
                     +\sigma^{\rm out}_{ij}\theta^{\rm out}_{ij},
\qquad S_{ij}=\zeta_{ij}(\mathbb R^{r+d})>0.
$$
One such choice satisfies the linear identity
$$
-d\int A(p)\,d\mu
=\sum_{i,j}\lambda_{ij}\left[-d\int_{H_{ij}} A(p)\,d\mu
                             +\int \ell_{ij}(p,x)\,d\zeta_{ij}\right]
\tag{1}
$$
simultaneously for every signed affine $A$ and every signed cap velocity $\ell_{ij}(p,x)=\delta a_{ij}\cdot p+\delta u_{ij}\cdot x-\delta b_{ij}$ satisfying, for every $i$,
$$
\sum_j\rho_{ij}\delta u_{ij}=0,\qquad
\sum_j\rho_{ij}(\delta a_{ij}\cdot p_i-\delta b_{ij})=0.
\tag{2}
$$
In particular, the same certificate gives
$$
\sum_{i,j}\lambda_{ij}=\frac1\beta,\qquad
\int A(p)\,d\mu=\sum_{i,j}\lambda_{ij}\int_{H_{ij}} A(p)\,d\mu
\quad\text{for every affine }A,\qquad
\lambda_{ij} S_{ij}=c_i\rho_{ij}\quad(c_i\ge0).
\tag{3}
$$
Consequently each group has either all multipliers positive or all zero. Equivalently, $\lambda_{ij}=\pi_i\kappa_{ij}/\beta$, where $\pi_i=\beta\sum_j\lambda_{ij}$ are nonnegative and sum to one, and $\kappa_{ij}=(\rho_{ij}/S_{ij})/\sum_l(\rho_{il}/S_{il})$. The same choice of outside allocations and multipliers works for all tests in (1)–(3) for the prescribed inside system.

For any fixed representation of j by actual bases using a source z∈P_+ with coefficient λ>0, p_j≥λ^m p_z and the source and target have the same limiting affine direction space. For sufficiently large l with |Q_{l,z}|≥ηM_l, their widths are uniformly comparable by §§1–2 with a=λ^m and D=(1+λ^{-1})^m/η. In particular same-parity positive sources share a direction space, with at most 2^k such strata, and the direct same-parity comparison also holds with a=η,D=2^m/η when both sources have mass at least ηM_l.

c0cb4d49afb99df3:03.reason: The exact Minkowski average illustrates why the positive limiting-mass assumption is needed. The direction result does not assert a uniform law on a lower-dimensional limit or an allocation of cap mass.
c0cb4d49afb99df3:03.statement: At bases −1,+1 take rectangles [−1,1]×[−ε,ε] and [−ε,ε]×[−1,1], ε>0, and their lifted convex hull. The middle integer fiber is a square of side 1+ε, and the three areas are 4ε,(1+ε)^2,4ε, totaling 1+10ε+ε². As ε→0 the orthogonal endpoint limit segments have zero limiting relative weight and the middle weight tends to one.

external_dependencies: Implicit function theorem applied to the first-order condition in the affine parameter.
c0fc791108fc8765:01.reason: Smoothness follows by the implicit function theorem in a positive local denominator neighborhood. The envelope derivative then gives the tangent to the concave root, yielding the exact closed-body floor.
c0fc791108fc8765:01.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, and let $y\in\operatorname{int}K$. Define $E_K(y)=\min_a\int_K[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx$ over $a$ for which the denominator is positive on $K$, and let $a_y$ be its unique minimizer. The maps $y\mapsto a_y$ and $y\mapsto E_K(y)$ are smooth on $\operatorname{int}K$ and
$$
\nabla_y E_K(y)=(d+1)E_K(y)a_y,\qquad
\nabla_y E_K(y)^{1/d}=\frac{d+1}{d}E_K(y)^{1/d}a_y.
$$
The optimal denominator $1+a_y\cdot(x-y)$ is at least $1/(d+1)$ on $K$ and strictly greater than $1/(d+1)$ on $\operatorname{int}K$.

external_dependencies: Finite LP strong duality, attained dual optimum, and vertex existence for nonempty pointed polyhedra.
c0fc791108fc8765:02.reason: The finite support LP has a common bounded set of possible affine slopes, including relative-boundary bases. Weighted inballs give a uniform inradius.
c0fc791108fc8765:02.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite and nonempty, with a compact convex body $K_p\subset\mathbb R^d$ of nonempty interior for every $p\in P$, where $d\ge1$. Let $Q=\operatorname{conv}P$ and $C=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{p\in P}(\{p\}\times K_p)$. For every $z\in Q$ let $C_z=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}$. The fibers $C_z$ are convex bodies with a uniform positive inradius. If $h_K(u)=\max_{x\in K}u\cdot x$, then
$$
h_{C_z}(u)=\max_{\substack{\lambda_p\ge0,\ \sum_p\lambda_p=1\\ \sum_p\lambda_p p=z}}
\sum_p\lambda_p h_{K_p}(u).
$$
There is a finite constant $L$ depending on the given family such that $d_H(C_z,C_{z'})\le L\|z-z'\|$ for all $z,z'\in Q$, including its relative boundary. In particular, for each $y\in\operatorname{int}C_z$, the fibers at all sufficiently close bases in $Q$ contain a common ball centered at $y$.

external_dependencies: Supporting subgradient existence for a finite convex function on a finite-dimensional full vector space.
c0fc791108fc8765:03.reason: Local Lipschitz continuity of the root on the canonical hull gives a finite global supergradient at a relative-boundary base. Its continuous component is forced by the own-interior derivative, and positivity gives the affine denominator floor.
c0fc791108fc8765:03.statement:
Let $d\ge1$. Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite and nonempty, let each $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ for $z\in P$ be a convex body, and assume $\sum_z\lambda_z K_z\subset K_p$ whenever $\lambda_z\ge0$, $\sum_z\lambda_z=1$, and $\sum_z\lambda_z z=p\in P$. Set $Q=\operatorname{conv}P$ and $C=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$. For the positive attained energy
$E_K(y)=\min_a\int_K[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx$ over denominators positive on $K$, put $F(z,x)=E_{C_z}(x)^{1/d}$ on $\Omega_C=\{(z,x):z\in Q,\ x\in\operatorname{int}C_z\}$.

Fix $p\in P$ and $y\in\operatorname{int}K_p$, let $a_y$ be the optimizer at this mark in $K_p$, and put $F_0=F(p,y)$. The function $F$ is locally Lipschitz relative to $\operatorname{aff}(Q)\times\mathbb R^d$ on its domain near $(p,y)$, and there is a finite $B\in\operatorname{span}(Q-Q)$ such that
$$
F(z,x)\le F_0\left[1+B\cdot(z-p)+\frac{d+1}{d}a_y\cdot(x-y)\right]\qquad((z,x)\in\Omega_C).
$$
Every supergradient at $(p,y)$ has continuous component $\frac{d+1}{d}F_0a_y$. The associated affine chart
$$
L(z,x)=1+a_y\cdot(x-y)+\frac{d}{d+1}B\cdot(z-p)
$$
is at least $1/(d+1)$ on $C$ and strictly greater on $\Omega_C$. The base point $p$ may lie on the relative boundary of $Q$. For arbitrary compact convex ambient bodies a finite boundary-base energy supergradient can fail, even with full-dimensional ball fibers.

c0fc791108fc8765:04.reason: For a≠0 evaluate the accepted support majorant at −a/|a| and multiply the slope by |a|. Equality is attained on the source support face. Use b=0 for a=0. The optimizer's numerical δ=1/(d+1) is a separate pending §2 input.
c0fc791108fc8765:04.statement: Let P⊂R^n be finite with nonempty compact convex K_z, fix p∈P with all anchored Minkowski inclusions at p, and let C be the lifted hull. For any y,a∈R^d there exists b∈R^n such that inf_C [1+a·(x−y)+b·(z−p)]=min_{x∈K_p}[1+a·(x−y)]. If this floor is δ>0, an inverse-power continuation threshold strictly below δ is inactive on a neighborhood of C.

c0fc791108fc8765:05.reason: The reviewed last example has radius 1+√z and its sampled two-fiber hull has radius 1+z. Each ball's center has optimizer zero. The square-root secant diverges at the boundary base, excluding a finite supergradient.
c0fc791108fc8765:05.statement: For C={(z,x):0≤z≤1, |x|≤1+√z} the root energy at (z,0) is |B_d|^(1/d)(1+√z), so no finite relative base supergradient exists at (0,0). Sampling z=0,1 gives a canonical hull with radius 1+z. In both constructions the source optimizer has constant denominator one.

c0fc791108fc8765:06.reason: The support transfer preserves the exact source minimum throughout the canonical hull. The attained denominator floor keeps the pure inverse power valid on a neighborhood. Under lattice completeness the accepted one-action cut theorem gives the fixed integer census and regular old-contact speed.
c0fc791108fc8765:06.statement:
Let $d\ge1$. Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite and nonempty, let each $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ for $z\in P$ be a convex body, and assume the sampled anchored Minkowski inclusions. Put $C=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$. Fix $p\in P$ and $y\in\operatorname{int}K_p$, and let $a_y$ be the optimal parameter for $E_{K_p}(y)=\min_a\int_{K_p}[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx$ over positive denominators. There exists a fixed base vector $b$ for which
$$
L(z,x)=1+a_y\cdot(x-y)+b\cdot(z-p),\qquad
\min_C L=\min_{x\in K_p}[1+a_y\cdot(x-y)]\ge\frac1{d+1}.
$$
For every threshold $0<\delta<1/(d+1)$, a tangent continuation of $t^{-d}$ below $\delta$ is inactive on a neighborhood of $C$ when evaluated at $L$.

If $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$, choose any continuous anchored support majorant $\ell(u,z)=h_{K_p}(u)+A_p(u)\cdot(z-p)\ge h_{K_z}(u)$ on $P$ for each unit $u$. Then the pure inverse-power cuts
$$
C_\varepsilon=C\cap\bigcap_{u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}}
\{(z,x):u\cdot x+\varepsilon h_{K_p-y}(u)L(z,x)^{-d}\le \ell(u,z)\}
$$
give a nested compact convex deformation for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon\ge0$, in $\operatorname{aff}(P)\times\mathbb R^d$, with projection $\operatorname{conv}(P)$ and positive integer fibers exactly at $P$. On the source fiber the cuts are exactly the prescribed single-source cuts with denominator $1+a_y\cdot(x-y)$. At a regular old boundary point $x\in\partial K_z$ with normal $\nu$, the inward first speed is $h_{K_p-y}(\nu)L(z,x)^{-d}$ if $\ell(\nu,z)=h_{K_z}(\nu)$, and zero otherwise.

c21aa22115d69526:01.reason: The mesh quadrature with a derivative jump is proved and used in the uniform expansion; the trapezoid remainder includes the last support cell.
c21aa22115d69526:01.statement: If g is continuous and compactly supported on [0,∞), piecewise C² with right derivative of bounded variation, then for any a>0, Σ_{h≥0}g(ah)=a^(-1)∫_0^∞g(x)dx+g(0)/2+E_a with |E_a|≤(a/8)Var(g').

c21aa22115d69526:02.reason: Take the same v=β/(at) in the uniform expansion and its mesh estimates. The continuous integral term, including its direct v=0 evaluation, is the same one in the accepted quartic kernel fact.
c21aa22115d69526:02.statement: For integer d≥2 set t=1/(d+1), Γ=(d/(d+1))^d. For a>0 and 0≤β≤at define r_h=(1−ah)_+, q_h=t−βh, p_h=t+β(h+1), h=0,1,…, and D=ΓΣ_h r_h^d−Σ_h[E(q_h,r_h)+E(p_h,r_h)], where E(s,r)=d^d s^(d−1)(r−ds)_+ for r,s>0 and E(s,0)=0. Put θ=d/(d+1), v=β/(at), f(v)=(1+v)^(d+1)/(1+θv)^d, L_v(x)=(1−vx)^(d−1)[1−(d+1−dv)x]_+, R_(a,v)(x)=(1+av+vx)^(d−1)[1−dav−(d+1+dv)x]_+ on their active supports on [0,∞), and zero elsewhere. Set I_R(a,v)=∫R_(a,v), J_d(v)=∂_aI_R(0,v) and G_d(v)=∫L_v+I_R(0,v)−1/(d+1), with integrals over [0,∞). Then J_d is continuous with J_d(0)=0, G_d is continuous with G_d(0)=0, and G_d(v)=[f(v)+f(−v)−2]/(dv²)−1/(d+1) for v>0. Uniformly for 0<a≤1/(2d), 0≤v≤1, D(a,atv)/Γ=−G_d(v)/a−J_d(v)−1/2+O_d(a).

c21aa22115d69526:03.reason: For fixed d the coefficient C_d+(d+1)K_d² is finite. Taking the supremum over the same β interval and then the upper limit a↓0 in the pointwise linear bound gives −Γ/2. The explicit cutoff gives D≤−Γ/4 on the whole small-slope region.
c21aa22115d69526:03.statement: For integer d≥2 set t=1/(d+1), Γ=(d/(d+1))^d. For a>0 and 0≤β≤at define r_h=(1−ah)_+, q_h=t−βh, p_h=t+β(h+1), h=0,1,…, and D=ΓΣ_h r_h^d−Σ_h[E(q_h,r_h)+E(p_h,r_h)], where E(s,r)=d^d s^(d−1)(r−ds)_+ for r,s>0 and E(s,0)=0. c21aa22115d69526:04.statement: For integer d≥2 set t=1/(d+1), Γ=(d/(d+1))^d. For a>0 and 0≤β≤at define r_h=(1−ah)_+, q_h=t−βh, p_h=t+β(h+1), h=0,1,…, and D=ΓΣ_h r_h^d−Σ_h[E(q_h,r_h)+E(p_h,r_h)], where E(s,r)=d^d s^(d−1)(r−ds)_+ for r,s>0 and E(s,0)=0. c21aa22115d69526:05.reason: The uniform expansion proof covers moving active supports, the derivative jump and both endpoint tilts with the exact derivative and remainder constants.
c21aa22115d69526:05.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge2$ and put $t=1/(d+1)$ and $\Gamma=(dt)^d$. For $a>0$, $0\le\beta\le at$ and $h\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$, set $r_h=(1-ah)_+$, $q_h=t-\beta h$ and $p_h=t+\beta(h+1)$, where $x_+=\max\{x,0\}$. The diagonal-envelope deficit is
$$
D(a,\beta)=\Gamma\sum_{h\ge0}r_h^d
-d^d\sum_{\substack{h\ge0\\r_h>0}}
  \left[q_h^{d-1}(r_h-dq_h)_++p_h^{d-1}(r_h-dp_h)_+\right].
$$
Both sums have only finitely many nonzero terms. Whenever $r_h>0$, one has $q_h\ge tr_h>0$ and $p_h\ge t>0$.

For $0\le a\le1/(2d)$ and $v\in[0,1]$, let
$$
\begin{aligned}
L_v(x)&=(1-vx)^{d-1}[1-(d+1-dv)x]_+,\\
R_{a,v}(x)&=(1+av+vx)^{d-1}[1-dav-(d+1+dv)x]_+ .
\end{aligned}
$$
The kernels are defined for $x\ge0$ and set to zero beyond the positive-part supports. Let $I_R(a,v)=\int_0^\infty R_{a,v}(x)\,dx$, $J_d(v)=\partial_a I_R(0,v)$ (the right derivative), and $G_d(v)=\int_0^\infty L_v(x)\,dx+I_R(0,v)-1/(d+1)$. Then $J_d$ and $G_d$ are continuous on $[0,1]$ and both vanish at $0$. For $0<v\le1$, with $f(z)=(1+z)^{d+1}/(1+dz/(d+1))^d$,
$$
G_d(v)=\frac{f(v)+f(-v)-2}{dv^2}-\frac1{d+1}.
$$
Set
$$
\begin{aligned}
V_d&=3d(3d+1)2^{d-3},&
T_d&=\frac{2^{d-3}(9d^2-7d+2)}{d+1},&
B_d&=(d+2)2^{d-4},\\
C_d&=\frac{V_d}{4}+\frac d8+\frac{T_d}{2}+B_d,&
K_d&=\frac{d(2d+1)}{(d+1)^2}\left(1+\frac1{d+1}\right)^{d-2}.
\end{aligned}
$$
For every $0<a\le1/(2d)$ and every $v\in[0,1]$,
$$
\frac{D(a,atv)}{\Gamma}=-\frac{G_d(v)}a-J_d(v)-\frac12+\rho_d(a,v),
\qquad
|\rho_d(a,v)|\le C_d a,\qquad |J_d(v)|\le K_d v .
$$

c21aa22115d69526:06.reason: The reviewed proof combines the uniform expansion and quartic lower gain, then completes the square. This gives the exact positive cutoff for all admissible tilts.
c21aa22115d69526:06.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge2$ and put $t=1/(d+1)$ and $\Gamma=(dt)^d$. For $a>0$, $0\le\beta\le at$ and $h\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$, set $r_h=(1-ah)_+$, $q_h=t-\beta h$ and $p_h=t+\beta(h+1)$, where $x_+=\max\{x,0\}$. The diagonal-envelope deficit is
$$
D(a,\beta)=\Gamma\sum_{h\ge0}r_h^d
-d^d\sum_{\substack{h\ge0\\r_h>0}}
  \left[q_h^{d-1}(r_h-dq_h)_++p_h^{d-1}(r_h-dp_h)_+\right].
$$
Both sums have only finitely many nonzero terms. Whenever $r_h>0$, one has $q_h\ge tr_h>0$ and $p_h\ge t>0$.

With the constants $C_d$ and $K_d$ of the uniform deficit expansion, define
$$
\varepsilon_d=\min\left\{\frac1{2d},\frac1{4[C_d+(d+1)K_d^2]}\right\}.
$$
For every $0<a\le1/(2d)$ and $0\le\beta\le at$,
$$
\frac{D(a,\beta)}{\Gamma}\le -\frac12+[C_d+(d+1)K_d^2]a.
$$
In particular $D(a,\beta)\le-\Gamma/4$ for all $0<a\le\varepsilon_d$ and $0\le\beta\le at$.

c22519c29667168e:01.reason: The exact weighted chord theorem applies to each finite balanced family. Reduction to a support of at most three and the sharp truncation proof give the 4/9 bound and the equality conditions.
c22519c29667168e:01.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a compact convex body with $0\in\operatorname{int}K$. Let $p_1,\ldots,p_m$ be nonzero vectors with $p_i,-p_i\in\partial K$ for every $i$. Write $R(x_1,x_2)=(-x_2,x_1)$ and $H_i=\{x:(Rp_i)\cdot x\ge0\}$. If $\theta_i\ge0$, $\sum_i\theta_i=1$, and $\sum_i\theta_i p_i=0$, then
$$
\sum_i\theta_i|K\cap H_i|\ge \frac49|K|,
$$
where $|\cdot|$ denotes planar area. The constant is sharp. Equality holds exactly when $K$ is a triangle with centroid $0$ and, after dropping zero weights and merging repeated oriented chords, the three $H_i$ are the vertex halfplanes through $0$ parallel to the opposite sides, with total weight $1/3$ on each. A balanced opposite pair, or a positive noncollinear triple with one weight $1/2$, has weighted cap area $|K|/2$.

c22519c29667168e:02.reason: The accepted theorem includes the exactly balanced collinear and half-weight cases and the complete triangle equality classification after merging repeated orientations.
c22519c29667168e:02.statement: For a planar convex body with 0 interior, centered chords with signed endpoints p_i and inward cap normals Rp_i, and positive weights balancing Σθ_ip_i=0 and summing to 1, the weighted cap fraction is exactly 1/2 for an opposite pair, or for a noncollinear triple with one weight 1/2. For a positive noncollinear triple, equality at 4/9 occurs exactly for a triangle centered at 0 with its three facet-parallel vertex caps through 0 and equal weights.

c22519c29667168e:03.reason: The heavy-sector truncation, exact sector areas and strict triple calculation are the intermediate geometric steps of the accepted sharp bound.
c22519c29667168e:03.statement: In the strict positive noncollinear triple of §1 with all θ_i<1/2, the heavy-sector truncation yields H⊆K′⊆T, where T is a triangle, H=T∩(−T), and the integrand W−4/9 has positive integral on each removed piece of positive area. For barycentric coordinates l_i of 0 in T, set t_i=1−2l_i>0 and e=Σ_{i<j}t_it_j. Then Σt_i=1, θ_i=t_i(1−t_i)/(2e), |H|/|T|=2e and light corner areas are t_i²|T|. Every box-vertex mean (e+Σ_{i∈I}θ_i t_i²)/(2e+Σ_{i∈I}t_i²) is at least 4/9, with equality exactly when I includes all three corners and t_i=1/3 for all i.

c2528b1460a23da4:01.reason: Inline the short partition of pending 5fcdb1b3fadb0891 §§1–3. On dist(a,V)≥ε take actual representatives of distinct projected vertices of a finite δ-support approximation with δ<ε, and choose the smallest maximizing index. The gap ||πa||(||πa||−δ)>0 avoids the original cylinder. Two maximizing inequalities and equal output would give −||p_i−p_j||²≥0, so the map is injective on all ties. Disjoint translated Borel pieces and source-only monotone convergence prove the transfer. Equivalently its first inequality follows by layer cake from that pending note's Borel-target theorem applied to E_t={g>t}, H_t={F>t}. The affine baseline lies entirely inside the translated cylinder, disjoint from the transferred mass; repeated baselines cannot be summed.
c2528b1460a23da4:01.statement: Let A,B⊂ℝ^m be nonempty compact, V a linear subspace, q≥0 with H_q(A)<∞, and Z=V+conv B. For nonnegative Borel F on ℝ^m and g on A such that F(a+b)≥g(a) for all a∈A,b∈B, ∫_{(A+B)∖Z}F dH_q≥∫_{A∖V}g dH_q, allowing extended integrals. If P is one compact subset of A in an affine subspace L, then ∫_{A+B}F dH_q≥∫_{P+B}F dH_q+∫_{A∖L}g dH_q. This holds at q=0 and in actual mixed-lattice sum coordinates.

c2528b1460a23da4:02.reason: Strict source incidence survives every actual translation by B coordinatewise, and zero-level incidence is unchanged by midpoint dilation. The affine span loss is Lebesgue-null in the ordinary body case. In the mixed variant the precise term is ∫_{A∖aff P}Ψ(ρ)dH_q and scaling is Hausdorff 2^q, including q=0. Matching weak versions also work if both source and target incidence are weak. The same weighted geometry handles each Ψ. Marginal cap masses alone cannot determine OR/AND or multiplicity; the example with equal mass on 00,11 versus 01,10 illustrates this without claiming an actual body.
c2528b1460a23da4:02.statement: Let A,B,K⊂ℝ^d be full-dimensional convex bodies with (A+B)/2⊂K, P⊂A compact with dim aff P<d, and v_i·b≤1 for b∈B and i=1,…,s. Put σ_i(x)=1_{v_i·x<0} and ρ_i(a)=1_{v_i·a<−1}. For every coordinatewise nondecreasing Ψ:{0,1}^s→[0,∞), the same P satisfies 2^d∫_K Ψ(σ)≥∫_{P+B}Ψ(σ)+∫_A Ψ(ρ). This includes OR, AND and (Σ_{i∈I}σ_i−ℓ)₊ for integer ℓ≥0, with the analogous robust source count. For compact sets of finite intrinsic source measure H_q on one common integer parity class, the midpoint version uses 2^q and retains A∖aff P in the last term when it carries mass; K must contain the actual lattice midpoints.

external_dependencies: Classical Brunn–Minkowski, used only for the strength comparison. For compact sets see Livshyts, Marsiglietti, Nayar and Zvavitch, On the Brunn–Minkowski inequality for general measures with applications to new isoperimetric-type inequalities, equation (1), https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.04878. Approximate the strict-cut convex residual from within by compact tightened cuts if using the compact-set version.
c2528b1460a23da4:03.reason: The baseline has affine dimension ≤k−1 and the selected translates P_j+B lie in disjoint residual sign cells by positive balance. This is an immediate choice of increasing indicator for the preceding joint theorem. The marginal sum estimate alone is also implied by separate Brunn–Minkowski on each selected R_j(A) and B: (a_j^(1/d)+b^(1/d))^d≥a_j+b, and for each other nonempty residual it yields ≥a_j. These convex Borel residuals and their convex sums are Lebesgue measurable, including strict cuts. The actual baseline integral remains additional information.
c2528b1460a23da4:03.statement: For full-dimensional convex bodies A,B,K⊂ℝ^d with (A+B)/2⊂K and B⊂⋂_i{v_i·b≤1} for circuit normals v_0,…,v_d with Σv_i=0, write R_j(A)=A∩⋂_{i≠j}{v_i·a<−1}, R_j(K)=K∩⋂_{i≠j}{v_i·x<0}. For J of size k≤d with each R_j(A), j∈J, nonempty, choose one actual point P_j in each and one baseline P=conv{P_j:j∈J}. For every J′⊇J, 2^d Σ_{j∈J′}|R_j(K)|≥k|B|+Σ_{j∈J′}|R_j(A)|.

c2528b1460a23da4:04.reason: The caps have zero B area, so their own K fractions in raw units are Q−U_i. Outside the three null lines K has either one or two missed cap signs by Σv_i=0. The integral of (N_K−1)₊ is therefore exactly 2k−3Q+Σ U_i. On A the robust clipped count equals the disjoint residual union indicator. This exact identity ties an actual common baseline to the three shared critical cap masses. Accepted ceecf08780802b6a is a different two-cap covering ledger without midpoint injection, the three fixed cap slopes, or the shared baseline.

c3c2ca0e4dcbdc9d:01.statement:
Let $g_0,\ldots,g_{m-1}$ be a nonnegative, nonzero concave sequence on consecutive indices, with $m\ge1$. Concavity means that its successive differences are nonincreasing. Put $H=\max_i g_i$ and choose any index $j$ with $g_j=H$. For every real $p\ge2$,
$$
(p+1)\sum_i g_i^p-pH\sum_i g_i^{p-1}
\ge \frac{H^p}{2}\left(\frac1{2j+1}+\frac1{2(m-1-j)+1}\right).
$$
The bound allows zero endpoints, a peak at either endpoint, and an arbitrary choice of peak in a plateau.

c3c2ca0e4dcbdc9d:02.statement:
Let $f_0,\ldots,f_{L-1}$ be a nonnegative, nonzero concave sequence on consecutive indices, with $L\ge1$. Put $R=\max_i f_i$ and choose any $j$ with $f_j=R$. For real $p\ge2$ and $0\le c\le R$, set $Q_p(c)=\sum_i(f_i-c)_+^p$, where $x_+=\max\{x,0\}$. For $0\le t<R$ let $[a(t),b(t)]$ be the strict superlevel interval of indices with $f_i>t$, and set
$$
\kappa_j(t)=\frac12\left(\frac1{2(j-a(t))+1}+\frac1{2(b(t)-j)+1}\right).
$$
The function $\kappa_j$ is nondecreasing and $1/L\le\kappa_j(t)\le1$. For $0\le c<R$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
Q_p(c)
&\ge (1-c/R)^{p+1}Q_p(0)
  +(R-c)^{p+1}\int_0^c\frac{\kappa_j(t)}{(R-t)^2}\,dt\\
&\ge (1-c/R)^{p+1}Q_p(0)+\kappa_j(0)\frac{c(R-c)^p}{R}.
\end{aligned}
$$
For $0<c<R$, partition $[0,c]$ at the distinct sequence values in $(0,c)$, writing the endpoints and knots as $0=t_0<\cdots<t_m=c$. The integral is exactly
$$
\sum_{\ell=0}^{m-1}\kappa_j(s_\ell)
  \left(\frac1{R-t_{\ell+1}}-\frac1{R-t_\ell}\right),
\qquad s_\ell\in(t_\ell,t_{\ell+1}),
$$
and it is zero at $c=0$. At $c=R$ the scaled integral remainder has continuous extension zero. Both inequalities are equalities at $c=0$ and $c=R$, and are identities for every $c$ if $L=1$. The bound with the remainder dropped is strict for $0<c<R$.

c62d1cc13c75171f:01.statement:
Let $F$ be a $k$-dimensional simplex, $k\ge1$, with normalized volume $\mu_F$, and let $t$ be one of its barycentric coordinates. For $b\in(0,1)$ put $r=\frac14\min\{b,(1-b)/k\}$. Every continuous nonnegative convex function $f$ on $F$ satisfies
$$
\int_{\{|t-b|\le\eta\}} f\,d\mu_F
\le \frac{2\eta}{r}\int_F f\,d\mu_F,\qquad 0\le\eta\le r.
$$

Let $S$ be a full-dimensional simplex in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, with centroid $g$ and barycentric functions $\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_d$. Put $m=d+1$, $b=1/m$, and $C_i=\{x:\lambda_i(x)\ge b\}$. Suppose $K$ is a compact convex body with $g+(1-\delta)(S-g)\subseteq K\subseteq S$ for $0\le\delta<1$. Write $\tau=1-|K|/|S|$ and $R_i=|(S\setminus K)\cap C_i|/|S|$, where $|\cdot|$ is $d$-dimensional volume. For any affine margin $\phi$ with $H=\{x:\phi(x)\ge0\}$, if $\sup_{x\in S}|\phi(x)-(\lambda_i(x)-b)|\le\eta\le(1-\delta)/(4m)$, then
$$
\frac{|(S\setminus K)\cap(H\mathbin{\triangle}C_i)|}{|S|}
\le 8m\eta(1-\delta)^{-d-1}\tau .
$$
In particular, $|(S\setminus K)\cap H|/|S|\le R_i+8m\eta(1-\delta)^{-d-1}\tau$. The affine margin may have any threshold satisfying the stated bound.

For the radial formula used to obtain this bound, let $F_j=\{\lambda_j=0\}\cap S$, let $\rho$ be the Minkowski gauge of $K-g$, and put $f_j(z)=\rho(z-g)-1$ and $w_j(z)=1-\rho(z-g)^{-d}$ on $F_j$. Each $f_j$ is continuous, convex and nonnegative, and $d(1-\delta)^d f_j\le w_j\le d f_j$. cb7ea417552f0084:02.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with nonempty interior, and let $y,o\in\operatorname{int}K$. Let $K_\varepsilon$ be nested compact convex bodies for $\varepsilon\ge0$ with $K_0=K$. Suppose that for some $C\ge0$ and all sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$,
$$
o+(1-C\varepsilon)(K-o)\subseteq K_\varepsilon\subseteq K.
$$
For $x\in\partial K$, write the radial endpoint of $K_\varepsilon$ on the ray from $o$ through $x$ as $o+(1-t_\varepsilon(x))(x-o)$. At a regular boundary point $x$, let $n(x)$ be its unique outward unit normal and set $dS=d\mathcal H^{d-1}$ on $\partial K$. Assume that for a bounded measurable $v$,
$$
\frac{t_\varepsilon(x)}{\varepsilon}\longrightarrow
\frac{v(x)}{n(x)\cdot(x-o)}
\qquad\text{for $dS$ almost every }x.
$$
Then $v\ge0$ almost everywhere. Take $y_\varepsilon=y+\varepsilon w+o(\varepsilon)$ for a fixed $w\in\mathbb R^d$. For a body $L$ and $q\in\operatorname{int}L$, let
$$
T_L(q)=\max\left\{\int_L f(x)\,dx:\ 0\le f\le1,\ f\text{ measurable},\
                       \int_L(x-q)f(x)\,dx=0\right\}.
$$
Set $T=T_K(y)$ and let $U$ be the compact nonempty set of minimizers of $G_0(u)=\int_K[1+u\cdot(x-y)]_+\,dx$, where $[a]_+=\max(a,0)$. For all sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, $y_\varepsilon\in\operatorname{int}K_\varepsilon$. The following right derivative exists, and the minimum is attained:
$$
\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\right|_{0+}T_{K_\varepsilon}(y_\varepsilon)
=\min_{u\in U}\left\{
-\int_{\partial K}[1+u\cdot(x-y)]_+v(x)\,dS(x)-T\,u\cdot w
\right\}. \tag{1}
$$
When $y$ differs from the centroid $g_K$, $U$ is a singleton. When $y=g_K$, put $V=|K|$, $D=\int_{\partial K}v\,dS$ and $B=\int_{\partial K}(x-y)v(x)\,dS(x)$. For the Minkowski gauge $p_{K-y}(z)=\inf\{t\ge0:z\in t(K-y)\}$, (1) becomes
$$
\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\right|_{0+}T_{K_\varepsilon}(y_\varepsilon)
=-D-p_{K-y}(-B-Vw).
\tag{2}
$$
The ordinary centroid satisfies $g_{K_\varepsilon}=y-\varepsilon B/V+o(\varepsilon)$. The derivative in (2) equals $-D$ exactly when $w=-B/V$, and is strictly smaller otherwise. In dimension $1$, $dS$ is counting measure on the two endpoints. The formula allows hinge hyperplanes incident with vertices, edges, and supporting facets; it does not require a differentiable cutting section.

cb7ea417552f0084:03.reason: At the centroid the active hinge set is the negative polar, whose support gives the exact gauge penalty. The centroid velocity is −B/V and is the unique penalty-free velocity.
cb7ea417552f0084:03.statement: Under the erosion hypotheses of §§1–3, at y=g_K let V=|K|, D=∫_{∂K}v, B=∫_{∂K}(x−y)v, and p_{K−y} be the Minkowski gauge. Then T' = −D−p_{K−y}(−B−Vw) and g_{Kε}=y−εB/V+o(ε). Equality T'=−D holds exactly when w=−B/V; all other w give a strict extra loss.

cb7ea417552f0084:06.reason: The physical derivative and total mass loss give the quotient rows, with fixed-baseline averaging and a conditional finite-path envelope stated separately.
cb7ea417552f0084:06.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty, $n\ge0$, and let the positive-volume $d$-dimensional fibers $K_{z,\varepsilon}$, $z\in P$, be those of an actual nested convex deformation with fixed measured sites $P$. Assume each fiber satisfies the homothet and almost-everywhere radial speed hypotheses of the physical retained-mass derivative theorem, with old fiber $K_z$ and inward speed $v_z$. Let
$$
M_\varepsilon=\sum_{z\in P}|K_{z,\varepsilon}|,\qquad
M=M_0,\qquad D_{\rm mix}=\sum_{z\in P}\int_{\partial K_z}v_z\,dS .
$$
Fix $p\in P$ and $y\in\operatorname{int}K_p$ and prescribe $y_\varepsilon=y+\varepsilon w+o(\varepsilon)$ in that fiber. Let $U_p$ be the old optimizing hinge set for $T=T_{K_p}(y)$ and put $\tau=T/M$. The right derivative is
$$
\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\right|_{0+}
\frac{T_{K_{p,\varepsilon}}(y_\varepsilon)}{M_\varepsilon}
=\frac1M\min_{u\in U_p}\left\{
\tau D_{\rm mix}
-\int_{\partial K_p}[1+u\cdot(x-y)]_+v_p(x)\,dS(x)-T\,u\cdot w
\right\}. \tag{6}
$$
It is nonnegative exactly when every row in braces is nonnegative. Off the centroid there is a single row. At $y=g_{K_p}$ the criterion is exactly
$$
\tau D_{\rm mix}-D_p-p_{K_p-y}(-B_p-|K_p|w)\ge0,\qquad
D_p=\int_{\partial K_p}v_p\,dS,\quad
B_p=\int_{\partial K_p}(x-y)v_p\,dS .
\tag{7}
$$
When $K_p$ is a polytope and $y=g_{K_p}$, the minimum can be taken at the finitely many vertices of $U_p=\{u:1+u\cdot(a-y)\ge0\text{ for every vertex }a\text{ of }K_p\}$. These are linear response rows when the actual physical speeds and prescribed velocity depend linearly on deformation parameters.

One actual setting for such averaging is the single-baseline case of accepted fact 84cd8a85417b0d7a. Use one fixed continuous-in-normal, affine-in-base support baseline satisfying its majorization hypotheses; average the nonnegative convex cut fields on that baseline before constructing the body. For a Borel probability average, assume a nonempty compact metric field parameter space and joint continuity of the fields, and average prescribed velocities integrable in that parameter. The response in (6) is then the average of individual responses off the centroid; at the centroid it is the minimum of the averaged rows.

For a conditional use of (6), define depth as the infimum of the physical mixed masses of closed ambient halfspaces containing the mark, and deepest points as the maximum-depth points on $\bigcup_{p\in P}\{p\}\times K_{p,\varepsilon}$. For this maximum, define $T_L(q)$ at boundary marks by the same mass and moment constraints; it is zero there since a supporting hyperplane through $q$ is Lebesgue-null and every feasible density with barycenter $q$ must be concentrated on that hyperplane. Suppose the secondary maximum $S(\varepsilon)$ of $T_{K_{p,\varepsilon}}(y)/M_\varepsilon$ among deepest points exists for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon\ge0$. Assume a fixed nonempty finite list of paths $(p_j,y_j(\varepsilon))$, each deepest for all such $\varepsilon$, with $p_j\in P$, $y_j(0)\in\operatorname{int}K_{p_j}$ and $y_j(\varepsilon)=y_j(0)+\varepsilon w_j+o(\varepsilon)$. cd833c78fb705a2e:01.statement:
Let $D\ge1$, let $\mu$ be a finite nonnegative Borel measure on $\mathbb{R}^D$ with convex support $K=\operatorname{supp}\mu$, and suppose every affine hyperplane has zero $\mu$-mass. Assume there is a fixed $g>0$ such that every closed convex subset $L\subseteq K$ of positive $\mu$-mass contains a point $y$ satisfying $\mu(L\cap H)\ge g\mu(L)$ for every closed halfspace $H$ containing $y$.

Let $H_1,\ldots,H_m$ be a finite cover of $K$ by closed halfspaces with nonzero normals, with $m\ge1$, and let $A_i=\mu(H_i)$. For every $\alpha\ge0$,
$$
\mu(K)\le\sum_{i=1}^m(A_i-\alpha)_+ + \frac{\alpha}{g},
\qquad x_+=\max\{x,0\}.
\tag{1}
$$

For ordinary volume on a convex body $K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^D$, write $V=\operatorname{vol}_D(K)$ and $\gamma_D=(D/(D+1))^D$. Then (1) holds with $g=\gamma_D$ and $A_i=\operatorname{vol}_D(K\cap H_i)$. In particular, for $a=\min_i A_i$,
$$
\sum_{i=1}^m A_i-V\ge(m-1/\gamma_D)a.
\tag{2}
$$
Arrange the cap masses in decreasing order and append zeros if $m<3$. For $D\ge2$,
$$
A_{(1)}+A_{(2)}+(1/\gamma_D-2)A_{(3)}\ge V,
\tag{3}
$$
where $0<1/\gamma_D-2<1$. For $D=1$, $A_{(1)}+A_{(2)}\ge V$.

cd9374750b11bd94:04.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, and let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body of volume $V>0$ and volume centroid zero. Let $0<r\le s$, and for $u\ne0$ define $F_u(t)=|K\cap\{x:u\cdot x\ge t\}|/V$, where $|\cdot|$ is $d$-dimensional volume.

Write $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ and $c_d=(2\Gamma_d)^{1/d}$. Define
$$
\Phi_d(r,s)=
\begin{cases}
r, & d=1,\\
\left[r c_d+\dfrac{s-r}{d-1}(1-c_d)\right]^d, & d\ge2,\ r\le s\le dr,\\
r^d, & d\ge2,\ s\ge dr.
\end{cases}
$$
The two $d\ge2$ branches agree at $s=dr$.

For every $u\ne0$ and $t\in\mathbb R$,
$$
r^dF_u(t/r)+s^dF_u(-t/s)\ge\Phi_d(r,s).
$$
If $d\ge2$ and $s>r$, then $\Phi_d(r,s)>2\Gamma_d r^d$. For each fixed $u\ne0$ the minimum of the left side over $t\in\mathbb R$ is at most $r^d$. It equals $r^d$ and is attained at a finite threshold if $s\ge dr$, which includes every $0<r\le s$ in dimension one.

Let $n,d\ge1$ and let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body. For $z\in\mathbb Z^n$ write $C_z=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}$. Let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be full-dimensional, compact and convex with volume centroid zero and volume $V>0$. Suppose that for $p\in\mathbb Z^n$, $v\in\mathbb Z^n\setminus\{0\}$, $a_-,a_+\in\mathbb R^d$ and $0<r\le s$, the actual fibers $C_{p-v}$ and $C_{p+v}$ contain $a_-+rK$ and $a_++sK$, respectively. Put $g=(a_-+a_+)/2$ and $q=(r+s)/2$. Then $g+qK\subseteq C_p$.

Write $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ and $c_d=(2\Gamma_d)^{1/d}$. Define
$$
\Phi_d(r,s)=
\begin{cases}
r, & d=1,\\
\left[r c_d+\dfrac{s-r}{d-1}(1-c_d)\right]^d, & d\ge2,\ r\le s\le dr,\\
r^d, & d\ge2,\ s\ge dr.
\end{cases}
$$
The two $d\ge2$ branches agree at $s=dr$.

Every closed ambient halfspace $H$ containing $(p,g)$ captures total $d$-volume at least
$$
V\bigl[\Phi_d(r,s)+\Gamma_d q^d\bigr]
$$
from the three retained copies on the distinct bases $p-v,p,p+v$. In particular this lower bounds the raw depth of $(p,g)$ for $C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$.

ce31fbbf06cede9c:03.statement:
Let \(n\ge0\) and \(d\ge1\). Let \(P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n\) be finite and nonempty, and let \(K_p\subset\mathbb R^d\), \(p\in P\), be convex bodies satisfying the anchored inclusions
$$
\sum_i\lambda_i K_{p_i}\subseteq K_q
\quad\text{whenever}\quad
\lambda_i\ge0,\quad\sum_i\lambda_i=1,\quad q=\sum_i\lambda_i p_i\in P.
$$
Put \(S=\bigcup_{p\in P}\{p\}\times K_p\), let \(\mu\) be the sum of fiber volumes on \(S\), and let \(D_\mu(Y)=\inf_{H\ni Y}\mu(H)\) over closed ambient halfspaces. Write \(Q=\max_{Y\in S}D_\mu(Y)\), \(D=\{Y\in\mathbb R^{n+d}:D_\mu(Y)\ge Q\}\), and
$$
E_K(y)=\inf_{a:\ 1+a\cdot(x-y)>0\ \forall x\in K}\int_K[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx
\quad (y\in\operatorname{int}K).
$$
Then \(Q>0\) is attained, \(D\) is compact and convex, and every \((p,y)\in D\cap S\) has \(y\in\operatorname{int}K_p\). The positive number
$$
R=\max_{(p,y)\in D\cap S}E_{K_p}(y)^{1/d}
$$
is attained. Its attaining bases \(J\) satisfy \(J=\operatorname{conv}(J)\cap\mathbb Z^n\), with a unique attaining mark \(y_p\) at each \(p\in J\). For every \(p_i\in J\) and positive weights \(\lambda_i\) summing to one with \(q=\sum_i\lambda_i p_i\in\mathbb Z^n\),
$$
q\in J,\qquad y_q=\sum_i\lambda_i y_{p_i},\qquad
K_q=\sum_i\lambda_i K_{p_i},\qquad
K_{p_i}-y_{p_i}=K_q-y_q\quad\text{for every }i.
$$
If \(k(J)\) is the number of occupied parities modulo \(2\mathbb Z^n\) and \(M_J=\sum_{p\in J}|K_p|\), then \(Q\ge (d/(d+1))^d M_J/k(J)\).

cebdfbe6dc0c0994:01.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and $m\ge0$ be integers. Put $T_d=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_d)$, $V_d=1/d!$ and $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Take finite radii $R=r_0\ge r_1\ge\cdots\ge r_m\ge0$ with $R>0$ and with the drops $r_{h-1}-r_h$ nondecreasing in $h$. At each of the integer bases $-h$ and $h+1$, for $0\le h\le m$, take the fiber $r_hT_d$. Let $\mu$ denote the sum of the $d$-dimensional Lebesgue measures of these fibers.

Fix $u\in[0,\infty)^d$ with $\sum_i u_i=1$ and fix $\beta\ge0$. With $t=R/(d+1)$, the closed halfspace $H=\{(z,x):-\beta z+u\cdot x\ge t\}$ passes through $y=(0,t,\ldots,t)$, the actual centroid at base $0$. For $r\ge0$, $s\in\mathbb R$ and $h\ge0$, put
$$
F_r(s)=\frac{\operatorname{vol}_d(rT_d\cap\{x:u\cdot x\ge s\})}{V_d},
\qquad
G_h(r)=F_r(t-\beta h)+F_r(t+\beta(h+1))-\Gamma_d r^d .
$$
For $m\ge1$ there is a slope $a\in[0,R/m]$ such that $\ell_h=R-ah$ satisfies
$$
G_h(\ell_h)\le G_h(r_h)\qquad(0\le h\le m).
$$
The slope can be chosen with $\ell_h$ between $r_h$ and the unique minimizer of $G_h$ on $[0,\infty)$ for each $1\le h\le m$. For every such choice, equality in the comparison at an index holds exactly when $\ell_h=r_h$. Equality in the sum for such a choice is attainable exactly when the original radii are already affine in $h$. For $m=0$ leave the radius unchanged.

The replacement is realized by a compact convex body with the indicated fibers at the same integer bases and no other integer fibers. It retains $y$ and the very same $H$. The original signed cap surplus relative to the fraction $\Gamma_d/2$ is $V_d\sum_{h=0}^m G_h(r_h)$, with the identical formula using $\ell_h$ for the replacement. Hence an original cap below that fraction yields a replacement cap below the same fraction, measured against the replacement's own total mass.

d494e7e71949ac0b:03.statement:
Let $d\ge3$ be an integer and $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. If $Z$ has a compactly supported, nonatomic, centered $1/d$-concave probability law on $\mathbb R$, then for every $s\ne0$,
$$
\mathbb P(Z\ge s)+\mathbb P(Z\ge -s)>2\Gamma_d.
$$
In particular, if $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ is a convex body with volume $V>0$ and centroid $g$, then for each $u\ne0$ and $s\ne0$ the two closed caps $K\cap\{x:u\cdot(x-g)\ge s\}$ and $K\cap\{x:u\cdot(x-g)\ge -s\}$ have total volume greater than $2\Gamma_d V$.

d494e7e71949ac0b:04.statement:
Let $d\ge3$ be an integer, $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ a convex body, $\mu_K$ its normalized volume, and $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Define
$$
p_K(y)=\inf_{\substack{u\ne0\\s\in\mathbb R}}\frac{\mu_K\{x:u\cdot(x-y)\ge s\}+\mu_K\{x:u\cdot(x-y)\ge -s\}}{2}.
$$
The maximum $D_{\rm pair}(K)=\max_{y\in K}p_K(y)$ exists, satisfies $D_{\rm pair}(K)\ge\Gamma_d$, and equals $\Gamma_d$ exactly for simplices.

For fixed $0<r\le R$ and $\varepsilon>0$, consider the bodies with $rB_2^d\subseteq K\subseteq RB_2^d$ whose Hausdorff distance to the set of full-dimensional simplices is at least $\varepsilon$. If this class is nonempty, then $D_{\rm pair}(K)-\Gamma_d$ attains a strictly positive minimum on it.

The map D_pair is 1-Lipschitz in total variation distance sup_H|μ(H)−ν(H)| with the supremum defining the distance taken over all Borel H. For uniform laws on convex bodies, the ambient supremum equals the maximum over the body. For fixed d≥3 and 0<r≤R, D_pair is Hausdorff-continuous on rB⊂K⊂RB. On any nonempty subclass of these bodies at Hausdorff distance at least ε>0 from all simplices, the infimum of D_pair(K)−Γ_d is attained and strictly positive.

dafd411c026c302c:1.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional convex body, $d\ge1$, with volume $V$ and centroid $g$. For $u\ne0$ write $F(s)=|K\cap\{x:u\cdot(x-g)\ge s\}|/V$, and set $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. For every $s\in\mathbb R$,
$$
F(0)+F(s)+\frac12F(-s)\ge\gamma_d+\frac12.
$$
The right-hand side is attained. Equivalently, for every Lebesgue-measurable $A\subseteq K$ of volume $a$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$$
|K\cap\{u\cdot(x-g)\ge0\}|+
|A\cap\{u\cdot(x-g)\ge t\}|+
|K\cap\{u\cdot(x-g)\ge-t\}|
\ge \gamma_d V+\frac a2.
$$

dafd411c026c302c:5.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, and let $A,B,C\subset\mathbb R^d$ be convex bodies with $(A+C)/2\subseteq B$. Set $S=(\{-1\}\times A)\cup(\{0\}\times B)\cup(\{1\}\times C)$, measured by summing $d$-dimensional volumes on its three fibers. If a convex body $K$ satisfies $A\subseteq K\subseteq B\cap C$, let $a=|A|$, $V=|K|$, $E=|B|+|C|-2V$ and let $g_K$ be the volume centroid of $K$. Then the actual point $(0,g_K)$ has normalized mixed halfspace depth at least
$$
\frac{\gamma_d V+a/2}{2V+E+a}.
$$
This is at least $\gamma_d/2$ if $E\le(1/\gamma_d-1)a$. In particular, for $B=C=K$ the displayed bound holds with $E=0$, and the same conclusion holds at the actual middle centroid when $B$ and $C$ are translates of one another, taking $V=|B|$.

If $A,B,C$ are totally ordered by inclusion, some actual mixed point has normalized depth at least $\gamma_d/2$. The same holds if such an order is obtained by an affine change preserving $\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R^d$, including a shear affine in the integer base.

e06a5b80357a8187:01.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ be an integer, $t=1/(d+1)$, and $\Gamma=(dt)^d$. For $a>0$ and $0\le\beta\le at$, put $r_h=(1-ah)_+$, $q_h=t-\beta h$, and $p_h=t+\beta(h+1)$ for integers $h\ge0$, where $x_+=\max\{x,0\}$. For $r,q>0$ set $E_d(q,r)=d^dq^{d-1}(r-dq)_+$. The diagonal-envelope deficit is
$$
D_d(a,\beta)=\Gamma\sum_{h\ge0} r_h^d-
\sum_{\substack{h\ge0\\r_h>0}}\bigl[E_d(q_h,r_h)+E_d(p_h,r_h)\bigr].
$$
Every term in the second sum has positive thresholds. For $1\le H\le d$ put
$$
a_H=\frac{H+1}{H(d+1)},\qquad
W_{d,H}=\sum_{h\ge0}(1-a_Hh)_+^d,\qquad
K_{d,H}=\sum_{h=0}^{H-1}(1-h/d)^{d-1}(1-h/H).

The unrestricted maximum of $D_d(a,\beta)$ on the specified domain is attained and satisfies
$$

=\Gamma\max_{1\le H\le d}(W_{d,H}-K_{d,H})
<\frac{\Gamma}{6}.

Equivalently, the envelope sum for every admissible $(a,\beta)$ is strictly larger than $\Gamma\sum_h r_h^d-\Gamma/6$.

e239a5fb0d0efe4d:03.statement:

$$
S_i=\mathcal H^{d-1}(K\cap u_i^\perp),\qquad
p_i=\frac{|K\cap\{x:u_i\cdot x\ge0\}|}{V}.
$$
Suppose the centroid of each section $K\cap u_i^\perp$ has orthogonal projection $0$ onto $E$. If $\theta_i\ge0$, $\sum_i\theta_i=1$, and $\sum_i\theta_i S_i u_i=0$, then
$$
\sum_i\theta_i p_i\ge c_d,\qquad
c_2=\frac49,\qquad
c_d=\frac1{1+\max\{4/3,\sqrt{2(d-1)/d}\}}\quad(d\ge3).
$$
For $3\le d\le9$ this is $3/7$. For $d\ge10$ it is strictly greater than $2/5$. In particular $c_d>(d/(d+1))^d$ for $d\ge3$.

Consequently, in any dimension $d\ge1$, if $0\in\operatorname{int}K$, each central section has full centroid $0$, and the positive-weight normals span a space of dimension at most two, then the same weighted mean is at least $(d/(d+1))^d$. e4ccf81294305ade:09.statement:
Let $n,d\ge1$ and let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body. For $z\in\mathbb Z^n$ write $K_z=\{y:(z,y)\in C\}$ and let $g_z$ be its volume centroid when $|K_z|>0$. Fix an integer base $w$ with $|K_w|>0$. For any finite convex representation
$$
(w,x)=\sum_i\lambda_i(z_i,g_{z_i}),\qquad
\lambda_i>0,\quad \sum_i\lambda_i=1,\quad |K_{z_i}|>0,
$$
set $a=(\sum_i\lambda_i|K_{z_i}|^{1/d})^d$ and $\delta=1-a/|K_w|\in[0,1)$. For a nonzero linear functional $u$ on $\mathbb R^d$ let $W=\max_{K_w}u-\min_{K_w}u$. Then
$$
\frac{|u(x-g_w)|}{W}
\le \min\left\{\delta,\ \frac{d}{d+1}\frac{\delta}{1-\delta},\ \frac{d}{d+1}\right\}.
$$
For $0\le\varepsilon<1$, let $S_\varepsilon(w)$ be the set of all $x$ admitting such a representation with $a\ge (1-\varepsilon)|K_w|$. The width of $u(S_\varepsilon(w))$ is at most $\frac{\varepsilon}{1-\varepsilon}W$.

For every $d\ge1$ and $0<\delta<1$, an actual body with $n=1$, three integer fibers, and a representation at $w=0$ attains
$$
\frac{u(x-g_w)}{W}=\frac{d}{d+1}\frac{\delta(1-\delta^{1/d})}{1-\delta}.
$$
Consequently the coefficient $d/(d+1)$ is optimal to first order as $\delta\downarrow0$, even for such bodies. For every $d\ge1$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$, an actual body with $n=2$, five integer fibers, and $w=0$ has width $\varepsilon W$ for $u(S_\varepsilon(0))$. Thus the width coefficient one is optimal to first order as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$.

e81e0e86f9a482f3:01.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, $d\ge2$, with centroid $g$, and let $X$ be uniform on $K$. Fix a linear functional $\ell$ of width one on $K$. Write $p$ for the density of $\ell(X)$ given by section volumes, $m=\ell(g)$, and $A=m-\min_K\ell$. Then $p\le d$ and $p(m)\ge1$. Lowering a cap threshold by $a\ge0$ increases its normalized mass by at most $da$. For $0\le a\le A$,
$$
\mathbb P\{m-a\le\ell(X)\le m\}\ge a/d.
$$
In particular, if $y\in K$ and $\ell(g-y)\ge0$, then
$$
\frac{|K\cap\{\ell(x)\ge\ell(y)\}|}{|K|}
\ge \left(\frac{d}{d+1}\right)^d+\frac{\ell(g-y)}{d}.
$$

e81e0e86f9a482f3:03.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, $d\ge2$, with centroid $g$. Put $D=K-K$, let $\|\cdot\|_D$ be its gauge, and write $\gamma_j=(j/(j+1))^j$ for $j\ge1$. Suppose finitely many closed halfspaces $H_i=\{x:\ell_i(x-y)\ge0\}$ cover $\mathbb R^d$, where each $\ell_i$ has width one on $K$. Assume $|K\cap H_i|\le\tau|K|$ for every $i$, with $\gamma_d\le\tau<\gamma_{d-1}$. Then $y\in\operatorname{int}K$, and for every $v\in\partial D$,
$$
\max_i\ell_i(v)\ge\frac{\gamma_{d-1}-\tau}{d}.
$$
Equivalently, the convex hull of the $\ell_i$ contains $(\gamma_{d-1}-\tau)D^\circ/d$, where $D^\circ$ is the polar. Moreover,
$$
\|y-g\|_D
\le\min\left\{1,\frac{d^2(\tau-\gamma_d)}{\gamma_{d-1}-\tau}\right\}.
$$
In particular $\tau=\gamma_d$ forces $y=g$. If $0\le\epsilon=\tau-\gamma_d\le(\gamma_{d-1}-\gamma_d)/2$, the bound is at most $2d^2\epsilon/(\gamma_{d-1}-\gamma_d)$.

ecc8b4db4896dd08:03.statement:
For a full-dimensional convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, write $\Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d$. For $y\in K$, a unit vector $u$ and $s\ge0$, put $H_\pm(y,u,s)=\{x:u\cdot(x-y)\ge\pm s\}$ and
$$
p_K(y)=\min_{\lVert u\rVert_2=1,\ s\ge0}\frac{|K\cap H_+(y,u,s)|+|K\cap H_-(y,u,s)|}{2|K|},\qquad
P(K)=\max_{y\in K}p_K(y).
$$
Here $|\cdot|$ is ordinary $d$-dimensional volume.

Let $d\ge3$, $m=d+1$, and $c=(1-d^{1-d})/[(d-1)^2m]$. There exists $\delta_d>0$ depending only on $d$ such that for every full-dimensional simplex $S$ with centroid $g$, and every convex body $K$ with
$$
g+(1-\delta)(S-g)\subseteq K\subseteq S,\qquad 0\le\delta\le\delta_d,
$$
whose intersection with each facet of $S$ contains that facet's centroid, there is one $y\in\operatorname{int}K$ such that
$$
p_K(y)-\Gamma\ \ge\ \frac{\Gamma c}{4}\left(1-\frac{|K|}{|S|}\right).
$$
With $\tau=1-|K|/|S|$ and barycentric functions $\lambda_i$ of $S$, one may take $\lambda_i(y)=1/m+(\bar L-L_i)/(m\Gamma)$, where
$$
\eta=\min\left\{\frac1{8m},\frac{\Gamma c}{4\cdot 8m\cdot 2^{d+1}}\right\},\quad
R_i=\frac{|(S\setminus K)\cap\{\lambda_i\ge1/m\}|}{|S|},\quad
L_i=\min\{\tau,R_i+8m\eta\,2^{d+1}\tau\},\quad \bar L=\frac1m\sum_i L_i.
$$

In the ordinary affine frame of a reference simplex, let $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_d)$, $L=8(d+1)^3$, and
$$
\varepsilon_d=\min\left\{\frac1{64(d+1)^3},\ \frac{\delta_d}{d(d+1)(L+1)}\right\}.
$$
If the Hausdorff distance in the infinity norm satisfies $d_{H,\infty}(K,T)\le\varepsilon_d$, a minimum-volume enclosing simplex exists, and every such simplex $S$ satisfies $P(K)-\Gamma\ge(\Gamma c/4)(1-|K|/|S|)$. The claim applies in any ordinary affine image of this frame.

edf02845b3275e8c:02.statement:
Let $n,d$ be positive integers and let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body. Put $\Lambda=\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$, $S=C\cap\Lambda$, and assume $q=\dim_{\mathrm H}S\ge 1$. Set $\mu=\mathcal H_q|_S$. For $z\in\mathbb Z^n$ put $K_z=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}$, and let $P=\{z:w_z=\mathcal H_q(K_z)>0\}$.

Suppose finitely many labeled mass and base moment pairs $(t_i,m_i)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^n$ are feasible: there are $s_{iz}\ge 0$ with $\sum_i s_{iz}=w_z$ for $z\in P$ and $(t_i,m_i)=\sum_{z\in P}s_{iz}(1,z)$ for every label. Discard the labels with $t_i=0$ and index the remaining $k$ labels by $1,\ldots,k$. Fix any vectors $u_i\in\mathbb R^d$ such that $x\mapsto(u_i-u_j)\cdot x$ is nonconstant on each $K_z$ for $z\in P$ whenever $i\ne j$.

There are finite $\theta_i\in\mathbb R^{n+1}$ such that the affine scores $L_i(z,x)=\theta_i\cdot(1,z)+u_i\cdot x$ give closed cells
$$
D_i=C\cap\bigcap_{j\ne i}\{(z,x):L_i(z,x)\ge L_j(z,x)\}.
$$
Each $D_i$ is an ambient convex body cut from $C$ by at most $k-1$ closed halfspaces, and $D_i\cap\Lambda$ has Hausdorff dimension $q$. The cells satisfy
$$
\bigcup_iD_i=C,\qquad
\mu(D_i\cap D_j)=0\quad(i\ne j),\qquad
\left(\mu(D_i),\int_{D_i} z\,d\mu\right)=(t_i,m_i).
$$
In particular they exhaust the mixed measure. The centroid of $\mathcal H_q|_{D_i\cap\Lambda}$ belongs to $D_i$, has base $m_i/t_i$, and lies in $D_i\cap\Lambda$ if that base is integral. Suitable $u_i$ always exist.

edf02845b3275e8c:03.reason: Choose the integral-mean label first. The affine cut adjustment and null boundary give both labels. Positive mass on both sides gives strict winning points and ambient interior.
