edf02845b3275e8c:07.statement:
Let $n,d$ be positive integers and let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body. Write $\Lambda=\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$, $S=C\cap\Lambda$, and assume $q=\dim_{\mathrm H}S\ge1$. Then $C$ is the union of $k\le2^n$ closed affine-score winner cells that are ambient convex bodies, each cut from $C$ by at most $k-1$ closed halfspaces. Every mixed piece $D_i\cap\Lambda$ has dimension $q$ and positive $\mathcal H_q$ measure. Distinct mixed pieces overlap in $\mathcal H_q$-null sets. The actual centroid of $\mathcal H_q|_{D_i\cap\Lambda}$ belongs to $D_i\cap\Lambda$, and the distinct centroid bases are exactly the vertices and all the lattice points of their convex hull. In particular $\sum_i\mathcal H_q(D_i\cap\Lambda)=\mathcal H_q(S)$.

The universal count $2^n$ is sharp already for $q=d$, even if fractional splitting of the mixed measure is allowed instead of convex cells.

For the lower limit compare by a multiplicative factor using only the smallest strictly positive entry, with x=0 covered by max_j x_j. Atoms are allowed. Compactness gives attainment. The accepted sign-cone and finite-vertex capacity theorems bound volumes of simplex intersections for a different problem, rather than this row functional. Pending 8095e181b6be7bf1 §§1–5 uses the uniform simplex law and a different weighted dual.
f62fe2e83b180bf3:01.statement: For d≥1, m≥1 and any probability law of Ξ on the standard m-coordinate simplex, define φ(x)=inf_{t>0, Pr(x·Ξ≤t)>0} t/Pr(x·Ξ≤t)^(1/d) for x∈R^m_+. Then φ is coordinatewise nondecreasing, positively homogeneous, continuous on the whole orthant, and bounded above by max_j x_j. For each fixed finite number of rows and each fixed list of weights c_i≥0, H_c(X)=Σ_i c_i φ(X_i) attains its maximum over nonnegative matrices with m columns summing individually to one, and has a maximizer with a minimum number of nonzero rows.

f62fe2e83b180bf3:02.reason: A nontrivial dependence Σ_i a_iX_i=0 of nonnegative nonzero rows has both coefficient signs. Multiplication of the rows by 1+ta_i preserves every column sum and the objective is affine in t. Feasibility in both signs makes its slope zero, so a finite endpoint killing at least one row contradicts minimality. No differentiability, stochastic-law regularity or determinant margin is needed.
f62fe2e83b180bf3:02.statement: For the attained weighted homogeneous objective of §1, every maximizing nonnegative column-stochastic matrix chosen with minimum nonzero-row count has linearly independent nonzero rows, and therefore at most m such rows. f62fe2e83b180bf3:03.reason: The compensating scalings preserve columns and supports exactly and are affine in objective by homogeneity; the one varied row gives the projective remainder after the total linear term vanishes. Independence gives the dimension count. The prose summary at §3 drops the positive weight condition, which must be restored as in its preceding equation and the historical comments e3366154e3bb9635 and 0bff1578dd7bd3d0. The latter also points to pending 61582452a1450270 as a full proper row with negative semidefinite Hessian and only radial kernel; pending a5d3d44181ebed82 supplies a scoped curvature input. f62fe2e83b180bf3:03.statement: Let X maximize H_c of §1, and let its fully positive row r have c_r>0. For every v in the span of the active rows choose a_i with v+Σ_i a_iX_i=0. Vary the active rows by X_i(t)=(1+ta_i)X_i, adding tv only in row r. This is feasible for small signed t. If φ is differentiable at X_r and s=t/(1+ta_r), the exact total objective remainder is H_c(X(t))−H_c(X)=c_r(1+ta_r)[φ(X_r+sv)−φ(X_r)−sDφ(X_r)[v]]. Thus every existing second directional coefficient in the active-row span is nonpositive, and a strict increase over the tangent at arbitrarily small feasible s contradicts maximality. At a minimum-active maximizer with k active rows, a p-dimensional positive-definite Hessian subspace of such a row is impossible when k+p>m. In particular k=m excludes every such row that has a positive second direction.

external_dependencies: Farkas' lemma for linear inequalities. Ux≤b is feasible exactly when λ·b≥0 for every λ≥0 with Uᵀλ=0. See Boyd and Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization, §5.8.3, https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/cvxbook/bv_cvxbook.pdf.

Doignon's lattice Helly theorem, Convexity in crystallographical lattices, J. Geom. 3 (1973), 71–85, https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01949705. A finite convex family with no common integer point has such a subfamily of at most 2^n members.
f66dcff3eb3e1f03:01.reason: The auxiliary polytope construction at d2b290ebd8e35052 §1 works in both initial feasibility cases, with the critical singleton argument reproduced in this note. Farkas gives the circuit-defined projection facets and their contacts. Apply Doignon to the whole projected facet system, whose intersection avoids ℤ^n. f66dcff3eb3e1f03:01.statement: Let n,d≥1 and C be a convex body with S=C∩(ℤ^n×ℝ^d), positive full mixed volume M and finite nonempty base set P=π(S). Suppose for every point of S some closed containing cap has raw mass strictly below T>0. One can choose at most 2^n attained-contact positive circuits of at most d+1 nonvertical outward caps each, of raw masses <T, whose open caps together cover all of ℤ^n×ℝ^d, including fiber planes beyond π(C).

f66dcff3eb3e1f03:02.reason: Every possible p-section point of the enlarged hull arises from a feasible representation, and each represented Minkowski set occurs. For each direction the inclusion inequality is linear in α, so checking all vertices suffices, with α_q=0 handled by compatibility. Intersecting the resulting closed halfspaces in x gives the exact feasible set.
f66dcff3eb3e1f03:02.statement: Let P⊂ℤ^n be a nonempty finite lattice-complete set, with compatible positive d-dimensional compact convex fibers K_p defining C=conv⋃_{p∈P}({p}×K_p), d≥1. For any q outside B=conv(P), define R_p(q) by α≥0, α_q+∑_zα_z=1, α_q q+∑_zα_z z=p. Then conv(C,(q,x)) preserves all original fibers exactly iff for every p and each vertex α of R_p(q) with α_q>0 one has α_q x+∑_zα_zK_z⊆K_p. The feasible x form a closed convex set, possibly empty. For polytopal K_p the inclusion at each such vertex is equivalent to the finite facet inequalities α_q u·x≤h_{K_p}(u)−∑_zα_z h_{K_z}(u).

f66dcff3eb3e1f03:03.reason: The q-fiber is exposed, and d≥1 makes it null. Any other new integer r has a convex representation with coefficient λ<1 on q. The old canonical body has a positive real fiber over the remaining represented base, so the new r-fiber contains its positive homothetic copy. The source introduces q outside B without integrality before (1)–(2), but (3) with q on the right is the integer-birth statement and requires q∈ℤ^n.
f66dcff3eb3e1f03:03.statement: Under the preceding compatible positive-fiber hypotheses, for an integer q∉conv(P) and a feasible extension point x, the enlarged hull changes no mixed volume outside P iff conv(P∪{q})∩ℤ^n=P∪{q}. Its q-fiber is the singleton x.

f66dcff3eb3e1f03:04.reason: The centered convex and concave roofs realize the four prescribed fibers. For through-caps at (1,0), the nonnegative slope knots a/4,a/2,b/2 and opposite orientations give the minimum b/2+a. Source pairs of opposite tilted caps with this mass cover the entire left and right integer sides, proving global optimality; vertical containing caps at the sources are no smaller. Interpolating a new point at −r with the length-b fiber at 1 forces length at least rb/(r+1) at 0, giving the reserve and excluding all new integer bases. Reflect for the right side.
f66dcff3eb3e1f03:04.statement: For n=d=1, take the canonical convex hull of the four centered interval fibers at bases 0,1,2,3 with lengths (a,b,b,a), 0<a and b>2a. The raw maximum mixed depth is Q=b/2+a, total M=2(a+b), and normalized maximum β=1/4+a/[4(a+b)]. No convex extension preserving all original fibers has any point over a new integer base. A preserving real extension at base −r<0 requires r≤a/(b−a), and the same reserve applies beyond base 3.

f66dcff3eb3e1f03:05.reason: Each cap captures 21/4 in its source interval and one full endpoint interval, with all other traces empty. Averaging each pair gives the two stated projection inequalities, and x=0 realizes their full interval. The midpoint (3/2,0) has raw depth 11 by central symmetry and a null-boundary halfspace. The mixed maximum is 6, so the depth region excludes the mixed lattice. Every cap of mass below T misses the region, and the reserve calculation excludes a preserving integer extension. Here 6/22>1/4, so this calibrates global-cover geometry above the target.
f66dcff3eb3e1f03:05.statement: For n=d=1, take the canonical convex hull of the four centered interval fibers at bases 0,1,2,3 with lengths (a,b,b,a), 0<a and b>2a. f6c4fce660e140cf:02.reason: T_t maps every fiber by a determinant-one translation and bijects all ambient halfspaces. f6c4fce660e140cf:02.statement: For any fixed buffered configuration (C,L,ε), continuous vector v and finite η>0, put T_t(z,X)=(z,X+tηv), C_t=T_t C, L_t=L∘T_t⁻¹. Thus the singular part of −λI, λ>0, is nonnegative and has Hessian (λA/η)[[1,1],[1,1]] in unscaled displacements (h,k), with null line k=−h.

f7422e63e37f7d98:01.reason: Every directional sampled support is a concave sequence by actual convex compatibility. Its adjacent linear interpolation is concave, so every feasible weighted support sum at a fixed real base is at most that interpolation. The adjacent mixture attains it. Real widths are therefore the adjacent interpolants of integer widths. Taking the maximum in each direction proves the difference-body equality since D_all is the compact convex vertical section of C_*−C_*. The proof is insensitive to lower-dimensional fibers. Accepted 7227bbfcd12ad3d2 gives the underlying support LP for full-dimensional input fibers, without the all-dimensional exact adjacent formula or the difference-body conclusion. Pending f525b2b4bb53c54e:6 is the interval-fiber specialization on an affine grid.
f7422e63e37f7d98:01.statement: Let a≤b be integers and let K_j⊂R^d be all actual nonempty integer fibers of a compact convex body in R×R^d, at j=a,…,b, allowing arbitrary affine dimensions. Set C_*=conv⋃_j({j}×K_j), D_int=conv⋃_j(K_j−K_j), and D_all={v:(0,v)∈C_*−C_*}. This hull preserves the sampled fibers. At each j+t with j,j+1∈[a,b] and 0≤t≤1, (C_*)_(j+t)=(1−t)K_j+tK_(j+1). Moreover D_all=D_int, including when a=b.

f7422e63e37f7d98:02.reason: The two added points attain the maximum common-base difference at z=1/2, and all heights stay in [−L,L]. This is a calibration of the needed hull replacement, not a competing real-fiber interpolation theorem.

The bound follows by subtraction. Vertex choices and affine interpolation give the section on a simplex projection by compatibility. f7422e63e37f7d98:03.statement: For any finite complete base P⊂Z^n and actual nonempty compact convex fibers K_z, set C_*=conv⋃_(z∈P)({z}×K_z), D_int=conv⋃_(z∈P)(K_z−K_z), and D_all={v:(0,v)∈C_*−C_*}. f7afca279c65bd1a:01.reason: The median on the supporting line lies in the triangle and in at least one selected cap, so the corresponding closed trace contains at least half its conditional law, including atomic laws. The bound uses only the zero-fiber law and mass; arbitrary line laws in other fibers cannot repair it.

The caps H_i={λ_i(x,y)−z≥1/3} each have probability 4/27<2/9 and jointly cover the zero fiber. f7afca279c65bd1a:02.reason: The perturbation is multiplicative by a positive affine factor on compact support. Its exact linear constraints use the actual cap centroids (5/9,2/9) and (2/9,5/9). This affine kernel obstruction and the median no-needle theorem concern different allowed perturbations.
f7afca279c65bd1a:02.statement: For a jointly log-concave density f on compact convex support and affine h, small two-sided perturbations f(1±th) stay jointly log-concave. f7cc6152bd66304f:01.reason: Endpoint medians use a fiber of length at least M/2 and select its midpoint. At a middle median (2) makes the balanced endpoint-mass interval nonempty. In the normalized coordinates of (1), (3) gives 0≤y≤e and y≤a for s≤1 or y≤a/2 for s≥1. Substitution in (6), with a≥(s−1)/2, bounds both oblique orientations. Pure-base caps retain the middle and one side. This is strictly narrower in selected mass than e5b69d1af4c631dc §§1–5, whose proof covers every feasible t≥M/2. No identity alias for the full theorem.
f7cc6152bd66304f:01.statement: In the planar mixed model n=d=1 with positive-length fibers on at most three consecutive integer bases, let M>0 be original mixed length and let j be any closed weighted marginal median. The feasible moment interval of continuous barycenters of 0≤f≤1 with ∫f dμ=M/2 and ∫(z−j)f dμ=0 is nonempty, and its midpoint has original raw depth at least M/4 in every containing closed ambient halfspace.

f7cc6152bd66304f:02.reason: Expand the sum of the two endpoint threshold moments and the middle threshold moment with middle selected mass t−2ℓ. Both objectives have constant t/2−t²/2 and opposite signs on 2eℓ. The compact interval I gives the indicated one-sided Lipschitz bounds. This exact computable quadratic formula is additional to the general t proof's comparison of support optima, which leaves the quadratic unexpanded.
f7cc6152bd66304f:02.statement: Normalize three positive interval fibers at −1,0,1 to [e−a/2,e+a/2], [−1/2,1/2], [e−c/2,e+c/2], where 0<a≤c, s=a+c≤2, 0≤e≤(2−s)/4 and a≥(s−1)/2. At t=(s+1)/2 the equal endpoint retained mass ℓ ranges over I=[max(0,(s−1)/4),min(a,(s+1)/4)]. Put G(p)=max_{ℓ∈I}(pℓ−3ℓ²). The exact midpoint of the balanced mass-t moment interval is [G(3s/2+2e)−G(3s/2−2e)]/(s+1). It satisfies 0≤y≤e, with y≤a if s≤1 and y≤a/2 if s≥1.

f89d52b54ff6950f:1.reason: The two proper pieces come from similar corner triangles. The formulas and first derivatives agree at the middle vertex and the empty/full transitions. This is the exact coordinate setup for the moment and depth results.
f89d52b54ff6950f:1.statement: For any finite P⊂R^n, z0∈P, and radii r_z>0, put T=conv{(−1,−1),(2,−1),(−1,2)}, with area 9/2. Every nonzero continuous normal for centered fibers r_zT reduces by triangle symmetry and positive rescaling to (1,θ), 0≤θ≤1. For 0<θ<1 and k=α·(z−z0), the planar cap area across thresholds −(2−θ)r, (1−2θ)r, (1+θ)r is respectively 0, ((2−θ)r+k)^2/[2(1−θ)], (9/2)r²−((1+θ)r−k)^2/(2θ), (9/2)r². The area sum Q is C¹ in (α,θ).

f89d52b54ff6950f:2.reason: The two gradient entries are Σℓ_z t_z and Σ(ℓ_z²/2−r_zℓ_z). Differentiating both yields all Hessian blocks. Dotting base stationarity with α gives the allocation identities. No accepted match for the signed mixed Hessian was located.
f89d52b54ff6950f:2.statement: In that chart let t_z=z−z0, ℓ_z be the cut length measured in x2 (zero at saturation), and v_z=(t_z,ℓ_z−r_z). The two proper states I and J capture a corner and leave a corner, respectively. At any interior stationary point, Σℓ_z t_z=0 and Σℓ_z²=2Σr_zℓ_z. For either state X write S_X=Σ_Xℓ_z², T_X=Σ_X r_zℓ_z and M=T_I+T_J. Then S_I=3T_I−(1−θ)M and S_J=3T_J−θM. f89d52b54ff6950f:4.reason: Finite tilt clamping and strict improvement eliminate purely integer directions. In the interior angular chart stationary endpoints have equal positive width and must lie strictly in states I,J. The α-curvature, Hessian determinant, and one-sided second variation at θ=1/2 exclude every interior angle. Accepted 2a8c2bc6d7992c5e covers compact tilt reduction for compatible planar slices but supplies no angular classification.
f89d52b54ff6950f:4.statement: For any a,b,c>0 and centered triangle fibers aT,cT,bT at bases −1,0,1, the depth at (0,0) is attained by a through-source cap. Every minimizing cap has nonzero continuous normal in a canonical vertex direction or its opposite, with no assumption c≥(a+b)/2.

f89d52b54ff6950f:5.reason: The only interior quadratic minimum occurs at α=a−b and is feasible exactly for a/2≤b≤2a. Saturation plateaus and full transitions give the other extrema. Complementarity gives the opposite-direction minimum and §2 closes the angular search.
f89d52b54ff6950f:5.statement: For r>0 let f_r(k) be 0 for k≤−2r, (2r+k)^2/2 for −2r≤k≤r, and (9/2)r² for k≥r. For g(α)=f_a(−α)+f_b(α), a,b>0, min g=min{(a+b)^2,(9/2)a²,(9/2)b²} and max g=max{(9/2)a²+(2b−a)_+²/2,(9/2)b²+(2a−b)_+²/2}. For any c>0 the middle depth is the smaller of 2c²+min g and (5/2)c²+(9/2)(a²+b²)−max g.

f89d52b54ff6950f:6.reason: Shift the integer bases by one. Convexity forces the midpoint inclusion, which for homothetic copies of the same nondegenerate triangle is precisely c≥(a+b)/2. The accepted lifted-hull construction proves sufficiency and accounts for all integer bases.
f89d52b54ff6950f:6.statement: Centered triangle fibers aT,cT,bT at bases −1,0,1 with positive radii are realized as exactly the integer fibers of a convex body if and only if c≥(a+b)/2.

f89d52b54ff6950f:7.reason: The two scalar minima from §3 differ strictly in favor of the canonical branch. For a≤b<2a the two difference lower bounds in (18) cover complementary ratio ranges, and for b≥2a the difference is c²/2.
f89d52b54ff6950f:7.statement: If a,b,c>0 and c≥(a+b)/2, then the middle centroid raw depth is D0=2c²+min{(a+b)^2,(9/2)a²,(9/2)b²}, and every minimizing continuous normal is one of the three canonical vertex directions.

f89d52b54ff6950f:8.reason: Convex depth superlevels contain the average of the triangle-symmetry orbit. Finite tilts isolate an endpoint while preserving its ordinary cut. The exact middle formula supplies the remaining candidate for the maximum.
f89d52b54ff6950f:8.statement: For the compatible three centered homothets, the centroid maximizes depth within each fiber. At either endpoint base the depth at every point equals its ordinary depth in that triangle, with centroid depth 2a² or 2b². f9c635ce5abe9f17:01.statement:
Let $p\ge1$, and let $f$ be a bounded nonnegative upper-semicontinuous function of compact support on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space. Assume $\{f>0\}$ has nonempty interior and the extended function $f^{-1/(p+1)}$, with value $+\infty$ where $f=0$, is convex. For $x\ne0$ put $I_p(x)=\int_0^\infty t^{p-1}f(tx)\,dt$. Then
$$
U_p=\{0\}\cup\{x\ne0:I_p(x)\ge1\}
$$
is compact and convex. Its gauge is $I_p(x)^{-1/p}$ for $x\ne0$, interpreted as $+\infty$ if $I_p(x)=0$, and is zero at the origin. If $f$ is positive on a neighborhood of the origin, $U_p$ is a convex body with the origin in its interior.

f9c635ce5abe9f17:02.statement: Let $r\ge1$ be an integer. Let $f$ be a bounded nonnegative upper-semicontinuous density of compact support in $\mathbb R^r$. Assume $\{f>0\}$ has nonempty interior and the function $f^{-1/(r+1)}$, extended by $+\infty$ where $f=0$, is convex. Then there is a point $y$ in the interior of the support of $f$ such that every closed halfspace containing $y$ has $f$-mass at least $\gamma_r\int f$, where $\gamma_r=(r/(r+1))^r$. The constant is sharp.

f9c635ce5abe9f17:03.statement:

$$
\max_i |K\cap H_i|\ge\gamma_{d-1}|K|,
\qquad \gamma_j=\left(\frac{j}{j+1}\right)^j\ (j\ge1),\quad \gamma_0=1.
$$
For each $d$ the constant is attained both for some $y\notin K$ and for some $y\in\partial K$. For $d\ge2$ the constant also remains the infimum for each contact type when the normals span $\mathbb R^d$, equivalently when $y$ is the unique common point of their boundaries.

fc860651e80d6fd0:01.statement:
Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional Euclidean space and $P\subset E$ a nonempty finite set. For $z\in P$ let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body, where $d\ge1$, and write $w_z=|K_z|_d>0$ and $g_z$ for its volume centroid. Let $M=\sum_{z\in P}w_z$ and $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Give the graph $T=\{(z,g_z):z\in P\}$ the atomic weights $w_z$, and write $w(F)=\sum_{(z,g_z)\in T\cap F}w_z$. The measured family has raw cap mass $\mu(H)=\sum_{z\in P}|\{x\in K_z:(z,x)\in H\}|_d$.

Fix $0<\alpha\le M$ and $y=(p,g_p)\in T$ such that every closed ambient halfspace containing $y$ has atomic weight at least $\alpha$. Let $F$ be the minimal face of $\operatorname{conv}T$ containing $y$, allowing the whole hull. Then the raw halfspace depth $h_\mu(y)=\inf_{H\ni y}\mu(H)$ is at least $\gamma_d\alpha$. Equality implies $w(F)=\alpha$ and the existence of a single unit $u\in\mathbb R^d$ satisfying
$$
|K_z\cap\{x:u\cdot(x-g_z)\ge0\}|_d=\gamma_d w_z
\qquad\text{for every }(z,g_z)\in F\cap T.
$$
In particular, $w(F)>\alpha$ implies $h_\mu(y)>\gamma_d\alpha$.

If $g_z=G(z)$ for a single affine map $G:E\to\mathbb R^d$, these two conditions also imply equality and a through-$y$ closed halfspace attains it. In this case the atomic center assumption is equivalent to weighted closed base depth at least $\alpha$ at $p$, and $F$ projects to the minimal face of $\operatorname{conv}P$ containing $p$.

fc860651e80d6fd0:04.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite set in a Euclidean space, with weights $w_z>0$ of total $M$, and write $B=\operatorname{conv}P$. Fix an integer $h\ge1$ and set $\alpha=M/h$. Let $\mathcal F$ be the proper faces of $B$ of weight $w(F)=\sum_{z\in P\cap F}w_z=\alpha$. Exactly one of the following holds.

1. Some $v\in\mathbb R^P$ has $\sum_{z\in P}v_z=0$ and $\sum_{z\in P\cap F}v_z<0$ for every $F\in\mathcal F$. This holds vacuously for an empty face list.
2. There are numbers $\theta_F\ge0$ for $F\in\mathcal F$ such that $\sum_{F\in\mathcal F}\theta_F\mathbf1_{P\cap F}=\mathbf1_P$ and $\sum_{F\in\mathcal F}\theta_F=h$.

Suppose further that $h>1$ bounds the relative Helly number of $P$, and that the weights are the volumes of compact convex fibers $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ with positive $d$-volume, $d\ge1$, whose centroids are given by one affine function on the base. In case 1 there is an actual centroid mark of raw mixed halfspace depth strictly greater than $\gamma_d M/h$, where $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Thus if the maximum raw depth equals $\gamma_d M/h$, the critical proper faces have the fractional partition in case 2. The strict conclusion holds in particular if some site of $P$ lies outside every proper face of weight at most $\alpha$, including when $P$ meets $\operatorname{relint}B$.
